short_description.id: White Dragon Horse adalah tokoh novel klasik Tiongkok Journey to the West: pangeran naga yang dihukum, lalu diubah menjadi kuda putih untuk membawa biksu Tang Sanzang dalam perjalanannya.
short_description.en: The White Dragon Horse is a character of the classic Chinese novel Journey to the West: a dragon prince who is punished and then turned into a white horse to carry the monk Tang Sanzang on his journey.

long_description.id: White Dragon Horse adalah tokoh sastra dari novel Journey to the West, yang terbit pada abad ke-16 pada masa dinasti Ming dan dikaitkan dengan Wu Cheng'en. Dalam novel itu ia pangeran naga, putra ketiga Raja Naga Laut Barat, yang kemudian menjadi tunggangan Tang Sanzang; ia juga dikenal sebagai Ao Lie.
long_description.en: The White Dragon Horse is a literary character from Journey to the West, a novel that appeared in the 16th century under the Ming dynasty and is credited to Wu Cheng'en. In the novel he is a dragon prince, third son of the Dragon King of the West Sea, who later becomes Tang Sanzang's steed; he is also known as Ao Lie.

long_description.id: Menurut teks bab 8, ia digantung di udara dan dipukul karena membakar mutiara, hingga Guanyin menyelamatkannya dan menaruhnya di ngarai untuk menunggu pengambil sutra. Pada bab 15 ia menelan kuda putih Tang Sanzang, melawan Sun Wukong, lalu diubah Guanyin menjadi kuda putih pengganti.
long_description.en: According to the chapter 8 text he is hung in the air and beaten for burning a pearl until Guanyin rescues him and places him in a gorge to wait for the scripture seeker. In chapter 15 he swallows Tang Sanzang's white horse, fights Sun Wukong, and is then turned by Guanyin into a white horse as a replacement.

long_description.id: Di akhir novel ia dinaikkan menjadi Kuda Naga Delapan Bagian Surgawi, kembali ke wujud naga, dan melingkari tiang di kuil. Ia sering digambarkan pendiam dan cerdas, dan dalam tafsir tradisional dikaitkan dengan "Kuda Pikiran"; ia juga dipuja sebagai dewa dalam agama rakyat Tiongkok.
long_description.en: At the end of the novel he is raised to the Dragon Horse of the Eight Heavenly Sections, returns to dragon form and coils around a pillar in the temple. He is often depicted as quiet and intelligent, and in traditional interpretation is linked with the "Horse of the Mind"; he is also worshipped as a deity in Chinese folk religion.

cultural_context.id: Dalam kritik sastra tradisional dan tafsir Neidan, White Dragon Horse dikaitkan dengan "Kuda Pikiran" atau "Kuda Kehendak"; dan Bai Longma dipuja sebagai dewa dalam agama rakyat Tiongkok. Dalam pengantar tahun 1913, Timothy Richard menafsirkannya sebagai naga yang berdosa lalu direndahkan menjadi kuda.
cultural_context.en: In traditional literary criticism and Neidan interpretation the White Dragon Horse is linked with the "Horse of the Mind" or "Horse of the Will", and Bai Longma is worshipped as a deity in Chinese folk religion. In his 1913 introduction Timothy Richard presents him as a dragon who sinned and was degraded into a horse.

literal_meaning.id: Bai Longma secara harfiah berarti "kuda naga putih"; Yulong berarti "naga giok".
literal_meaning.en: Bai Longma literally means "white dragon horse"; Yulong means "jade dragon".

statement.id: Dalam bahasa Tionghoa, White Dragon Horse dikenal sebagai Bai Longma (白龍馬).
statement.en: In Chinese the White Dragon Horse is known as Bai Longma (白龍馬).

claims.quote: In Journey to the West, Bai Longma is a dragon prince and the third son of the Dragon King of the West Sea. He once accidentally set fire to a pearl that had been given as a gift by the Jade Emperor.

statement.id: Dalam Journey to the West, Bai Longma adalah pangeran naga, putra ketiga Raja Naga Laut Barat; ia pernah tak sengaja membakar mutiara yang dihadiahkan Kaisar Giok.
statement.en: In Journey to the West Bai Longma is a dragon prince, the third son of the Dragon King of the West Sea; he once accidentally set fire to a pearl given as a gift by the Jade Emperor.

claims.quote: The dragon prince was spared and banished to Yingchou Stream (鷹愁澗) in Shepan Mountain (蛇盤山), where he was instructed to wait for the monk whom Guanyin would send on a pilgrimage to the Buddha.

statement.id: Sang pangeran naga diampuni dan dibuang ke Sungai Yingchou (鷹愁澗) di Gunung Shepan (蛇盤山), tempat ia diperintahkan menunggu biksu yang akan dikirim Guanyin berziarah menemui Buddha.
statement.en: The dragon prince was spared and banished to Yingchou Stream (鷹愁澗) in Shepan Mountain (蛇盤山), where he was told to wait for the monk whom Guanyin would send on a pilgrimage to the Buddha.

claims.quote: When Tang Sanzang crosses the stream, the prince appears as a gigantic white dragon and swallows Tang's white horse. He fights Sun Wukong but is defeated and retreats underwater.

statement.id: Ketika Tang Sanzang menyeberangi sungai itu, sang pangeran muncul sebagai naga putih raksasa dan menelan kuda putih Tang; ia melawan Sun Wukong, kalah, dan mundur ke bawah air.
statement.en: When Tang Sanzang crosses the stream the prince appears as a gigantic white dragon and swallows Tang's white horse; he fights Sun Wukong but is defeated and retreats underwater.

claims.quote: He is then transformed into the White Dragon Horse and serves as Tang Sanzang's steed for the rest of the journey. Compared with some of the other pilgrims, he is often depicted as quiet and intelligent, and he occasionally returns to dragon form to fight when the group is in danger.

statement.id: Ia kemudian diubah menjadi White Dragon Horse dan menjadi tunggangan Tang Sanzang sepanjang sisa perjalanan; dibandingkan beberapa peziarah lain ia sering digambarkan pendiam dan cerdas, dan sesekali kembali ke wujud naga untuk bertarung saat rombongan terancam.
statement.en: He is then transformed into the White Dragon Horse and serves as Tang Sanzang's steed for the rest of the journey; compared with some of the other pilgrims he is often depicted as quiet and intelligent, and occasionally returns to dragon form to fight when the group is in danger.

statement.id: Ketika Tang Sanzang ditawan Iblis Jubah Kuning, White Dragon Horse berubah menjadi pemuda dan mencoba menyelamatkannya, tetapi gagal.
statement.en: When Tang Sanzang is captured by the Yellow Robe Demon, the White Dragon Horse transforms into a young man and tries to rescue him, but fails.

claims.quote: He resumes his white dragon form and coils around one of the pillars in the Great Leiyin Temple.

statement.id: Di akhir novel ia kembali ke wujud naga putih dan melingkari salah satu tiang di Kuil Leiyin Agung.

statement.id: Dalam pengantar terjemahannya tahun 1913, Timothy Richard menulis bahwa White Dragon Horse berasal dari samudra barat, berdosa sebagai naga, yang pemimpinnya adalah dewa hujan, lalu direndahkan menjadi kuda.

statement.id: Dalam terjemahan Richard (1913), seekor naga memakan kuda putih dan itu menakutkan Sang Guru.
statement.en: In Richard's 1913 translation one dragon ate the white horse, and this terrified the Master.

claims.quote: So saying she went and spoke to the dragon, and he became a white horse to carry the Master

statement.id: Dalam terjemahan Richard (1913), Kwanyin berbicara kepada naga itu dan ia menjadi kuda putih untuk membawa Sang Guru.
statement.en: In Richard's 1913 translation Kwanyin goes and speaks to the dragon, and he becomes a white horse to carry the Master.

claims.quote: 我是西海龍王敖閏之子，因縱火燒了殿上明珠，我父王表奏天庭，告了忤逆。玉帝把我吊在空中，打了三百，不日遭誅。

statement.id: Dalam bab 8, naga yang digantung di udara berkata ia putra Raja Naga Laut Barat, Ao Run (敖閏); karena membakar mutiara di aula, ayahnya melaporkannya ke langit sebagai durhaka, dan Kaisar Giok menggantung serta memukulnya tiga ratus kali, hampir dihukum mati.
statement.en: In chapter 8 the dragon hanging in the air says he is the son of the Dragon King of the West Sea, Ao Run (敖閏); for setting fire to the pearl in the hall his father reported him to heaven as unfilial, and the Jade Emperor hung him up and had him struck three hundred times, soon to be executed.

claims.quote: 菩薩把他送在深澗之中，只等取經人來，變做白馬，上西方立功。小龍領命潛身不題。

statement.id: Guanyin menaruhnya di ngarai yang dalam untuk menunggu pengambil sutra, agar berubah menjadi kuda putih dan berjasa menuju Barat; sang naga kecil menerima perintah dan menyembunyikan diri.
statement.en: The bodhisattva places him in a deep gorge to wait for the scripture seeker, to become a white horse and win merit going west; the little dragon accepts the order and hides himself.

claims.quote: 那條龍就趕不上，把他的白馬連鞍轡一口吞下肚去，依然伏水潛蹤。

statement.id: Dalam bab 15, sang naga tidak berhasil mengejar Tang Sanzang tetapi menelan kuda putihnya beserta pelana dan kekang dalam satu suapan, lalu bersembunyi lagi di air.
statement.en: In chapter 15 the dragon cannot catch up with the elder but swallows his white horse with saddle and bridle in one gulp and hides again in the water.

claims.quote: 那條龍，是我親奏玉帝，討他在此，專為求經人做個腳力。你想那東土來的凡馬，怎歷得這萬水千山？怎到得那靈山佛地？須是得這個龍馬，方才去得。

statement.id: Guanyin menjelaskan bahwa ia sendiri meminta naga itu kepada Kaisar Giok untuk menjadi tunggangan para pengambil sutra, karena kuda biasa tak akan sanggup menempuh ribuan gunung dan sungai ke Tanah Buddha tanpa kuda naga ini.
statement.en: The bodhisattva explains that she herself asked the Jade Emperor for the dragon to serve as a mount for scripture seekers, since an ordinary horse could not cross the myriad mountains and rivers to the Buddha land without this dragon horse.

claims.quote: 菩薩叫揭諦道：「你去澗邊叫一聲『敖閏龍王玉龍三太子，你出來，有南海菩薩在此。』他就出來了。

statement.id: Guanyin menyuruh pengawal memanggilnya dengan sebutan "敖閏龍王玉龍三太子" (Pangeran Ketiga Naga Giok dari Raja Naga Ao Run) agar keluar.
statement.en: The bodhisattva has an attendant call him by the title "敖閏龍王玉龍三太子" (third prince Jade Dragon of the Dragon King Ao Run) to come out.

claims.quote: 又叫那白馬：「汝本是西洋大海廣晉龍王之子，因汝違逆父命，犯了不孝之罪。幸得皈身皈法，皈我沙門，每日家虧你馱負聖僧來西，又虧你馱負聖經去東，亦有功者，加陞汝職正果，為八部天龍馬。」

statement.id: Di akhir novel, Buddha memanggil kuda putih itu dan berkata ia putra Raja Naga Guangjin (廣晉) dari Samudra Barat, bersalah tidak berbakti karena melawan perintah ayahnya; karena jasanya memikul biksu ke barat dan kitab ke timur, ia dinaikkan menjadi Kuda Naga Delapan Bagian Surgawi (八部天龍馬).
statement.en: At the end of the novel the Buddha addresses the white horse and says he is a son of the Dragon King Guangjin (廣晉) of the Western Ocean, guilty of unfilial conduct for defying his father's order; for carrying the holy monk west and the scriptures east he is raised to the Dragon Horse of the Eight Heavenly Sections (八部天龍馬).

claims.quote: 須臾間，那馬打個展身，即退了毛皮，換了頭角，渾身上長起金鱗，腮頷下生出銀鬚，一身瑞氣，四爪祥雲，飛出化龍池，盤繞在山門裡擎天華表柱上。

statement.id: Setelah dimasukkan ke Kolam Perubahan Naga, kuda itu meregangkan tubuh, menanggalkan bulu dan kulit, bertanduk, bersisik emas, berjanggut perak, lalu terbang dan melingkar di tiang tinggi di gerbang gunung.
statement.en: After being put into the Dragon-Transforming Pool the horse stretches, sheds its hair and skin, grows horns, gold scales and a silver beard, and flies out to coil around a tall pillar at the mountain gate.

short_description.id: Melon heads adalah makhluk mirip manusia berkepala sangat besar dalam cerita rakyat Ohio, Michigan, dan Connecticut yang sesekali keluar dari persembunyian untuk menyerang orang. Asal-usulnya berbeda di tiap daerah, dan tidak ada bukti nyata untuk legenda ini.
short_description.en: Melon heads are large-headed humanoids in the folklore of Ohio, Michigan and Connecticut who occasionally emerge from hiding to attack people. Their origin differs by region, and commentators say there is no real evidence for the legend.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Ohio, Michigan, dan Connecticut, melon heads digambarkan sebagai makhluk mirip manusia berkepala besar dengan tengkorak menggembung yang sesekali keluar dari persembunyian untuk menyerang orang. Berbagai versi legenda memberi mereka asal-usul berbeda. Skeptoid menyebut penjelasan standarnya adalah bahwa mereka anak-anak penderita hidrosefalus, dan bahwa tidak ada foto, video, atau bukti empiris apa pun; menurutnya, anak dengan kepala yang tampak membesar berarti sangat muda, mungkin kurang dari dua tahun, dan sebelum 1940-an sulit bertahan hidup.
long_description.en: In the folklore of Ohio, Michigan and Connecticut, melon heads are described as large-headed humanoids with bulbous craniums who occasionally emerge from hiding places to attack people. Different versions of the legend give them different origins. Skeptoid says the standard explanation is that they are children with hydrocephalus, and that there are no photographs, videos or empirical evidence of any kind; in its view, a child with a visibly enlarged head would be very young, probably under two, and unlikely to have survived before the 1940s.

long_description.id: Di Michigan, melon heads konon tinggal di sekitar Felt Mansion. Menurut satu cerita, mereka anak-anak penderita hidrosefalus dari Junction Insane Asylum tetapi Allegan County Historical Society menyatakan asilum itu tidak pernah ada, dan Skeptoid pun menyatakan tidak pernah ada rumah sakit atau asilum di sekitar tempat itu. Skeptoid juga mencatat satu varian lain yang menyebut kamp tawanan perang Jerman bernama Camp Allegan, tempat orang Amerika melakukan eksperimen medis yang membuat kepala para tahanan membengkak besar.
long_description.en: In Michigan, the melon heads are said to reside around Felt Mansion. According to one story they were children with hydrocephalus from the Junction Insane Asylum, but the Allegan County Historical Society asserts that the asylum never existed, and Skeptoid likewise says there never was a hospital or asylum in the vicinity. Skeptoid also records another variation that names a German prisoner-of-war camp called Camp Allegan, where Americans did medical experiments that caused the prisoners' heads to swell hugely.

long_description.id: Di Kirtland, Ohio, kisahnya menyebut anak-anak yatim di bawah asuhan Dr. Crow yang akhirnya membunuhnya, membakar panti, dan mundur ke hutan; melon heads konon terlihat di Wisner Road. Di Connecticut, satu kisah menyebut mereka akibat perkawinan sedarah yang hidup terpencil di hutan, sedangkan varian lain menyebut keturunan keluarga era kolonial yang diasingkan karena tuduhan sihir. Skeptoid menyatakan kisah Dr. Crow tanpa bukti.
long_description.en: In Kirtland, Ohio, the story has orphans under Dr. Crow's watch who eventually killed him, burned the orphanage and retreated to the forests; melon heads are said to be sighted on Wisner Road. In Connecticut, one story calls them the result of inbreeding living in seclusion in the woods, while another variation calls them descendants of a Colonial-era family banished over witchcraft accusations. Skeptoid says the Dr. Crow story is without evidence.

cultural_context.id: Penulis Skeptoid berpendapat bahwa kisah melon heads menstigmatisasi orang dengan cacat fisik sebagai monster, sementara generasi muda sebaiknya diajari belas kasih dan penerimaan. Ensiklopedia daring menduga kedekatan lembaga pemasyarakatan dan psikiatri dengan daerah pedesaan di Connecticut mungkin menyumbang unsur legenda.
cultural_context.en: The Skeptoid author argues the melon head stories stigmatize people with physical disfigurements as monsters, whereas younger generations should be taught compassion and acceptance. The online encyclopedia suggests that the proximity of criminal and psychiatric institutions to rural areas in Connecticut may have contributed elements to the legend.

sources.title: Dr. Crow and the Melon Heads (Skeptoid Podcast #930)
sources.author: Brian Dunning

claims.quote: In the American folklore of Ohio, Michigan and Connecticut, melon heads are beings generally described as large-headed humanoids with bulbous large craniums who occasionally emerge from hiding places to attack people.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Ohio, Michigan, dan Connecticut, melon heads adalah makhluk mirip manusia berkepala sangat besar yang sesekali keluar dari persembunyian untuk menyerang orang.
statement.en: In the folklore of Ohio, Michigan and Connecticut, melon heads are large-headed humanoids who sometimes emerge from hiding to attack people.

claims.quote: Different variations of the legend attribute different origins to the entities.

statement.id: Versi-versi legenda memberi asal-usul yang berbeda bagi mereka.
statement.en: Different versions give them different origins.

claims.quote: According to one story, they were originally children with hydrocephalus who lived at the Junction Insane Asylum near Felt Mansion.

statement.id: Menurut satu cerita, mereka semula anak-anak penderita hidrosefalus yang tinggal di Junction Insane Asylum dekat Felt Mansion.
statement.en: One story says they were originally children with hydrocephalus who lived at the Junction Insane Asylum near Felt Mansion.

claims.quote: The Allegan County Historical Society asserts that the asylum never existed

statement.id: Allegan County Historical Society menyatakan rumah sakit jiwa itu tidak pernah ada.
statement.en: The Allegan County Historical Society says the asylum never existed.

claims.quote: The melon heads of Michigan are said to reside around Felt Mansion, although they have also been reportedly seen in southern forested areas of Ottawa County.

statement.id: Melon heads di Michigan konon tinggal di sekitar Felt Mansion, meski juga dilaporkan terlihat di kawasan hutan di selatan Ottawa County.
statement.en: The melon heads of Michigan are said to reside around Felt Mansion, though they have also reportedly been seen in southern forested areas of Ottawa County.

claims.quote: Some versions of the legend say that the children once lived in the mansion itself but later retreated to a system of caverns (or caves in a nearby hill left over from an abandoned zoo).

statement.id: Sebagian versi legenda menyebut anak-anak itu dulu tinggal di rumah besar itu tetapi kemudian mundur ke sistem gua (atau gua di bukit terdekat peninggalan kebun binatang yang ditinggalkan).
statement.en: Some versions say the children once lived in the mansion itself but later retreated to a system of caverns (or caves in a nearby hill left over from an abandoned zoo).

claims.quote: Laketown Township Manager Al Meshkin told the Holland Sentinel that he had heard the tales as a teenager, noting that his friends referred to the beings as "wobbleheads".

statement.id: Al Meshkin, manajer Laketown Township, mengatakan kepada Holland Sentinel bahwa ia mendengar kisah itu saat remaja dan teman-temannya menyebut makhluk itu "wobbleheads".
statement.en: Laketown Township Manager Al Meshkin told the Holland Sentinel he heard the tales as a teenager and that his friends called the beings "wobbleheads".

claims.quote: The melon head stories of Ohio are primarily associated with the Cleveland suburb of Kirtland in Lake County. According to local lore, the melon heads were originally orphans under the watch of a mysterious figure known as Dr. Crow (sometimes spelled Crowe, Krohe or Kroh or known as Dr. Melonhead).

statement.id: Menurut cerita setempat di Ohio, melon heads semula yatim piatu yang diasuh sosok misterius bernama Dr. Crow (kadang ditulis Crowe, Krohe, atau Kroh, atau disebut Dr. Melonhead).
statement.en: According to local lore in Ohio, the melon heads were originally orphans under the watch of a mysterious figure known as Dr. Crow (sometimes spelled Crowe, Krohe or Kroh, or called Dr. Melonhead).

claims.quote: Eventually, the legend continues, the children killed Crow, burned the orphanage, and retreated to the surrounding forests and supposedly feed on babies.

statement.id: Dalam kelanjutan legenda, anak-anak itu akhirnya membunuh Crow, membakar panti asuhan, lalu mundur ke hutan sekitar dan konon memangsa bayi.
statement.en: The legend continues that the children eventually killed Crow, burned the orphanage, and retreated to the surrounding forests, supposedly feeding on babies.

claims.quote: Legend holds that the melon heads may be sighted along Wisner Road in Kirtland and adjacent Chardon Township in Geauga County.

statement.id: Menurut legenda, melon heads dapat terlihat di sepanjang Wisner Road di Kirtland dan Chardon Township di Geauga County.
statement.en: Legend holds that the melon heads may be sighted along Wisner Road in Kirtland and adjacent Chardon Township in Geauga County.

claims.quote: There are several primary Connecticut variations. ... According to the second variation, the melon heads are descendants of a Colonial-era family from Shelton-Trumbull who were banished after accusations of witchcraft were made against them causing them to retreat to the woods.

statement.id: Menurut varian kedua di Connecticut, melon heads adalah keturunan keluarga era kolonial dari Shelton-Trumbull yang diasingkan setelah dituduh melakukan sihir sehingga mundur ke hutan.
statement.en: According to the second Connecticut variation, the melon heads are descendants of a Colonial-era family from Shelton-Trumbull banished after accusations of witchcraft, causing them to retreat to the woods.

claims.quote: Melon Heads allegedly prey upon humans who wander into their territory.

statement.id: Melon heads konon memangsa manusia yang tersesat ke wilayah mereka.
statement.en: Melon Heads allegedly prey upon humans who wander into their territory.

claims.quote: None of the towns that have a melon head legend have roads designated as Dracula Drive.

statement.id: Tidak satu pun kota yang memiliki legenda melon head punya jalan resmi bernama Dracula Drive.
statement.en: None of the towns that have a melon head legend have roads designated as Dracula Drive.

claims.quote: The proximity of several criminal and psychiatric institutions as well as their juxtaposition to rural areas of the county may have contributed elements to the legend of the Melon Heads.

statement.id: Kedekatan beberapa lembaga pemasyarakatan dan psikiatri dengan daerah pedesaan mungkin menyumbang unsur pada legenda Melon Heads.
statement.en: The proximity of several criminal and psychiatric institutions to rural areas of the county may have contributed elements to the Melon Heads legend.

claims.quote: even becoming the subject of a 2011 film simply titled The Melonheads, which is based around the West Michigan legend.

statement.id: Legenda itu bahkan menjadi subjek film tahun 2011 berjudul The Melonheads yang berlatar legenda Michigan Barat.
statement.en: The legend even became the subject of a 2011 film titled The Melonheads, based around the West Michigan legend.

claims.quote: A movie, Legend of the Melonheads, released in 2010, is based on the Ohio legend and various other legends in the Kirtland area.

statement.id: Film Legend of the Melonheads, dirilis 2010, berdasar legenda Ohio dan berbagai legenda lain di daerah Kirtland.
statement.en: The movie Legend of the Melonheads, released in 2010, is based on the Ohio legend and various other legends in the Kirtland area.

claims.quote: children with great big balloon-like heads, chasing people through the forests at night, appearing by the side of the road to frighten motorists, and striking fear into the hearts of those unlucky enough to encounter them.

statement.id: Skeptoid menggambarkan legenda urban melon heads sebagai anak-anak berkepala besar seperti balon yang mengejar orang di hutan pada malam hari dan muncul di pinggir jalan untuk menakuti pengendara.
statement.en: Skeptoid describes the melon head urban legend as children with great balloon-like heads who chase people through forests at night and appear by the roadside to frighten motorists.

claims.quote: There are no photographs or videos of the melon heads, and no empirical evidence of any kind for us to examine

statement.id: Menurut Skeptoid, tidak ada foto atau video melon heads dan tidak ada bukti empiris apa pun untuk diperiksa.
statement.en: According to Skeptoid, there are no photographs or videos of the melon heads and no empirical evidence of any kind to examine.

claims.quote: The standard explanation given for most melon head stories — as these legends are found in several US states — is that the melon heads are children with hydrocephalus.

statement.id: Menurut Skeptoid, penjelasan standar untuk kebanyakan kisah melon heads, yang tersebar di beberapa negara bagian AS, adalah bahwa mereka anak-anak penderita hidrosefalus.
statement.en: According to Skeptoid, the standard explanation in most melon head stories, found in several US states, is that the melon heads are children with hydrocephalus.

claims.quote: There never was a hospital or asylum anywhere in the vicinity, and even if there had been, such facilities were not in the habit of turning their patients loose to fend for themselves in the wild.

statement.id: Menurut Skeptoid, tidak pernah ada rumah sakit atau asilum di sekitar tempat itu, dan fasilitas semacam itu tidak biasa melepas pasiennya ke alam liar.
statement.en: According to Skeptoid, there never was a hospital or asylum anywhere in the vicinity, and such facilities were not in the habit of turning patients loose in the wild.

claims.quote: One interesting variation relies on the fact that during World War II, there was a POW camp for German soldiers located there, called Camp Allegan. In this version, the Americans did medical experiments on the German prisoners, causing huge swollen heads.

statement.id: Dalam salah satu varian, pada Perang Dunia II ada kamp tawanan perang tentara Jerman bernama Camp Allegan; orang Amerika melakukan eksperimen medis pada para tahanan hingga kepala mereka membengkak besar.
statement.en: In one variation, a POW camp for German soldiers called Camp Allegan existed there during World War II; the Americans did medical experiments on the prisoners, causing huge swollen heads.

claims.quote: Connecticut has a very different version of the melon heads. In that story, the melon heads are the result of inbreeding, and they live in the woods in seclusion on the edge of society.

statement.id: Dalam kisah Connecticut, melon heads adalah akibat perkawinan sedarah dan hidup terpencil di hutan di tepi masyarakat.
statement.en: In the Connecticut story, the melon heads are the result of inbreeding and live in seclusion in the woods on the edge of society.

claims.quote: But the most famous and complete melon head story comes from Kirtland, Ohio. ... the basic plot is that around the year 1900 a Dr. Crow and his wife, who may have lived on Wisner Road, cared for a number of children with hydrocephalus at their home.

statement.id: Menurut Skeptoid, alur dasar kisah Kirtland, Ohio adalah bahwa sekitar tahun 1900 Dr. Crow dan istrinya, yang mungkin tinggal di Wisner Road, merawat sejumlah anak penderita hidrosefalus di rumah mereka.
statement.en: According to Skeptoid, the basic plot of the Kirtland, Ohio story is that around 1900 a Dr. Crow and his wife, who may have lived on Wisner Road, cared for a number of children with hydrocephalus at home.

claims.quote: The children thought the doctor had killed her, so they rose up and attacked and murdered him. They then set the house on fire and escaped into the woods, where ever since they lived off the land, sometimes appearing and frightening humans.

statement.id: Dalam kisah itu, anak-anak mengira sang dokter membunuh istrinya, lalu menyerang dan membunuhnya, membakar rumah, dan kabur ke hutan; sejak itu mereka hidup dari alam dan kadang muncul menakuti manusia.
statement.en: In the story the children thought the doctor had killed his wife, rose up and murdered him, set the house on fire and escaped into the woods, living off the land ever since and sometimes appearing to frighten humans.

claims.quote: The story is without any evidence; any number of researchers have tried to track down records or news articles mentioning such a doctor, using various spellings of Crow.

statement.id: Menurut Skeptoid, kisah itu tanpa bukti; banyak peneliti telah mencari catatan atau artikel berita tentang dokter semacam itu dengan berbagai ejaan Crow.
statement.en: According to Skeptoid, the story is without evidence; many researchers have tried to find records or news articles mentioning such a doctor, using various spellings of Crow.

claims.quote: If the children's heads were visibly enlarged, it would mean they were very young, probably less than two, and prior to the 1940s it was unlikely they would have survived at all, as the shunt treatment had not yet been developed.

statement.id: Menurut Skeptoid, jika kepala anak-anak itu tampak membesar, berarti mereka sangat muda, mungkin kurang dari dua tahun, dan sebelum 1940-an mereka hampir tak mungkin bertahan hidup karena perawatan shunt belum dikembangkan.
statement.en: According to Skeptoid, if the children's heads were visibly enlarged they would have been very young, probably under two, and before the 1940s they were unlikely to have survived at all as shunt treatment had not yet been developed.

claims.quote: In previous eras, more people accepted the stigmatization of people with physical disfigurements; today, I would hope, most of us would rather teach our younger generation to have compassion and acceptance for such people, rather than to vilify them as monsters for our late night fiction.

statement.id: Penulis Skeptoid berpendapat bahwa kisah melon heads memburukkan orang dengan cacat fisik sebagai monster, padahal generasi muda sebaiknya diajari belas kasih dan penerimaan terhadap mereka.
statement.en: The Skeptoid author argues the melon head stories vilify people with physical disfigurements as monsters, whereas younger generations should rather be taught compassion and acceptance of such people.

summary.en: Michigan: children with hydrocephalus from an asylum.

cultural_context.id: Kisah ma bong diceritakan turun-temurun di kalangan orang utara, dan menurut penulis sebuah artikel populer disertai nasihat agar berhati-hati dan tidak menyapa sosok itu bila bertemu.
cultural_context.en: The ma bong tale is passed down among northern people and, according to the writer of a popular article, comes with warnings to take care and not to speak to the figure if met.

description.id: Dalam kisah Lanna, cabai dioleskan pada kepala kerbau, telur dilemparkan satu per satu kepada yang mengejar, dan tangga rumah dibalik agar roh itu tak bisa naik dan tersesat.
description.en: In the Lanna tale, chilli is smeared on the buffalo head, eggs are thrown one at a time to the pursuer, and the house ladder is turned upside down so the spirit cannot climb and loses its way.

title.en: The two friends and the ma bong

role.id: Sahabat yang berubah menjadi roh bertubuh kuda
role.en: The friend who becomes a horse-bodied spirit

summary.id: Dua sahabat pergi bersama melakukan "แอ่วสาว-อู้สาว", tetapi seorang di antaranya selalu memisahkan diri. Yang lain membuntutinya dan melihatnya menjilati tengkorak kepala kerbau. Atas nasihat pembimbing, ia mengoleskan cabai pada tengkorak itu. Saat dikejar sahabatnya yang bermata merah, ia melemparkan telur satu per satu, lalu membalik tangga rumahnya. Sahabat itu berjalan mengitari rumah dengan kepala manusia dan tubuh kuda, dan paginya tampak jejak kaki kuda di sekeliling rumah. Ada versi yang menyebut ia ditemukan mati sebagai mayat, ada pula yang menyebut seekor kuda kecil mati di dalam rumah.
summary.en: Two friends go out together on "แอ่วสาว-อู้สาว", but one keeps slipping away. The other follows and sees him licking a buffalo skull. On an adviser's counsel he smears chilli on the skull. Chased by his red-eyed friend, he throws eggs one at a time and then turns his ladder upside down. The friend circles the house with a human head and a horse's body, and in the morning horse hoofprints are seen around the house. Some versions say he was found dead as a corpse, others that a small horse lay dead in the house.

short_description.id: Ma bong adalah roh dalam kepercayaan orang Lanna di Thailand utara yang selalu dikaitkan dengan kuda, sering digambarkan bertubuh bawah kuda dan bertubuh atas manusia.
short_description.en: Ma bong is a spirit believed in by the Lanna people of northern Thailand, always associated with horses and often described with a horse's lower body and a human's upper body.

long_description.id: Ma bong, Phi Ma bong, atau Phi Ma adalah roh gaib yang dipercaya orang Lanna di Thailand utara. Wujud dan cirinya berbeda menurut cerita: ada yang menggambarkannya bertubuh bawah kuda dan bertubuh atas laki-laki, arwah laki-laki yang belum pernah beristri; ada yang menganggapnya arwah kuda mati yang suka menggerogoti kepala kerbau kering; ada pula yang menyebutnya bertubuh atas perempuan cantik yang memikat pemuda lalu membunuhnya. Sebuah artikel jurnal menyebutnya hantu berwujud kuda yang keluar pada malam hari, dan nama ม้าบ้อง disusun dari unsur kuda dan sebuah organ.
long_description.en: Ma bong, Phi Ma bong or Phi Ma is a supernatural spirit believed in by the Lanna people of northern Thailand. Its form varies by story: some describe it with a horse's lower body and a man's upper body, the spirit of men who never had partners; some think it the spirit of a dead horse that likes to nibble dried buffalo heads; others give it the upper body of a beautiful woman who lures young men and kills them. A journal article calls it a ghost with a horse's form that goes out at night, and the name ม้าบ้อง is built from the elements horse and an organ.

long_description.id: Meski beragam, ma bong selalu dikaitkan dengan kuda: kehadirannya sering disertai suara ringkikan dan derap kuda, dan ia lenyap secara misterius dengan hanya meninggalkan jejak tapal kuda. Seorang penulis menuturkan bahwa ibunya mendengar derap kaki kuda dari belakang tetapi tak melihat apa pun, dan neneknya menggambarkan sosok itu sebagai kuda kecil yang kadang berjalan di tengah pekarangan.
long_description.en: Despite the variations, ma bong is always associated with horses: its presence is often accompanied by neighing and galloping, and it vanishes mysteriously, leaving only horse tracks. One writer relates that her mother heard hoofbeats from behind but saw nothing, and that her grandmother described the figure as a small horse that sometimes walks in the middle of the yard.

long_description.id: Dalam kisah Lanna yang paling terkenal, dua sahabat pergi bersama menjalankan tradisi "แอ่วสาว-อู้สาว". Seorang pemuda membuntuti sahabatnya dan melihatnya menjilati kepala kerbau karena lapar; atas nasihat seorang pembimbing ia melumurinya dengan cabai. Saat dikejar sahabatnya yang bermata merah, ia melemparkan telur satu per satu dan membalik tangga rumahnya; sahabat itu mengitari rumah dengan kepala manusia dan tubuh kuda, dan paginya tampak jejak kaki kuda di sekeliling rumah. Ada versi yang menyebut sahabat itu ditemukan mati sebagai mayat, ada pula yang menyebut seekor kuda kecil mati di rumah itu.
long_description.en: In the best-known Lanna tale, two friends go out together on the custom of "แอ่วสาว-อู้สาว". A young man follows his friend and sees him hungrily licking a buffalo's head; on an adviser's counsel he smears it with chilli. Chased by his red-eyed friend, he throws eggs one at a time and turns his ladder upside down; the friend circles the house with a human head and a horse's body, and in the morning hoofprints are seen around the house. Some versions say the friend was found dead as a corpse, others that a small horse lay dead in the house.

long_description.id: Konon phi ma bong sering keluar pada malam bulan mati dan bulan purnama, dan orang yang bertemu dengannya tidak boleh menyapanya agar tidak dicelakai; ada pula nasihat agar berhati-hati jangan sampai bertemu phi ma bong yang bersembunyi. Dalam sebuah pameran hantu lokal Thailand, Phi Ma Bong dari utara ditampilkan berwujud besar mirip kuda, bermata merah garang, dan menyeringai mengancam; kadang setengah manusia setengah kuda, dan konon menculik anak-anak atau memikat orang ke dunia roh.
long_description.en: It is said the phi ma bong often comes out on new-moon and full-moon nights, and anyone who meets it must not speak to it lest they be harmed; there is also a warning to take care not to meet a phi ma bong lying in wait. In an exhibition of Thai local ghosts, Phi Ma Bong from the North was shown with a large horse-like form, fierce red eyes and a menacing grin; sometimes half-human, half-horse, it is rumoured to abduct children or lure people into the spirit world.

statement.en: Ma bong (ม้าบ้อง), Phi Ma bong or Phi Ma is a supernatural spirit believed in by the Lanna of northern Thailand; its form varies by story.

claims.quote: Some describe Ma bong as a creature with the lower body of a horse and the upper body of a human male, said to be the spirit of men who have never had sexual partners. Or some believe that it is the spirit of a dead horse, also believed Ma bong likes to nibble on dried buffalo heads.

claims.quote: Despite these variations, one consistent detail is Ma bong's association with horses. Its presence is often accompanied by sounds of neighing and galloping, and it mysteriously disappears, leaving behind only horse tracks.

short_description.id: Beast of Bladenboro adalah kriptid yang dituduh membunuh banyak hewan di Bladenboro, North Carolina, pada 1953–54.
short_description.en: The Beast of Bladenboro is a cryptid blamed for killing many animals in Bladenboro, North Carolina, in 1953–54.

long_description.id: Beast of Bladenboro adalah kriptid yang dituduh atas serangkaian kematian hewan di Bladenboro, North Carolina, pada musim dingin 1953–54. Menurut laporan, hewan itu biasanya meremukkan atau memenggal korbannya, yang kebanyakan anjing. Menurut saksi dan pelacak, kemungkinan ia sejenis kucing liar, tetapi identitasnya tidak pernah dipastikan.
long_description.en: The Beast of Bladenboro is a cryptid blamed for a string of animal deaths in Bladenboro, North Carolina, in the winter of 1953–54. According to reports, the animal usually crushed or decapitated its victims, which were mostly dogs. Witnesses and trackers thought it likely a wildcat, but its identity was never confirmed.

long_description.id: Kematian hewan pertama yang mungkin berkaitan dilaporkan pada 29 Desember 1953, ketika saksi menggambarkan makhluk ramping, hitam, sekitar 5 kaki yang membunuh seekor anjing di Clarkton. Pada 31 Desember 1953, dua anjing warga Bladenboro ditemukan mati dengan banyak darah di dekat kandangnya. Otopsi pada salah satu anjing dilaporkan menemukan hanya dua atau tiga tetes darah di tubuhnya.
long_description.en: The first possibly related animal deaths were reported on December 29, 1953, when witnesses described a sleek, black creature about 5 feet long that killed a dog in Clarkton. On December 31, 1953, two dogs owned by a Bladenboro resident turned up dead near their kennels amid a great deal of blood. An autopsy on one of the dogs reportedly found only two or three drops of blood in the body.

long_description.id: Sebuah penanda sejarah di Bladenboro menyebut kota kecil itu diteror makhluk misterius mirip kucing yang menyerang hewan setempat dan menguras darahnya; penampakan yang dilaporkan menggambarkan jeritan mengerikan, dan serangannya menarik liputan berita nasional. Pada malam 5 Januari lebih dari 500 orang dan anjing memburunya, namun makhluk itu tetap sulit ditangkap. Pada 13 Januari seorang petani menembak bobcat yang tersangkut perangkap, dan wali kota mengumumkan beast telah ditemukan dan dibunuh, meski dipertanyakan apakah kucing sekecil itu bisa membunuh anjing-anjing tersebut.
long_description.en: A historical marker in Bladenboro says the small town was terrorized by a mysterious cat-like creature that attacked local animals, draining their blood; reported sightings described a terrible scream, and the attacks drew national news coverage. On the night of January 5, a crowd of over 500 people and dogs searched for it, yet the creature remained elusive. On January 13 a farmer shot a bobcat caught in a trap and the mayor announced the beast had been found and killed, though doubts were raised that so small a cat could have killed the dogs.

long_description.id: Banyak laporan menggambarkannya sebagai kucing tetapi tidak sepakat soal jenisnya. Seorang kurator museum menduga koyote, seorang warga Lumberton mengira anjing campuran bernama Big Boy, dan wali kota Fussell sendiri mengatakan ia yakin makhluk itu hoaks. Kota itu kini merayakan kisahnya dalam Beast Fest tahunan dengan "BOB" sebagai maskot.
long_description.en: Many accounts describe it as feline but do not agree on a species. A museum curator suggested a coyote, a man from Lumberton thought it was a dog named Big Boy, and Mayor Fussell himself said he believed the creature to be a hoax. The town now celebrates the story in an annual Beast Fest with "BOB" as mascot.

cultural_context.id: Kisah ini dirayakan kota Bladenboro dalam Beast Fest tahunan, dan literatur tentang peristiwanya cenderung skeptis karena publisitas yang didapat kota lewat berita sensasional.
cultural_context.en: The story is celebrated by the town of Bladenboro in its annual Beast Fest, and literature on the events tends toward skepticism because of the publicity the sensational news brought the town.

text.id: Burung dalam Taiheiki, kemudian dinamai dan digambar Toriyama Sekien (terbit 1779)
text.en: The bird of the Taiheiki, later named and drawn by Toriyama Sekien (published 1779)

short_description.id: Itsumade adalah burung aneh dalam Taiheiki yang muncul di atas Shishinden pada musim gugur 1334 saat wabah dan berseru "itsumade, itsumade" (sampai kapan?). Namanya diberikan Toriyama Sekien.
short_description.en: Itsumade is an eerie bird of the Taiheiki that appeared above the Shishinden in the autumn of 1334 during an epidemic, crying "itsumade, itsumade" (until when?). The name was given by Toriyama Sekien.

long_description.id: Itsumade (以津真天) adalah burung aneh dalam kumpulan gambar yōkai 『今昔画図続百鬼』 karya Toriyama Sekien, terbit pada 1779. Keterangan gambarnya merujuk pada kisah dalam Taiheiki bahwa Hiroari menembak burung aneh yang berseru "itsumade itsumade".
long_description.en: Itsumade (以津真天) is an eerie bird featured in the yōkai picture collection 『今昔画図続百鬼』 by Toriyama Sekien, published in 1779. Its caption refers to the Taiheiki episode in which Hiroari shot the eerie bird that cried "itsumade itsumade".

long_description.id: Menurut Taiheiki, sekitar musim gugur 1334 (tahun-tahun Kenmu), wabah menewaskan banyak orang dan hampir setiap malam seekor burung aneh muncul di atas Shishinden sambil berseru "itsumade itsumade" (sampai kapan?), sehingga menimbulkan ketakutan besar. Para bangsawan teringat bagaimana pemanah ulung Minamoto no Yorimasa menewaskan nue, dan meminta Oki Jirōzaemon Hiroari menembaknya; ia berhasil menjatuhkan burung itu dengan anak panah kabura-ya. Hiroari mendapat pangkat kelima dan dua perkebunan di Inaba; menurut Yokai.com ia kemudian diberi nama Mayumi, "busur sejati".
long_description.en: The Taiheiki places the episode around the fall of 1334 (the Kenmu years): a plague was killing many people, and on nearly every night a strange bird perched above the Shishinden calling "itsumade itsumade" (until when?), which terrified people. The nobles remembered how the master archer Minamoto no Yorimasa killed the nue, and requested Oki Jirōzaemon Hiroari, who brought the bird down with a kabura-ya. Hiroari was raised to the fifth rank and granted two estates in Inaba; according to Yokai.com he was afterwards given the name Mayumi, "true bow".

long_description.id: Taiheiki melukiskan burung itu berkepala seperti manusia, bertubuh ular, berparuh bengkok dengan gigi seperti gergaji, dan berbentang sayap satu jō enam shaku (sekitar 4,8 meter, menurut Yokai.com juga bercakar mengerikan); suaranya terasa seperti menyemburkan api dan kilat. Dalam Taiheiki burung itu hanya disebut "burung aneh"; nama Itsumade diberikan Sekien berdasarkan suara cuitnya.
long_description.en: The Taiheiki describes the bird with a human-like head, a snake-like body, a curved beak with saw-like teeth and a wingspan of one jō six shaku (about 4.8 meters, with terrible claws according to Yokai.com); its cry seemed to spit fire and lightning. In the Taiheiki the bird is only called an "eerie bird"; the name Itsumade was given by Sekien from its cry.

long_description.id: Literatur yōkai sejak era Shōwa menjelaskan bahwa burung ini berseru di dekat jenazah yang dibiarkan, atau bahwa ia adalah arwah penasaran korban perang dan kelaparan yang berubah menjadi burung. Yokai.com menambahkan bahwa Itsumade muncul di langit malam pada masa sulit dan terbang berputar-putar sepanjang malam.
long_description.en: Yōkai literature since the Shōwa era explains that the bird cries near corpses left unattended, or that it is the vengeful spirit of those who died in war and famine turned into a bird. Yokai.com adds that itsumade appear in the night sky during times of trouble and fly in circles all night long.

literal_meaning.id: "Sampai kapan?", dari suara cuitnya 「いつまで、いつまで」.
literal_meaning.en: "Until when?", from its cry 「いつまで、いつまで」.

summary.id: Saat wabah menyebar, burung itu berseru di atas Shishinden setiap malam. Oki Jirōzaemon Hiroari ditunjuk menembaknya dan menjatuhkannya dengan anak panah, lalu dihadiahi pangkat dan tanah.
summary.en: As the epidemic spread, the bird cried above the Shishinden every night. Oki Jirōzaemon Hiroari was chosen to shoot it, brought it down with an arrow, and was rewarded with rank and land.

description.en: According to the Taiheiki, during an epidemic an eerie bird appeared almost every night above the Shishinden and was later shot by Hiroari.

claims.quote: Itsumade (Japanese: 以津真天) is an eerie bird featured in the Japanese collection of Yōkai pictures, the Konjaku Gazu Zoku Hyakki by Toriyama Sekien published in 1779.

statement.id: Itsumade adalah burung aneh yang digambar Toriyama Sekien.
statement.en: Itsumade is a strange bird pictured by Toriyama Sekien.

claims.quote: According to the Taiheiki, around the fall of 1334 (in the Kenmu years), an epidemic illness was causing many deaths and almost every night, an eerie bird appeared on top of the Shishinden (ja:紫宸殿) crying "itsumade itsumade" (until when?

statement.id: Dalam Taiheiki, jeritannya terdengar saat wabah mematikan.
statement.en: A Taiheiki episode places its cries during a deadly epidemic.

claims.quote: The nobility thought back to how the master of arrows Minamoto no Yorimasa slew the nue and made a request to Oki Jirōzaemon Hiroari (ja:真弓広有) who splendidly shot down the eerie bird with a kabura-ya.

statement.id: Dalam kisah itu, pemanah bernama Hiroari menembaknya.
statement.en: In that account an archer named Hiroari shoots the bird.

claims.quote: In the Taiheiki, the bird is merely written to be the "eerie bird" with no distinctive name.

statement.id: Taiheiki hanya menyebut burung aneh tanpa nama Itsumade.
statement.en: The Taiheiki describes a strange bird without calling it Itsumade.

claims.quote: 以津真天（いつまで）は、鳥山石燕による江戸時代の日本の妖怪画集『今昔画図続百鬼』にある怪鳥。解説文に「広有 いつまでいつまでと鳴し怪鳥を射し事 太平記に委し」とあるように、『太平記』巻12の「広有射怪鳥事」に登場する怪鳥を題材に創られた妖怪であることがわかる。

statement.id: Wikipedia bahasa Jepang: Itsumade (以津真天) adalah burung aneh dalam kumpulan gambar yōkai zaman Edo 『今昔画図続百鬼』 karya Toriyama Sekien; keterangan gambarnya menunjukkan bahwa ia dibuat dari burung aneh dalam 「広有射怪鳥事」 di jilid 12 『太平記』.
statement.en: Japanese Wikipedia: Itsumade (以津真天) is an eerie bird in Toriyama Sekien's Edo-period yōkai picture collection 『今昔画図続百鬼』; its caption shows it was created from the eerie bird in 「広有射怪鳥事」 in scroll 12 of the 『太平記』.

claims.quote: その怪鳥は顔が人間のようで、曲がったくちばしに鋸のような歯が並び、体はヘビのようで、両足の爪は剣のように鋭く、翼長は1丈6尺（約4.8メートル）もあったという。

statement.id: Burung itu berwajah seperti manusia, berparuh bengkok dengan gigi seperti gergaji, bertubuh seperti ular, bercakar tajam seperti pedang di kedua kakinya, dan berbentang sayap 1 jō 6 shaku (sekitar 4,8 meter).
statement.en: The bird had a human-like face, a curved beak lined with saw-like teeth, a snake-like body, claws on both feet sharp as swords, and a wingspan of 1 jō 6 shaku (about 4.8 meters).

claims.quote: 昭和以降の妖怪関連の文献では、いつまでんとも読まれている。戦乱や飢餓などで死んだ人の死体をそのまま放っておくと、この怪鳥が死体の近くに止まり、「死体をいつまで放っておくのか」との意味で「いつまで、いつまで」と鳴くもの、またはそうして死んだ者たちの怨霊が鳥と化したものであるという解説がつけられて紹介されてもいる。

statement.id: Dalam literatur yōkai sejak era Shōwa, namanya juga dibaca Itsumaden; dijelaskan pula bahwa jika jenazah korban perang atau kelaparan dibiarkan, burung ini hinggap di dekatnya dan berseru 「いつまで、いつまで」 (sampai kapan?), atau bahwa ia adalah arwah penasaran orang-orang yang mati demikian yang berubah menjadi burung.
statement.en: In yōkai literature since the Shōwa era the name is also read Itsumaden; explanations also say that when the bodies of those who died in war or famine are left, this bird perches near them and cries 「いつまで、いつまで」 (until when?), or that it is the vengeful spirit of those who died thus, turned into a bird.

claims.quote: 『太平記』において、この鳥は「怪鳥」と記述されているのみで明確な名前などは記載されていない。『今昔画図続百鬼』において付された「以津真天」という名称は、鳥山石燕がこの逸話を『今昔画図続百鬼』に描く際、その鳴き声をもとに名づけたものとされる。

statement.id: Dalam 『太平記』 burung ini hanya disebut 「怪鳥」 tanpa nama jelas; nama 「以津真天」 dalam 『今昔画図続百鬼』 dianggap diberikan Toriyama Sekien berdasarkan suara cuitnya ketika menggambar kisah ini.
statement.en: In the 『太平記』 the bird is only described as a 「怪鳥」 with no clear name; the name 「以津真天」 in 『今昔画図続百鬼』 is regarded as given by Toriyama Sekien from its cry when he drew this episode.

claims.quote: 今年天下に疫癘有て、病死する者甚多し。是のみならず、其秋の比より紫宸殿の上に怪鳥出来て、「いつまで／＼。」とぞ鳴ける。

statement.id: Taiheiki: pada tahun itu wabah melanda negeri dan banyak orang meninggal; selain itu, sejak musim gugur seekor burung aneh muncul di atas Shishinden dan berseru 「いつまで、いつまで」.
statement.en: Taiheiki: that year an epidemic spread through the land and many died; moreover, from that autumn an eerie bird appeared above the Shishinden crying 「いつまで、いつまで」.

claims.quote: 頭は如人して、身は蛇の形也。嘴の前曲て歯如鋸生違。両の足に長距有て、利如剣。羽崎を延て見之、長一丈六尺也。

statement.id: Taiheiki: kepalanya seperti manusia dan tubuhnya berbentuk ular; paruhnya bengkok ke depan dengan gigi seperti gergaji, kedua kakinya bertaji panjang setajam pedang, dan bila sayapnya dibentangkan panjangnya satu jō enam shaku.
statement.en: Taiheiki: its head was like a human's and its body snake-shaped; its beak curved forward with saw-like teeth, both feet had long spurs sharp as swords, and its outstretched wings measured one jō six shaku.

claims.quote: 鳴時口より火炎を吐歟と覚て、声の内より電して、其光御簾の内へ散徹す。

statement.id: Taiheiki: saat berseru, seakan-akan api keluar dari mulutnya dan kilat memancar dari dalam suaranya, cahayanya menembus hingga ke dalam tirai istana.
statement.en: Taiheiki: when it cried, it seemed to spit flames from its mouth, lightning flashed from within its voice, and the light penetrated through to the inside of the blinds.

claims.quote: 二条関白左大臣殿の被召仕候、隠岐次郎左衛門広有と申者こそ、其器に堪たる者にて候へ。

statement.id: Taiheiki: dikatakan bahwa Oki Jirōzaemon Hiroari, pelayan Menteri Kiri Kanpaku dari Nijō, adalah orang yang mampu menangani tugas itu.
statement.en: Taiheiki: it was said that Oki Jirōzaemon Hiroari, in the service of the Nijō Kanpaku and Minister of the Left, was fit for the task.

claims.quote: 主上弥叡感有て、其夜軈て広有を被成五位、次の日因幡国に大庄二箇所賜てけり。

statement.id: Taiheiki: pada malam itu juga Hiroari dinaikkan ke pangkat kelima, dan keesokan harinya diberi dua perkebunan besar di Provinsi Inaba.
statement.en: Taiheiki: that same night Hiroari was raised to the fifth rank, and the next day was granted two large estates in Inaba Province.

claims.quote: Itsumade are kaichō, or strange birds. They have the face of a human with a pointed beak, and the body of a snake with wings, and terrible claws. Their wingspan is 4.8 meters.

statement.id: Yokai.com: Itsumade adalah kaichō, burung aneh, berwajah manusia dengan paruh runcing, bertubuh ular bersayap, dan bercakar mengerikan; bentang sayapnya 4,8 meter.
statement.en: Yokai.com: Itsumade are kaichō, strange birds, with a human face and pointed beak, a snake's body with wings, and terrible claws; their wingspan is 4.8 meters.

claims.quote: Itsumade appear in the night sky during times of trouble—such as plagues and disasters, or flying over battlegrounds where many have died.

statement.en: Yokai.com: itsumade appear in the night sky during times of trouble, such as plagues and disasters, or flying over battlegrounds where many have died.

claims.quote: The strange birds fly about in circles all night long, crying out in a terrible voice.

statement.id: Yokai.com: burung aneh ini terbang berputar-putar sepanjang malam sambil berseru dengan suara mengerikan.
statement.en: Yokai.com: the strange birds fly about in circles all night long, crying out in a terrible voice.

claims.quote: It is thought that the spirits of the dead and suffering form into onryō which take the shape of these birds. They demand recognition of their suffering and torment.

statement.id: Yokai.com: diduga arwah orang mati dan yang menderita membentuk onryō yang berwujud burung-burung ini, menuntut pengakuan atas penderitaan mereka.
statement.en: Yokai.com: it is thought that the spirits of the dead and suffering form into onryō that take the shape of these birds, demanding recognition of their suffering and torment.

claims.quote: Afterwards, Hiroari was given the name Mayumi, meaning true bow.

statement.id: Yokai.com: setelah itu Hiroari diberi nama Mayumi, yang berarti "busur sejati".
statement.en: Yokai.com: afterwards Hiroari was given the name Mayumi, meaning "true bow".

short_description.id: Mapinguari adalah kriptid dari cerita rakyat Brasil, digambarkan sebagai makhluk berbulu, berbau busuk, bermata tunggal, dan bermulut di perut yang memakan manusia.
short_description.en: The Mapinguari is a cryptid from Brazilian folklore, described as a hairy, foul-smelling, one-eyed creature with a mouth in its belly that eats people.

long_description.id: Mapinguari atau Mapinguary adalah kriptid dari cerita rakyat Brasil. Ia sering digambarkan sebagai hewan berbulu yang sangat berbau busuk dan berbeda dari Bigfoot Amerika Utara. Deskripsi lain menyebutnya pemakan manusia dengan kuku melengkung seperti kait, kaki menghadap ke belakang, berjalan dengan dua kaki, mulut menganga di perut, dan mata tunggal besar seperti Cyclops. Ukurannya digambarkan sebanding dengan manusia atau lebih besar.
long_description.en: The Mapinguari, or Mapinguary, is a cryptid from Brazilian folklore. It is often described as an extremely foul-smelling, hairy animal distinct from the North American Bigfoot. Other accounts add that it eats people, with hooked nails, feet that point backwards, an upright two-legged walk, a gaping mouth in its abdomen, and one large Cyclops-like eye. Its size has been depicted as comparable to a human or larger.

long_description.id: Bulunya yang panjang dan rapat konon cukup tebal hingga makhluk itu kebal peluru, kecuali di sekitar pusar yang dianggap satu-satunya bagian yang rentan terhadap tembakan. Ia mengaum dahsyat dan mengeluarkan bau yang dapat membuat orang gila atau bisu seumur hidup, mengunyah kepala korban perlahan seperti mengunyah tembakau, dan menandai kehadirannya dengan jeritan keras. Kotorannya diklaim menyerupai kotoran kuda.
long_description.en: Its long, dense hair is claimed to be thick enough to make the creature bulletproof except around the navel, said to be the only place vulnerable to gunshots. It roars terribly and gives off a stench said to drive people mad or mute for life, chews its victim's head slowly as though chewing tobacco, and announces itself with loud screaming. Its dung is claimed to resemble that of a horse.

long_description.id: Secara tradisional Mapinguari adalah salah satu roh yang melindungi hutan dan hewannya dari pemburu, penebang kayu, dan orang yang tidak hormat. Menurut cerita rakyat, ia semula manusia biasa, seorang dukun yang menemukan kunci keabadian dan dihukum para dewa menjadi makhluk mengerikan. Di Acre dikatakan orang Pribumi yang sangat tua berubah menjadi Mapinguari. Namanya, menurut Câmara Cascudo, berasal dari Tupi-Guarani yang berarti 'benda berkaki terpuntir atau menghadap ke belakang', dan suku Karitiana menyebutnya Kida harara.
long_description.en: By tradition the Mapinguari numbers among the spirits that guard the forest and its animals against hunters, woodcutters, and disrespectful visitors. In folklore it was originally a normal human, a shaman who discovered the key to immortality and was punished by the gods with a hideous form. In Acre, Indigenous people who reach advanced age were said to turn into Mapinguari. Its name, according to Câmara Cascudo, comes from Tupi-Guarani words meaning 'the thing with a twisted or backwards-turned foot', and the Karitiana call it Kida harara.

long_description.id: Bernard Heuvelmans (1958) menduga ia primata tak dikenal mirip Bigfoot, sedangkan pada makalah 1993 David C. Oren mengusulkan bahwa legenda itu didasarkan pada sloth tanah yang punah; Paul S. Martin (2005) menolak kemungkinan sloth tanah bertahan hidup karena tak ada sisanya dalam catatan fosil Holosen. Brian Dunning menilai tidak ada bukti bahwa mapinguari lebih dari makhluk cerita rakyat, kecuali anekdot yang dikumpulkan Oren.
long_description.en: Bernard Heuvelmans (1958) speculated it was an unknown primate akin to Bigfoot, while in a 1993 paper David C. Oren suggested the legend was based on an extinct ground sloth; Paul S. Martin (2005) argued against ground sloth survival because no remains had been found in Holocene fossil records. Brian Dunning judges there is no evidence the mapinguari is anything beyond a folkloric creature, except for the anecdotes Oren collected.

cultural_context.id: Mapinguari secara tradisional adalah salah satu roh yang melindungi hutan dan hewannya dari pemburu, penebang kayu, dan orang yang tidak hormat.
cultural_context.en: The Mapinguari has traditionally ranked among the spirits that shield the forest and its animals from hunters, woodcutters, and disrespectful visitors.

claims.quote: The Mapinguari is often described as an extremely foul-smelling, hairy animal that is distinct from the North American Bigfoot.

statement.id: Mapinguari kerap digambarkan sebagai hewan berbulu yang amat berbau busuk.
statement.en: The Mapinguari is often described as an extremely foul-smelling, hairy animal that is distinct from the North American Bigfoot.

claims.quote: Descriptions further allege that the cryptid is a man-eating creature with hook-shaped nails, backwards-facing feet, a bipedal gait, a gaping mouth in its abdomen, and a single eye like the mythological Cyclops.

statement.id: Makhluk ini digambarkan memangsa manusia dengan kuku kait, kaki terbalik, dan mulut menganga di perut.
statement.en: Descriptions further allege that the cryptid is a man-eating creature with hook-shaped nails, backwards-facing feet, a bipedal gait, a gaping mouth in its abdomen, and a single eye like the mythological Cyclops.

claims.quote: The creature's size has been depicted as either comparable to a human, or larger.

statement.id: Ukuran tubuh makhluk ini digambarkan seukuran manusia atau lebih besar.
statement.en: The creature's size has been depicted as either comparable to a human, or larger.

claims.quote: The other recurring feature of the Mapinguari is a large, single eye in either the abdomen or the forehead, like a Cyclops.

statement.id: Ciri berulang lainnya adalah mata tunggal besar di perut atau dahi mirip Cyclops.
statement.en: The other recurring feature of the Mapinguari is a large, single eye in either the abdomen or the forehead, like a Cyclops.

claims.quote: The Mapinguari or Mapinguary is a cryptid from Brazilian folklore.

statement.id: Mapinguari atau Mapinguary adalah kriptid dari cerita rakyat Brasil.
statement.en: The Mapinguari or Mapinguary is a cryptid from Brazilian folklore.

claims.quote: Câmara Cascudo identified the name Mapinguari as deriving from the Tupi-Guarani mbaé-pi-guari (Guarani: mba'e "that, the thing" + pĭ "foot" + guarî "crooked, twisted") meaning "the thing that has a clubbed, twisted, or backwards-turned foot".

statement.id: Câmara Cascudo mengidentifikasi nama Mapinguari berasal dari Tupi-Guarani mbaé-pi-guari (Guarani: mba'e 'itu, benda' + pĭ 'kaki' + guarî 'bengkok, terpuntir'), yang berarti 'benda yang berkaki membulat, terpuntir, atau menghadap ke belakang'.
statement.en: Câmara Cascudo identified the name Mapinguari as deriving from the Tupi-Guarani mbaé-pi-guari (Guarani: mba'e 'that, the thing' + pĭ 'foot' + guarî 'crooked, twisted'), meaning 'the thing that has a clubbed, twisted, or backwards-turned foot'.

claims.quote: The Mapinguari is known to the Karitiana people of Brazil as Kida harara (Karitiâna: "laughing beast"), Kida so'emo ("beast with black face") or Owoj/Owojo (lit. "maternal grandfather" or "mother's brother's son").

statement.id: Bagi suku Karitiana di Brasil, Mapinguari dikenal sebagai Kida harara ('binatang tertawa'), Kida so'emo ('binatang berwajah hitam'), atau Owoj/Owojo (harfiah 'kakek dari pihak ibu' atau 'anak saudara laki-laki ibu').
statement.en: The Mapinguari is known to the Karitiana people of Brazil as Kida harara ('laughing beast'), Kida so'emo ('beast with black face') or Owoj/Owojo (lit. 'maternal grandfather' or 'mother's brother's son').

claims.quote: Descriptions of the alleged creature portray a giant monkey with a likewise simian face ... It is purportedly hairy like a spider monkey, possessing long red, brown, or black hair, which is claimed to be dense enough to render the animal effectively bulletproof save only the area near the navel, which is further alleged to be the only place vulnerable to gunshots.

statement.id: Deskripsi makhluk yang diduga itu menggambarkan monyet raksasa berwajah mirip kera; ia konon berbulu seperti monyet laba-laba dengan rambut panjang merah, cokelat, atau hitam yang diklaim cukup rapat hingga kebal peluru, kecuali area dekat pusar yang diduga satu-satunya tempat rentan terhadap tembakan.
statement.en: Descriptions of the alleged creature portray a giant monkey with a simian face; it is purportedly hairy like a spider monkey, with long red, brown, or black hair claimed to be dense enough to make it effectively bulletproof save the area near the navel, alleged to be the only place vulnerable to gunshots.

claims.quote: The Mapinguari is a man-eater that eats its victims head-first. It chews its victim's head slowly, as though it were chewing tobacco.

statement.id: Mapinguari adalah pemakan manusia yang memakan korbannya dari kepala; ia mengunyah kepala korban perlahan seperti mengunyah tembakau.
statement.en: The Mapinguari is a man-eater that eats its victims head-first, chewing the head slowly as though it were chewing tobacco.

claims.quote: The Mapinguari is a man-eater that eats its victims head-first. ... It is variously said to be nocturnal, crepuscular, or diurnal, and to lay in wait in the dim light of the deep forest before lunging to attack. It announces itself with loud screaming, frightening humans into flight

statement.id: Mapinguari dikatakan aktif pada malam, senja, atau siang, dan menunggu dalam cahaya redup hutan dalam sebelum menerkam; ia menandai kehadirannya dengan jeritan keras yang membuat manusia lari ketakutan.
statement.en: The Mapinguari is variously said to be nocturnal, crepuscular, or diurnal and to lie in wait in the dim light of the deep forest before lunging to attack; it announces itself with loud screaming, frightening humans into flight.

claims.quote: In Acre, it was said that Indigenous people who attain an advanced age transform into Mapinguari.

statement.id: Di Acre dikatakan bahwa orang Pribumi yang mencapai usia lanjut berubah menjadi Mapinguari.
statement.en: In Acre, it was said that Indigenous people who attain an advanced age transform into Mapinguari.

claims.quote: Mapinguari dung is claimed to resemble the droppings of a horse.

statement.id: Kotoran Mapinguari diklaim menyerupai kotoran kuda.
statement.en: Mapinguari dung is claimed to resemble the droppings of a horse.

claims.quote: A rubber tapper (seringueiro) quoted in 1928 claimed that he had gone hunting in the woods while his workmate remained in their shared hut for the Sunday. When the rubber tapper returned to their dwellings, he found his companion being devoured by the Mapinguari, which had jaguar-like claws and a mouth "as large as a lapel", reaching from the face to the stomach.

statement.id: Seorang penyadap karet (seringueiro) yang dikutip pada 1928 mengaku pergi berburu sementara rekannya tinggal di pondok pada hari Minggu; saat kembali ia mendapati temannya sedang dimakan Mapinguari yang bercakar seperti jaguar dan bermulut 'sebesar kerah jas' dari wajah sampai perut.
statement.en: A rubber tapper (seringueiro) quoted in 1928 claimed he had gone hunting while his workmate stayed in their shared hut on the Sunday; returning, he found his companion being devoured by the Mapinguari, which had jaguar-like claws and a mouth 'as large as a lapel' reaching from the face to the stomach.

claims.quote: The Mapinguari was believed to haunt the forests of Pará, Amazonas, and Acre into the 20th century.

statement.id: Mapinguari dipercaya menghantui hutan-hutan Pará, Amazonas, dan Acre hingga abad ke-20.
statement.en: The Mapinguari was believed to haunt the forests of Pará, Amazonas, and Acre into the 20th century.

claims.quote: Although a legend rooted in the folklore of the Indigenous peoples of Brazil, the Mapinguari shares several similarities with the Afro-Brazilian Quibungo.

statement.id: Meski legenda yang berakar pada cerita rakyat masyarakat adat Brasil, Mapinguari memiliki beberapa kemiripan dengan Quibungo dari tradisi Afro-Brasil.
statement.en: Although a legend rooted in the folklore of the Indigenous peoples of Brazil, the Mapinguari shares several similarities with the Afro-Brazilian Quibungo.

claims.quote: Bernard Heuvelmans (1958) speculated that the Mapinguari was an unknown primate, akin to Bigfoot.

statement.id: Bernard Heuvelmans (1958) menduga Mapinguari adalah primata tak dikenal, mirip Bigfoot.
statement.en: Bernard Heuvelmans (1958) speculated that the Mapinguari was an unknown primate, akin to Bigfoot.

claims.quote: In a 1993 paper, David C. Oren suggested that the Mapinguari might be based on recent sightings of an extinct ground sloth.

statement.id: Dalam makalah 1993, David C. Oren mengusulkan bahwa Mapinguari mungkin didasarkan pada penampakan terbaru sloth tanah yang sudah punah.
statement.en: In a 1993 paper, David C. Oren suggested that the Mapinguari might be based on recent sightings of an extinct ground sloth.

claims.quote: Geobiologist Paul S. Martin (2005) argued against any credible possibility of ground sloth survival, pointing out that no ground sloth remains had been found in Holocene fossil records.

statement.id: Geobiolog Paul S. Martin (2005) menolak kemungkinan kredibel sloth tanah bertahan hidup, dengan menunjukkan bahwa tak ada sisa sloth tanah ditemukan dalam catatan fosil Holosen.
statement.en: Geobiologist Paul S. Martin (2005) argued against any credible possibility of ground sloth survival, pointing out that no ground sloth remains had been found in Holocene fossil records.

claims.quote: The mapinguari has traditionally been one of many characters said to be spirits that protect the forest and its animals from hunters, woodcutters, and any disrespectful people who come in and are loud, who make camps and leave messes, or build fires.

statement.id: Mapinguari secara tradisional adalah salah satu dari banyak tokoh yang dikatakan roh pelindung hutan dan hewannya dari pemburu, penebang kayu, dan orang tak hormat yang datang dengan berisik, mendirikan kemah lalu meninggalkan sampah, atau menyalakan api.
statement.en: The mapinguari has traditionally been one of many characters said to be spirits that protect the forest and its animals from hunters, woodcutters, and disrespectful people who come in loudly, make camps and leave messes, or build fires.

claims.quote: The mapinguari is said to be quite remarkable in its appearance. ... It's the size of a large human, with a frightening single large eye on the front of its head, its mouth enormous and located way down in the middle of its belly, its feet turned backwards to make it difficult to track, and covered in long, shaggy, reddish fur.

statement.id: Mapinguari dikatakan berpenampilan sangat mencolok: sebesar manusia besar, bermata tunggal besar yang menakutkan di depan kepala, bermulut raksasa di tengah perut, berkaki terbalik agar sulit dilacak, dan berbulu merah panjang yang lebat.
statement.en: The mapinguari is said to be quite remarkable in appearance: the size of a large human, with a frightening single large eye on the front of its head, an enormous mouth in the middle of its belly, feet turned backwards to make it difficult to track, and long, shaggy, reddish fur.

claims.quote: The mapinguari is said to be quite remarkable in its appearance. ... It roars terribly, and gives off a stench so bad it can drive to madness those unlucky enough to inhale it, even so powerful as to render them mute for the rest of their lives.

statement.id: Mapinguari mengaum dahsyat dan mengeluarkan bau busuk yang begitu hebat sehingga dapat membuat gila orang yang malang menghirupnya, bahkan membuat mereka bisu seumur hidup.
statement.en: The mapinguari roars terribly and gives off a stench so bad it can drive to madness those unlucky enough to inhale it, even so powerful as to render them mute for the rest of their lives.

claims.quote: The mapinguari in folklore has always traditionally been a normal human, a shaman who discovered the key to immortality, which angered the gods who punished him by turning him into a hideous creature with only a single eye, one huge mouth down in the middle of his abdomen, his feet turned backwards, and covered in reddish fur.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat, mapinguari secara tradisional adalah manusia biasa, seorang dukun yang menemukan kunci keabadian sehingga membuat para dewa murka dan menghukumnya menjadi makhluk mengerikan bermata tunggal, bermulut raksasa di tengah perut, berkaki terbalik, dan berbulu kemerahan.
statement.en: In folklore the mapinguari has traditionally been a normal human, a shaman who discovered the key to immortality, which angered the gods, who punished him by turning him into a hideous creature with a single eye, one huge mouth in the middle of his abdomen, backwards feet, and reddish fur.

claims.quote: No evidence exists to indicate that the mapinguari is anything but a purely folkloric creature, except for the anecdotes Oren has collected.

statement.id: Dunning menilai tidak ada bukti bahwa mapinguari adalah apa pun selain makhluk murni cerita rakyat, kecuali anekdot yang dikumpulkan Oren.
statement.en: Dunning argues that no evidence exists to indicate that the mapinguari is anything but a purely folkloric creature, except for the anecdotes Oren has collected.

short_description.id: Nine-headed bird atau Nine Phoenix adalah burung mitologis Tiongkok yang dikaitkan dengan tradisi Chu, dan dalam kisah rakyat dianggap pertanda buruk.
short_description.en: Nine-headed bird, or Nine Phoenix, is a Chinese mythological bird associated with Chu traditions, treated in folk accounts as an evil omen.

long_description.id: Nine-headed bird atau Nine Phoenix adalah burung mitologis yang dikaitkan dengan tradisi Chu. Burung ini dipuja oleh penduduk kuno Hubei yang wilayahnya pernah termasuk kerajaan Chu. Karena hubungan Chu yang bermusuhan dengan dinasti Zhou, burung totem ini dijelekkan. Teks Shanhaijing menyebut dewa berkepala sembilan, berwajah manusia dan bertubuh burung bernama Jiufeng.
long_description.en: Nine-headed bird, or Nine Phoenix, is a mythological bird associated with Chu traditions. The bird was worshipped by ancient Hubei inhabitants whose territory belonged to Chu. Because of Chu's hostile relationship with the Zhou dynasty, this totem bird was demonised. The Shanhaijing text mentions a nine-headed deity with a human face and bird's body named Jiufeng.

long_description.id: Sebuah kisah mengatakan burung semula berkepala sepuluh lalu kehilangan satu kepala akibat gigitan anjing. Menurut Bencao Gangmu, yang mencantumkan Burung Berkepala Sembilan sebagai nama Guiche, burung ini terbang dalam kegelapan, masuk ke rumah orang dan mengambil roh mereka, dan darah yang menetes dari lehernya membawa nasib buruk. Orang Jing-Chu mematikan lampu, memukul pintu, dan memelintir telinga anjing untuk mengusirnya karena burung itu konon takut anjing. Lu Changyuan mencatat kisah burung ini sebagai pertanda buruk.
long_description.en: One account says the bird originally had ten heads before losing one to a dog's bite. According to the Bencao Gangmu, which lists Nine-headed Bird as a name of the Guiche, the bird flies in the dark, enters homes and takes people's souls, and the blood dripping from its neck brings misfortune. People of Jing-Chu put out lamps, struck doors and twisted dogs' ears to ward it off, since the bird is said to fear dogs. Lu Changyuan records an account treating this bird as an evil omen.

long_description.id: Bencao Gangmu juga mencatat bahwa Guiche yang besar sayapnya membentang sekitar satu zhang, buta pada siang hari, dan jatuh bila melihat cahaya api, serta mengutip catatan Dinasti Song tentang seekor burung yang tertangkap di Changsha dengan sembilan kepala. Journey to the West menampilkan varian Nine-Headed Beast sebagai menantu Raja Naga Wansheng. Di Tiongkok modern, "burung berkepala sembilan" menjadi istilah merendahkan bagi orang Hubei.
long_description.en: The Bencao Gangmu also notes that the larger Guiche have wings spanning about a zhang, are blind by day and fall when they see firelight, and quotes a Song-period record of a bird caught at Changsha with nine heads. Journey to the West presents a Nine-Headed Beast variant as the Wansheng Dragon King's son-in-law. Today the phrase "nine-headed bird" is used in China as an insult aimed at people from Hubei.

statement.en: The Bencao Gangmu says people of Jing-Chu who heard it cry at night put out lamps, struck doors and twisted dogs' ears to ward it off, since the bird is said to fear dogs.

claims.quote: 時珍曰︰鬼車狀如鵂 ，而大者翼廣丈許，晝盲夜了，見火光輒墮。

statement.id: Li Shizhen menulis dalam entri itu bahwa Guiche (鬼車) yang besar sayapnya membentang sekitar satu zhang, buta pada siang hari tetapi melihat pada malam hari, dan jatuh bila melihat cahaya api.
statement.en: Li Shizhen writes in the entry that the larger Guiche (鬼車) have wings spanning about a zhang, are blind by day but see at night, and fall when they see firelight.

claims.quote: 宋‧李壽翁守長沙，曾捕得此鳥。狀類野鳧，赤色，身圓如箕。十頸環簇，有九頭，其一獨無而滴鮮血。

statement.id: Bencao Gangmu mengutip catatan bahwa Li Shouweng dari Dinasti Song, saat menjaga Changsha, pernah menangkap burung ini: mirip bebek liar, berwarna merah, bertubuh bundar seperti nyiru, dengan sepuluh leher berkelompok dan sembilan kepala, satu leher tanpa kepala meneteskan darah segar.
statement.en: The Bencao Gangmu quotes a record that Li Shouweng of the Song, while governing Changsha, once caught this bird: like a wild duck, red, with a round winnowing-basket body, ten necks clustered and nine heads, the one headless neck dripping fresh blood.

claims.quote: 有神，九首人面鳥身，名曰九鳳。又有神衘蛇操蛇，其狀虎首人身，四蹏長肘，名曰彊良。

statement.id: Teks Shanhaijing menyebut dewa berkepala sembilan, berwajah manusia dan bertubuh burung, bernama Jiufeng (九鳳, Sembilan Phoenix); juga disebut dewa lain berkepala harimau yang menggigit dan memegang ular, bernama Qiangliang.
statement.en: The Shanhaijing text mentions a deity with nine heads, a human face and a bird's body, named Jiufeng (九鳳, Nine Phoenix); it also mentions another deity with a tiger's head that holds snakes, named Qiangliang.

claims.quote: Due to the hostile relationship between the Kingdom of Chu and its former overlord, the reigning Zhou dynasty, the nine-headed bird, being the totem creature of the Chu people, was demonised as a result.

statement.id: Menurut artikel ini, karena hubungan yang bermusuhan antara Kerajaan Chu dan bekas penguasanya, dinasti Zhou, burung berkepala sembilan sebagai makhluk totem rakyat Chu dijelekkan.
statement.en: According to the article, owing to the hostile relationship between the Kingdom of Chu and its former overlord, the Zhou dynasty, the nine-headed bird, as the totem creature of the Chu people, was demonised.

claims.quote: In modern China, "nine-headed bird" is a derogatory term for Hubei people, used to mock Hubei people for being "cunning and deceitful."

statement.id: Menurut artikel ini, di Tiongkok modern "burung berkepala sembilan" adalah istilah merendahkan bagi orang Hubei, dipakai untuk mengejek mereka sebagai "licik dan curang".
statement.en: According to the article, in modern China "nine-headed bird" is a derogatory term for Hubei people, used to mock them as "cunning and deceitful".

claims.quote: 【釋名】 鬼鳥（《拾遺》）、九頭鳥（同上）、蒼 （《白澤圖》）、奇 。時珍曰︰鬼車，妖鳥也，取周易載鬼一車之義。

statement.id: Bencao Gangmu mencantumkan nama Guiche (鬼車) sebagai Burung Hantu (鬼鳥) dan Burung Berkepala Sembilan (九頭鳥), dan Li Shizhen menyebut Guiche sebagai burung siluman yang namanya mengambil makna dari Kitab Perubahan.
statement.en: The Bencao Gangmu lists the names of the Guiche (鬼車) as Ghost Bird (鬼鳥) and Nine-headed Bird (九頭鳥), and Li Shizhen calls the Guiche an uncanny bird whose name takes its sense from the Book of Changes.
