statement.en: The author wonders whether the Piguchén might have been the precursor of the Chupacabra.

claims.quote: Tal es por exemplo el Piguchén, quadrúpedo alado, ó especie de gran murciegalo, que á exîstir en la realidad, formaria uno de los eslabones ú anillos que unen los páxaros á los quadrúpedos.

statement.id: Sebuah teks sejarah alam yang didigitalkan menyebut Piguchén sebagai kuadruped bersayap atau sejenis kelelawar besar yang, andai nyata, akan menjadi salah satu mata rantai penghubung burung dan kuadruped.
statement.en: A digitized natural history calls the Piguchén a winged quadruped or kind of large bat which, if it really existed, would be one of the links joining birds to quadrupeds.

claims.quote: Este animal, que segun dicen, es de la magnitud y figura del conejo casero, está cubierto de un pelo fino de color de canela: tiene el hocico aguzado: los ojos grandes, redondos y resplandecientes: las orejas casi invisibles: las alas membranosas: las patas cortas, y semejantes á las del lagarto

statement.id: Menurut teks itu, hewan ini konon sebesar dan berbentuk seperti kelinci rumahan, berbulu halus berwarna kayu manis, berhidung runcing, bermata besar bulat dan berkilau, bertelinga nyaris tak tampak, bersayap selaput, dan berkaki pendek seperti kadal.
statement.en: According to the text, this animal is said to be the size and shape of the domestic rabbit, covered with fine cinnamon-colored hair, with a pointed muzzle, large round shining eyes, almost invisible ears, membranous wings and short legs like a lizard's.

claims.quote: silva como las culebras, y vuela como las perdices: habita en los huecos de los árboles, de donde sale unicamente durante la noche, y no hace mal á nadie sino es á los insectos, que le sirven de pasto.

statement.id: Menurut teks itu, hewan ini bersiul seperti ular, terbang seperti burung perdiz (partridge), tinggal di lubang pohon dan keluar hanya pada malam hari, dan tidak mencelakai siapa pun kecuali serangga yang menjadi makanannya.
statement.en: According to the text, the animal hisses like snakes, flies like partridges (perdiz), lives in tree hollows from which it comes out only at night, and harms no one except the insects that serve as its food.

short_description.id: Tarantasio adalah naga legendaris yang menurut cerita rakyat Lombardia menteror penghuni Danau Gerundo di sekitar Lodi, memakan anak-anak, merusak perahu, dan menebar napas pembawa penyakit.
short_description.en: Tarantasio is a legendary dragon that, in the lore of Lombardy, terrorized the people of Lake Gerundo near Lodi, devouring children, wrecking boats and spreading a disease-bearing breath.

long_description.id: Tarantasio adalah naga legendaris yang menteror penghuni Danau Gerundo kuno dan hipotetis di sekitar Lodi, Lombardia. Menurut legenda rakyat, ia juga dikenal sebagai Tarànto dan terutama memakan anak-anak. Ia dipercaya menghancurkan perahu dan mencemari udara dengan napas pembawa wabah yang menyebabkan penyakit yang disebut febbre gialla.
long_description.en: Tarantasio is a legendary dragon that terrorized the inhabitants of the ancient, hypothetical Lake Gerundo near Lodi in Lombardy. In popular legend he is also known as Tarànto and fed above all on children. He was believed to wreck boats and foul the air with a pestilential breath that caused a disease called febbre gialla.

long_description.id: Banyak legenda bersepakat bahwa pembunuhan naga itu bertepatan dengan pengeringan danau. Satu tradisi menyebut ia lahir dari daging busuk panglima Ezzelino III da Romano. Sebagian sumber rakyat menghubungkan pengeringan danau dengan Santo Kristoforus atau Federico Barbarossa, sedangkan versi yang paling memikat menyebut leluhur keluarga Visconti membunuh naga itu lalu memakai ular besar dengan anak di mulutnya sebagai lambang.
long_description.en: Many legends agree that the dragon's killing coincided with the draining of the lake. One tradition says he was born from the putrefying flesh of the commander Ezzelino III da Romano. Some popular sources link the draining to Saint Christopher or Frederick Barbarossa, while the most evocative version has the progenitor of the Visconti kill the dragon and adopt the biscione with a child in its mouth as an emblem.

long_description.id: Legenda itu sudah dibicarakan pada tahun 1100 oleh biarawan Sabbio dalam memoarnya tentang Lodi, dan sebuah fresko di serambi gereja San Marco di Milan menggambarkan naga itu di latar danau. Sebuah kelurahan di Cassano d'Adda dinamai Taranta merujuk legenda tersebut, dan beberapa gereja konon menyimpan rusuk naga yang oleh naturalis Enrico Caffi diidentifikasi sebagai milik mamut. Dalam budaya populer, pembunuhan tarantasio membuka novel Donna di spade (1991) dan legenda ini disebut mengilhami logo Eni.
long_description.en: The legend is already spoken of in 1100 by the monk Sabbio in his memoirs on Lodi, and a fresco in the cloister of the church of San Marco in Milan shows the dragon against the lake. A hamlet of Cassano d'Adda is named Taranta after the legend, and some churches are said to preserve dragon ribs, one of which the naturalist Enrico Caffi identified as a mammoth's. In popular culture the killing of a tarantasio opens the novel Donna di spade (1991), and the legend is said to have inspired the Eni logo.

statement.id: Rujukan eksplisit pada legenda naga Tarantasio ada dalam sebuah fresko di serambi gereja San Marco di Milan, berasal dari abad ke-13 sampai ke-14, yang menggambarkan hewan mitos itu di latar danau.
statement.en: An explicit reference to the legend of the dragon Tarantasio is found in a fresco in the cloister of the church of San Marco in Milan, datable to the 13th-14th century, showing the mythological animal against the lake.

claims.quote: Una frazione di Cassano d'Adda è denominata Taranta in riferimento alla leggenda.

statement.id: Konon beberapa tulang rusuk naga masih disimpan, antara lain di gereja San Bassiano di Pizzighettone, Cremona; salah satu rusuk itu diteliti naturalis Enrico Caffi pada abad ke-19, yang mengidentifikasinya sebagai milik mamut.
statement.en: Some ribs of the dragon are still preserved, among others at the church of San Bassiano in Pizzighettone, Cremona; one of the ribs was studied by the naturalist Enrico Caffi in the 19th century, who identified it as belonging to a mammoth.

cultural_context.id: Orang Tagalog memperhatikan burung dan makhluk lain yang melintas sebagai pertanda; menurut sebuah teks lama, bertemu burung Tigmamanuguin yang berkicau dapat membuat mereka segera pulang, dan sebelum Kristenisasi tigmamanukan diyakini diutus Bathala sebagai orakel tentang perjalanan.
cultural_context.en: The Tagalogs watched birds and other creatures crossing their path for omens; according to an early text, meeting a singing Tigmamanuguin bird could make them return home at once, and before Christianisation the tigmamanukan was believed sent by Bathala as an oracle about journeys.

short_description.id: Tigmamanukan adalah burung pertanda dalam kepercayaan Tagalog; arah terbang dan kicauannya menjadi pertanda perjalanan, dan sebelum Kristenisasi ia diyakini diutus Bathala.
short_description.en: The tigmamanukan is an omen bird of Tagalog belief; the direction of its flight and its song served as omens for journeys, and before Christianisation it was believed sent by Bathala.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Filipina, orang Tagalog meyakini tigmamanukan sebagai burung pertanda. Di antara burung dan kadal lain yang diamati sebagai pertanda, perhatian khusus diberikan kepadanya. Sebelum Kristenisasi, ia diyakini diutus Bathala, dewa tertinggi dan pencipta, sebagai orakel bagi manusia tentang perlu tidaknya melanjutkan perjalanan.
long_description.en: In Philippine mythology, the Tagalogs believed the tigmamanukan to be an omen bird. Among the other birds and lizards watched for omens, particular attention was paid to it. Before Christianisation it was believed to be sent by Bathala, the supreme deity and creator god, as an oracle to mankind about whether or not to proceed on a journey.

long_description.id: Sebuah teks lama menyebut burung bernama Tigmamanuguin yang berkicau di pohon: bila bertemu burung itu, atau ular, tikus, atau orang yang bersin, orang segera pulang karena menganggapnya pertanda celaka, terutama saat burung itu berkicau. Kicaunya punya dua bentuk, satu dianggap pertanda buruk dan yang lain pertanda baik sehingga perjalanan dilanjutkan.
long_description.en: An early text mentions a bird called Tigmamanuguin singing in a tree: on meeting it, or a serpent, a rat or someone who sneezed, people returned home at once, taking it as an augury of harm, especially when the bird sang. Its song had two forms, one taken as an evil omen and the other as a good omen, after which the journey went on.

long_description.id: Menurut kamus bahasa Tagalog tahun 1613 karya San Buenaventura, bila tigmamanukan terbang melintas ke kanan di awal perjalanan, perjalanan itu akan berhasil; bila ke kiri, para pengembara pasti tidak akan kembali, dan tanda itu disebut labay. Dikatakan pula bahwa pemburu yang menangkap tigmamanukan dalam jerat memotong paruhnya lalu melepaskannya sambil memohon agar burung itu berkicau di kanan.
long_description.en: According to San Buenaventura's 1613 Dictionary of the Tagalog Language, if a tigmamanukan flew across the path to the right at the start of a journey the expedition would succeed, and if it flew to the left the travelers would surely never return; the sign was called labay. It was also said that a hunter who trapped a tigmamanukan cut its beak and released it, asking it to sing on the right.

long_description.id: Dalam sedikitnya satu versi mitos penciptaan, Tigmamanukan membuka bambu tempat laki-laki pertama, Malakas, dan perempuan pertama, Maganda, keluar; dikatakan ia dinamai Manaul oleh Bathala, sedangkan sumber lain menyebut wujud burung Amihan yang mematuk bambu. Sebagian penjelajah Barat awal mengira burung ini burung biru peri (genus Irena), dan kebanyakan sumber sepakat bahwa ia berwarna biru; di Filipina kuno banyak burung pertanda lain juga berbulu biru.
long_description.en: In at least one telling of the creation myth, the Tigmamanukan opened the bamboo from which the first man, Malakas, and first woman, Maganda, emerged; it is said to have been named Manaul by Bathala, while other sources say it was Amihan's bird form that pecked the bamboo. Some early Western explorers took the bird to be a fairy bluebird (genus Irena), and most sources agree it was blue; many other omen birds of ancient Philippines were also blue-plumaged.

claims.quote: In Philippine mythology, the Tigmamanukan was believed by the Tagalog people to be an omen or augural bird. Although numerous other birds and lizards were observed for possible omens, particular attention was paid to the tigmamanukan. Before Christianisation, the Tagalogs believed the tigmamanukan was sent by the supreme deity and creator god Bathala

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Filipina, orang Tagalog meyakini tigmamanukan sebagai burung pertanda; di antara burung dan kadal lain yang diamati sebagai pertanda, perhatian khusus diberikan kepadanya, dan sebelum Kristenisasi ia diyakini diutus Bathala, dewa tertinggi dan pencipta.
statement.en: In Philippine mythology, the Tagalog believed the tigmamanukan was an omen or augural bird; among the other birds and lizards watched for omens, particular attention was paid to it, and before Christianisation it was believed sent by Bathala, the supreme deity and creator god.

claims.quote: The root of the word tigmamanukan is manók (from Proto-Austronesian *manuk), which in modern Filipino is exclusively used for the chicken (Gallus gallus domesticus).

statement.id: Akar kata tigmamanukan adalah manók (dari Proto-Austronesia *manuk), yang dalam bahasa Filipino modern hanya dipakai untuk ayam (Gallus gallus domesticus).
statement.en: The root of the word tigmamanukan is manók (from Proto-Austronesian *manuk), which in modern Filipino is used exclusively for the chicken (Gallus gallus domesticus).

claims.quote: According to San Buenaventura's 1613 Dictionary of the Tagalog Language ... the Tagalogs believed that the direction of a tigmamanukan flying across one's path at the beginning a journey indicated the undertaking's result. If it flew to the right, the expedition would be a success.

statement.id: Menurut Dictionary of the Tagalog Language karya San Buenaventura tahun 1613, orang Tagalog percaya arah terbang tigmamanukan yang melintas di awal perjalanan menandakan hasilnya; bila terbang ke kanan, perjalanan akan berhasil.
statement.en: According to San Buenaventura's 1613 Dictionary of the Tagalog Language, the Tagalogs believed that the direction of a tigmamanukan flying across one's path at the start of a journey indicated its result; if it flew to the right, the expedition would succeed.

claims.quote: some early western explorers say that the specific bird referred to by the name is a fairy bluebird (genus Irena and family Irenidae).

statement.en: Some early Western explorers say the bird referred to by the name is a fairy bluebird (genus Irena, family Irenidae).

claims.quote: It is said that the specific tigmamanukan that pecked the bamboo was named by Bathala as Manaul

statement.id: Dikatakan bahwa tigmamanukan tertentu yang mematuk bambu itu dinamai Manaul oleh Bathala.
statement.en: It is said that the particular tigmamanukan that pecked the bamboo was named Manaul by Bathala.

claims.quote: if they left their house and met on the way a serpent or rat, or a bird called Tigmamanuguin which was singing in the tree, or if they chanced upon anyone who sneezed, they returned at once to their house, considering the incident as an augury that some evil might befall them if they should continue their journey—especially when the above-mentioned bird sang.

statement.id: Menurut teks ini, bila di jalan mereka bertemu ular, tikus, atau burung bernama Tigmamanuguin yang berkicau di pohon, atau bertemu orang yang bersin, mereka segera pulang karena menganggapnya pertanda bahwa celaka dapat menimpa jika perjalanan dilanjutkan, terutama bila burung itu berkicau.
statement.en: According to this text, if on leaving home they met a serpent or rat, a bird called Tigmamanuguin singing in a tree, or someone who sneezed, they returned home at once, taking it as an augury that evil might befall them if they continued, especially when the bird sang.

claims.quote: especially when the above-mentioned bird sang. This song had two different forms: in the one case it was considered as an evil omen; in the other, as a good omen, and then they continued their journey.

statement.id: Menurut teks ini, kicau burung itu punya dua bentuk: yang satu dianggap pertanda buruk, yang lain pertanda baik, dan dalam hal kedua mereka melanjutkan perjalanan.
statement.en: According to this text, the bird's song had two forms: one was taken as an evil omen and the other as a good omen, in which case they continued their journey.

claims.quote: no one would go to heaven, where there dwelt only Bathala, "the maker of all things," who governed from above.

statement.id: Menurut teks ini, di surga hanya tinggal Bathala, "pencipta segala sesuatu", yang memerintah dari atas.
statement.en: According to this text, only Bathala, "the maker of all things," dwelt in heaven and governed from above.

claims.quote: The Tagalos adored a blue bird, as large as a thrush, and called it Bathala, which was among them a term of divinity.

statement.id: Menurut teks ini, orang Tagalos (ejaan teks itu) memuja seekor burung biru sebesar thrush dan menyebutnya Bathala, istilah ilahi di kalangan mereka.
statement.en: According to this text, the Tagalos (as the text spells the name) adored a blue bird as large as a thrush and called it Bathala, a term of divinity among them.

claims.quote: Tigmamanukin. A bird, also called tigmamanok, whose songs serve as an omen to the Tagalogs. Its scientific name is Jrena cyanogastra (according to Doctor A. B. Meyer).

statement.id: The Aswang Project mendaftar tigmamanukin, juga disebut tigmamanok, sebagai burung yang kicauannya menjadi pertanda bagi orang Tagalog; nama ilmiahnya ditulis Jrena cyanogastra (menurut Doctor A. B. Meyer).
statement.en: The Aswang Project lists tigmamanukin, also called tigmamanok, as a bird whose songs serve as an omen to the Tagalogs, giving its scientific name as Jrena cyanogastra (according to Doctor A. B. Meyer).

claims.quote: Limokon or Limukun. It is the Bagobo and Mandaya (Mindanao) name of the wild dove Phabotreron brevirostris whose song serves as an omen.

statement.id: Limokon atau Limukun adalah nama dalam bahasa Bagobo dan Mandaya (Mindanao) untuk merpati liar Phabotreron brevirostris yang kicauannya menjadi pertanda.
statement.en: Limokon or Limukun is the Bagobo and Mandaya (Mindanao) name of the wild dove Phabotreron brevirostris, whose song serves as an omen.

claims.quote: Before Christianisation, the Tagalogs believed the tigmamanukan was sent by the supreme deity and creator god Bathala as an oracle to mankind concerning whether or not they should proceed on a journey.

statement.id: Sebelum Kristenisasi, orang Tagalog percaya tigmamanukan diutus Bathala, dewa tertinggi dan pencipta, sebagai orakel bagi manusia tentang perlu tidaknya melanjutkan perjalanan.
statement.en: Before Christianisation, the Tagalogs believed the tigmamanukan was sent by Bathala, the supreme deity and creator god, as an oracle to mankind about whether or not to proceed on a journey.

claims.quote: In some Philippine creation myths, the tigmamanukan bird was sent by Bathala to split open the primordial bamboo whence the first man and woman came out.

statement.id: Dalam beberapa mitos penciptaan Filipina, burung tigmamanukan diutus Bathala untuk membelah bambu purba tempat laki-laki dan perempuan pertama keluar.
statement.en: In some Philippine creation myths, the tigmamanukan bird was sent by Bathala to split open the primordial bamboo from which the first man and woman came out.

claims.quote: Before Christianisation, as documented by Spanish accounts early in the colonial period, the word tigmamanukan was widely used for "any bird, lizard or snake that crossed one's path as an omen". Such encounters were called salúbong ("meeting", "encounter").

statement.id: Sebelum Kristenisasi, menurut catatan Spanyol awal masa kolonial, kata tigmamanukan banyak dipakai untuk "setiap burung, kadal, atau ular yang melintas di jalan seseorang sebagai pertanda"; pertemuan semacam itu disebut salúbong ("pertemuan").
statement.en: Before Christianisation, as documented by Spanish accounts early in the colonial period, the word tigmamanukan was widely used for "any bird, lizard or snake that crossed one's path as an omen"; such encounters were called salúbong ("meeting", "encounter").

claims.quote: The term most likely evolved from divination practises, i.e., reading omens following the ritual sacrifice of chickens and sometimes other animals like pigs.

statement.id: Istilah ini kemungkinan besar berkembang dari praktik ramalan, yaitu membaca pertanda setelah pengorbanan ritual ayam dan kadang hewan lain seperti babi.
statement.en: The term most likely evolved from divination practices, that is, reading omens after the ritual sacrifice of chickens and sometimes other animals such as pigs.

claims.quote: This sign was called "labay", a term still present in some Filipino languages with the meaning "proceed". If the bird flew to the left, the travelers would surely never return.

statement.id: Tanda itu disebut "labay", istilah yang masih ada di beberapa bahasa Filipina dengan arti "melanjutkan". Bila burung terbang ke kiri, para pengembara pasti tidak akan kembali.
statement.en: The sign was called "labay", a term still present in some Filipino languages meaning "proceed". If the bird flew to the left, the travelers would surely never return.

claims.quote: In any case, most of the sources which describe the tigmamanukan agree that it is distinguished by a "blue" color.

statement.id: Kebanyakan sumber yang menggambarkan tigmamanukan sepakat bahwa burung ini dicirikan oleh warna "biru".
statement.en: Most of the sources that describe the tigmamanukan agree that it is distinguished by a "blue" color.

claims.quote: In at least one telling of the Filipino creation myth, the Tigmamanukan was responsible for opening the bamboo from which emerged the first man, Malakas, and first woman, Maganda.

statement.id: Dalam sedikitnya satu versi mitos penciptaan Filipina, Tigmamanukan bertugas membuka bambu tempat keluar laki-laki pertama, Malakas, dan perempuan pertama, Maganda.
statement.en: In at least one telling of the Filipino creation myth, the Tigmamanukan was responsible for opening the bamboo from which the first man, Malakas, and first woman, Maganda, emerged.

claims.quote: however, in other sources, it was the bird form of Amihan, the deity of peace and wind, that pecked the bamboo. Some sources also state that Amihan's bird form is Manaul.

statement.id: Namun dalam sumber lain, yang mematuk bambu adalah wujud burung Amihan, dewi kedamaian dan angin; sebagian sumber juga menyebut wujud burung Amihan adalah Manaul.
statement.en: However, in other sources it was the bird form of Amihan, the deity of peace and wind, that pecked the bamboo; some sources also state that Amihan's bird form is Manaul.

claims.quote: It was also said that if a hunter caught a tigmamanukan in a trap, they would cut its beak and release it, saying "Kita ay iwawala, kung ako'y mey kakaunan, lalabay ka." ("You are free, so when I set forth, sing on the right.")

statement.id: Dikatakan pula bahwa bila pemburu menangkap tigmamanukan dalam jerat, ia memotong paruhnya lalu melepaskannya sambil berkata "Kita ay iwawala, kung ako'y mey kakaunan, lalabay ka" ("Kau bebas, maka saat aku berangkat, berkicaulah di sebelah kanan").
statement.en: It was also said that if a hunter caught a tigmamanukan in a trap, they would cut its beak and release it, saying "Kita ay iwawala, kung ako'y mey kakaunan, lalabay ka" ("You are free, so when I set forth, sing on the right").

claims.quote: Another kingfisher species was also called tigmamanukan. These birds were considered taboo to kill.

statement.id: Satu jenis raja udang lain juga disebut tigmamanukan; burung-burung ini dianggap tabu untuk dibunuh.
statement.en: Another kingfisher species was also called tigmamanukan; these birds were considered taboo to kill.

claims.quote: The Tagálogs worshiped a blue bird as large as a turtle-dove, which they called tigmamanuquin, to which they attributed the name of Bathala, which, as above stated, was among them a name for divinity.

statement.id: Dalam kutipan sebuah catatan sejarah, orang Tagalog memuja burung biru sebesar tekukur yang mereka sebut tigmamanuquin, yang dinamai Bathala, nama bagi keilahian di kalangan mereka.
statement.en: In a quoted historical account, the Tagalogs worshiped a blue bird as large as a turtle-dove, which they called tigmamanuquin, to which they attributed the name of Bathala, a name for divinity among them.

claims.quote: There were myriads of species considered "omen birds" in ancient Philippines. Many of them share a characteristic: blue plumage.
claims.locator: Other omen birds of the Philippine archipelago

statement.id: Di Filipina kuno ada sangat banyak jenis burung yang dianggap burung pertanda, dan banyak di antaranya memiliki ciri yang sama, yaitu bulu biru.
statement.en: There were myriads of species considered omen birds in ancient Philippines, and many of them share a characteristic: blue plumage.

text.id: Dicatat sebagai patianac oleh Juan de Plasencia pada 1589.
text.en: Recorded as the patianac by Juan de Plasencia in 1589.

cultural_context.id: Menurut sebuah artikel tentang makhluk ini, kisah-kisah tiyanak merekam kenyataan sosial seputar kelahiran dan masa kanak-kanak: kehamilan dan persalinan berbahaya, kematian bayi lazim, dan tangisan tak dikenal menuntut tanggapan moral, sehingga belas kasih menjadi perangkapnya.
cultural_context.en: According to an article on the creature, tiyanak stories preserve the social realities of birth and childhood: pregnancy and labour were dangerous, infant mortality was common and an unexplained cry demanded a moral response.

who.id: Makhluk pengisap darah yang menyamar sebagai bayi.
who.en: A vampiric creature that disguises itself as a baby.

origin.id: Mitologi Filipina.
origin.en: Philippine mythology.

role.id: Pemikat dan penyesat pejalan di hutan.
role.en: A lurer and misleader of travellers in the jungle.

famous_for.id: Tangisan bayi yang memikat korban.
famous_for.en: The baby's cry that lures victims.

did_you_know.id: Catatan tertua, dari 1589, tentang patianac tidak menggambarkan bayi pemikat, melainkan perempuan dan anak yang mati saat melahirkan dan terdengar meratap pada malam hari.
did_you_know.en: The oldest record, from 1589, of the patianac does not describe a baby lure but a woman and child who died in childbirth and were heard lamenting at night.

description.id: Menjelma bayi dan kembali ke wujud aslinya saat diangkat; meniru tangisan bayi untuk memikat korban; dalam satu catatan tubuh bayi berubah menjadi kakek kecil, dan dalam legenda Mindoro berubah menjadi burung hitam.
description.en: Takes a baby's form and reverts to its true form when picked up; imitates an infant's cries to lure victims; in one account a baby's body turns into a small old man, and in a Mindoro legend it turns into a black bird.

description.id: Dalam beberapa cerita tiyanak terlihat terbang di hutan atau terbang pergi sesudah menyerang korbannya.
description.en: In some stories the tiyanak is seen flying through the forest or flying away after attacking its victim.

description.id: Makhluk semacam ini dikatakan dapat menjadi terlihat atau tak terlihat.
description.en: Such beings were said to become visible or invisible.

description.id: Membalik pakaian mematahkan pesona atau daya tipunya.
description.en: Turning clothes inside out breaks its enchantment or power of deception.

description.en: Small nut-brown people floating in the air; in the Kapampangan story a crowd of them appeared on Mount Arayat.

summary.id: Sepasang suami istri menemukan bayi di hutan dan membawanya; bayi itu menempel pada dada sang istri dan menggigitnya, sang istri ditemukan mati, dan bayi itu terlihat terbang pergi di antara pepohonan.
summary.en: A couple find an infant in the forest and carry it with them; it fastens onto the wife's breast and bites her, she is found dead, and the infant is seen flying away among the trees.

role.id: Bayi menyerupai anak yang telah dikubur.
role.en: An infant resembling the buried child.

summary.id: Seorang bayi menyusu tanpa henti pada seorang ibu sampai ibu itu meninggal; sesudahnya bayi itu berubah menjadi burung hitam dan terbang dari rumah.
summary.en: An infant feeds without stopping at a mother's breast until she dies, after which it changes into a black bird and flies from the house.

role.id: Anak penggoda yang membawa Bata pergi.
role.en: A child who leads Bata away.

summary.id: Kisah ini ditutup dengan penjelasan bahwa tianac adalah anak yang meninggal tanpa dibaptis, yang berkeliaran di tempat sunyi dan menyesatkan anak muda; membalik pakaian disebut sebagai penangkalnya.
summary.en: The tale ends by identifying the tianac as a child who died unbaptized, said to roam lonely places and mislead the young; turning one's clothing inside out is named as the way to break its deception.

title.en: Vicente Meets a Crowd of Tianac (Kapampangan)

role.id: Kerumunan makhluk kecil yang menyesatkan seorang lelaki di gunung.
role.en: A crowd of small beings that mislead a man on a mountain.

summary.id: Vicente bertemu banyak tianac di Gunung Arayat; ia lenyapkan mereka dengan membalik pakaiannya, dan baru kemudian mengetahui bahwa hari sudah Senin padahal ia mengira hanya terlambat satu jam.
summary.en: Vicente meets many tianac on Mount Arayat; he makes them vanish by turning his clothes inside out and only afterwards learns that it is Monday although he believed he was merely an hour late.

role.id: Makhluk yang diduga membawa pergi seorang penjaga kolam.

summary.en: Villagers suspect the tianak have taken an elderly fishpond watchman and search for him while striking tin cans continuously so the beings will release him.

description.id: Tiyanak menjadi subjek banyak film Filipina, di antaranya Tianak (1953) dan Tiyanak (1988).

traditional.id: Catatan tertua tentang patianac menyangkut perempuan dan anak yang mati saat melahirkan, bukan bayi pemikat.
traditional.en: The oldest record of the patianac concerns a woman and child who died in childbirth, not a baby lure.

modern.id: Penulis dan seniman modern menafsirkan ulang tiyanak; satu penafsiran membacanya sebagai bayi yang berusaha memahami dunia kejam ciptaan orang dewasa.
modern.en: Modern writers and artists reinterpret the tiyanak; one reading approaches it as a newborn trying to understand a violent world created by adults.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa kepercayaan tentang tiyanak berubah setelah datangnya agama Katolik?
learning_questions.en: Why did beliefs about the tiyanak change after Catholicism arrived?

learning_questions.id: Mengapa tangisan bayi menjadi perangkap yang efektif dalam cerita ini?
learning_questions.en: Why does a baby's cry make such an effective trap in these stories?

summary.en: In the Catholic version it is the soul of an infant who died before baptism, and today also an aborted fetus.

short_description.id: Tiyanak adalah makhluk pengisap darah dalam mitologi Filipina yang menyamar sebagai bayi dan menangis di hutan untuk memikat pejalan, lalu kembali ke wujud aslinya dan menyerang.
short_description.en: The tiyanak is a vampiric creature of Philippine mythology that takes the form of a baby and cries in the jungle to lure travellers, then reverts to its true form and attacks.

long_description.id: Tiyanak, juga ditulis tianak atau tianac, adalah makhluk pengisap darah dalam mitologi Filipina yang berwujud balita atau bayi. Ia biasanya menjelma bayi baru lahir yang menangis di hutan untuk memikat pejalan; begitu diangkat, ia kembali ke wujud aslinya dan menyerang korbannya. Tiyanak juga digambarkan senang secara jahat menyesatkan pejalan atau menculik anak-anak, dan berbagai legenda sepakat bahwa ia mampu meniru bayi.
long_description.en: The tiyanak, also written tianak or tianac, is a vampiric being of Philippine mythology that appears as a toddler or baby. It usually appears as a newborn crying in the jungle to attract travellers; once picked up, it reverts to its true form and attacks the victim. It is also depicted as taking malevolent delight in leading travellers astray or abducting children, and different legends agree on its ability to mimic an infant.

long_description.id: Catatan tertulis tertua berasal dari Fr. Juan de Plasencia (1589), yang menulis tentang patianac: perempuan yang mati saat melahirkan dihukum bersama anaknya dan ratapannya terdengar pada malam hari. Uraian itu tidak menggambarkan bayi pemikat yang dikenal sekarang, dan ia menyatakan bahwa di antara semua orang Tagalog tidak ada lagi jejak kepercayaan semacam itu. Sebuah kumpulan cerita rakyat menjelaskan patianac sebagai roh kelahiran yang jahil, tinggal di hutan dan ladang, dan menyesatkan pejalan pada malam hari. Dalam catatan Cronicas karya Francisco de San Antonio (1738–44) dan Estadismo karya Martinez de Zuniga (1803), para pria menanggalkan pakaian dan, menurut yang terakhir, mengayunkan pedang agar patianac menjauh dari perempuan yang bersalin.
long_description.en: The oldest written record comes from Fr. Juan de Plasencia (1589), who wrote of the patianac: a woman who died in childbirth was punished together with her child and heard lamenting at night. That description does not present the familiar baby lure, and he states that among all the Tagalogs not a trace of such beliefs is left. A folklore collection explains the patianac as playful spirits of birth that dwell in woods and fields and mislead travellers by night. In San Antonio's Cronicas (1738–44) and Martinez de Zuniga's Estadismo (1803), men undress and, according to the latter, flourish a sword to keep the patianac away from a woman in labour.

long_description.id: Wujudnya berbeda menurut tempat. Dalam satu versi ia tetap berbentuk bayi tetapi menumbuhkan cakar dan taring tajam; dalam versi lain wujud sejatinya kakek kecil berkulit keriput, berjanggut dan berkumis panjang, berhidung pesek, dengan mata sebesar koin peseta. Di Pampanga tiyanak digambarkan sebagai orang kecil berkulit cokelat kacang yang melayang di udara; di pulau Mindoro ia berubah menjadi burung hitam; dan di Batangas ia digambarkan sebagai bayi biasa yang tersesat di alam liar. Menurut sebuah artikel tentang makhluk ini, rincian dari banyak tempat kadang tumpang tindih tetapi tidak membentuk satu anatomi baku. Dalam satu catatan, kakek kecil itu berkaki pincang, satu kakinya jauh lebih pendek, sehingga bergerak dengan lompatan mendadak.
long_description.en: Its form varies by place. In one version it keeps a baby's shape but grows sharp claws and fangs; in another its true form is a little old man with wrinkled skin, a long beard and moustache, a flat nose and eyes the size of peseta coins. In Pampanga the tiyanak appear as small people with nut-brown skin who hover instead of walking; on the island of Mindoro it turns into a black bird; and in Batangas it is described as regular babies lost in the wild. According to an article on the creature, details from many places sometimes overlap but do not form a single fixed anatomy. In one account the small old man had one leg much shorter than the other and moved in abrupt leaps.

long_description.id: Orang Mandaya di Mindanao memandang tiyanak sebagai arwah anak yang ibunya meninggal sebelum melahirkan; makhluk gaib serupa dalam cerita rakyat Melayu adalah pontianak. Dengan penjajahan Filipina oleh Spanyol pada abad ke-16, mitos tiyanak dipadukan dengan Katolik dan tiyanak dianggap arwah bayi yang meninggal sebelum dibaptis; di Filipina masa kini pengertian itu meluas hingga mencakup janin yang digugurkan yang kembali untuk membalas dendam.
long_description.en: The Mandaya of Mindanao regard the tiyanak as the spirit of a child whose mother died before giving birth; the Pontianak of Malay folklore is a similar supernatural creature. Following the Spanish colonization of the Philippines in the 16th century, the myth became part of Catholicism and tiyanak came to be seen as the souls of infants who died before baptism; in modern-day Philippines the definition has extended to aborted fetuses that returned to seek revenge.

long_description.id: Dalam kepercayaan setempat ada beberapa penangkal. Orang yang tersesat karena tangisan makhluk itu dipercaya dapat mematahkan pesonanya dengan membalik pakaian; suara keras seperti perayaan Tahun Baru dianggap mengusirnya; dan menurut Jose A. Samson, albularyo di pedesaan Luzon percaya bahwa memainkan gitar dapat menangkalnya. Dalam satu kisah, warga kampung memukul kaleng timah terus-menerus agar makhluk-makhluk itu melepaskan seorang penjaga kolam ikan yang hilang.
long_description.en: Local belief offers several countermeasures. Those led astray by the creature's cries are believed able to break the enchantment by turning their clothes inside out; loud noises such as a New Year's celebration are thought to drive it away; and according to Jose A. Samson, albularyos in rural Luzon believe that playing the guitar wards it off. In one story villagers struck tin cans continuously so that the beings would release a missing fishpond watchman.

claims.quote: is a vampiric creature in Philippine mythology that takes on the form of a toddler or baby. Although there are various types, it typically takes the form of a newborn baby and cries in the jungle to attract unwary travelers. Once it is picked up by an unfortunate passerby, it reverts to its true form and attacks the victim.

statement.id: Tiyanak adalah makhluk pengisap darah dalam mitologi Filipina yang berwujud balita atau bayi, biasanya bayi baru lahir yang menangis di hutan untuk memikat pejalan; begitu diangkat ia kembali ke wujud asli dan menyerang korbannya.
statement.en: The tiyanak is a vampiric creature of Philippine mythology in the form of a toddler or baby, usually a newborn crying in the jungle to attract travellers; once picked up it reverts to its true form and attacks the victim.

claims.quote: They had another deception—namely, that if any woman died in childbirth, she and the child suffered punishment; and that, at night, she could be heard lamenting. This was called patianac.

statement.id: Plasencia mencatat kepercayaan bahwa perempuan yang mati saat melahirkan dihukum bersama anaknya dan ratapannya terdengar di malam hari; ini disebut patianac.
statement.en: Plasencia recorded the belief that a woman who died in childbirth was punished with her child and heard lamenting at night; this was called patianac.

claims.quote: To counteract the malignity of this spirit, the husband, fastening the door, reduces himself to a state of complete nudity, lights a fire, and arming himself with his sword, continues to flourish it furiously, until the woman is delivered. ... Fr. Martinez de Zuniga, Estadismo (1803)

statement.id: Menurut Estadismo karya Martinez de Zuniga (1803), untuk melawan roh patianac sang suami mengunci pintu, menanggalkan seluruh pakaian, menyalakan api, dan mengayunkan pedang dengan garang sampai istrinya selesai bersalin.
statement.en: According to Martinez de Zuniga, Estadismo (1803), to counteract the patianac spirit the husband fastened the door, stripped completely naked, lit a fire and flourished his sword furiously until the woman was delivered.

claims.quote: In one version, it retains the general shape of a baby but then forms sharp claws and fangs to attack its victim.

statement.id: Dalam satu versi tiyanak tetap berbentuk umum seperti bayi tetapi menumbuhkan cakar dan taring tajam untuk menyerang korbannya.
statement.en: In one version the tiyanak retains the general shape of a baby but forms sharp claws and fangs to attack its victim.

claims.quote: In another version from Central Luzon, especially in Pampanga, the tiyanak are described as small, nut-brown people who don't walk on the ground but rather float on air.

statement.id: Dalam versi dari Luzon Tengah, terutama Pampanga, tiyanak digambarkan sebagai orang kecil berkulit cokelat kacang yang tidak berjalan di tanah melainkan melayang di udara.
statement.en: In a version from Central Luzon, especially Pampanga, the tiyanak are described as small, nut-brown people who do not walk on the ground but float on air.

claims.quote: The Mandaya people of Mindanao claim that the tiyanak is the spirit of a child whose mother died before giving birth.

statement.id: Orang Mandaya di Mindanao menyatakan bahwa tiyanak adalah arwah anak yang ibunya meninggal sebelum melahirkan.
statement.en: The Mandaya people of Mindanao claim that the tiyanak is the spirit of a child whose mother died before giving birth.

claims.quote: With the Spanish colonization of the Philippines in the 16th century, the tiyanak myth was integrated into Catholicism. The tiyanak in the Catholic version were supposedly the souls of infants that died before being baptized.

statement.id: Dengan penjajahan Filipina oleh Spanyol pada abad ke-16, mitos tiyanak dipadukan dengan Katolik; dalam versi Katolik tiyanak dianggap arwah bayi yang meninggal sebelum dibaptis.
statement.en: With the Spanish colonization of the Philippines in the 16th century the tiyanak myth was integrated into Catholicism; in the Catholic version tiyanak were supposedly the souls of infants who died before being baptized.

statement.en: According to Jose A. Samson, a common belief among albularyos in rural Luzon for warding off the tiyanak is to play the guitar.

claims.quote: The tiyanak is the subject of many Philippine films: Tianak (1953) Tiyanak (1988)

statement.id: Tiyanak menjadi subjek banyak film Filipina, di antaranya Tianak (1953) dan Tiyanak (1988).
statement.en: The tiyanak is the subject of many Philippine films, among them Tianak (1953) and Tiyanak (1988).

claims.quote: When a woman is about to give birth, some men undress until they are stark naked. ... They say that it is to keep the patiànac and the osuàng away from the woman. These are witches among them who come to obstruct the success of the childbirth, and to suck out the souls of children ... Fr. Francisco de San Antonio, Cronicas (1738–44)

statement.id: Menurut Cronicas karya Francisco de San Antonio (1738–44), ketika seorang perempuan hendak melahirkan, sejumlah pria menanggalkan pakaian; mereka mengatakan itu untuk menjauhkan patianac dan osuang, penyihir yang datang menghalangi kelancaran persalinan dan menyedot jiwa anak-anak.
statement.en: According to Cronicas by Francisco de San Antonio (1738–44), when a woman is about to give birth some men undress completely; they say this is to keep the patianac and the osuang away, witches who come to obstruct the childbirth and suck out the souls of children.

claims.quote: In 1589, the Franciscan missionary Juan de Plasencia included the patianac among beings feared by Tagalog communities. His short description does not present the familiar monster disguised as an abandoned baby. Instead, it concerns a woman and child who die during childbirth and are said to be heard lamenting at night.
claims.locator: A Belief with More Than One History

statement.id: Pada 1589 misionaris Fransiskan Juan de Plasencia memasukkan patianac di antara makhluk yang ditakuti komunitas Tagalog. Uraiannya tidak menggambarkan monster bayi terlantar yang dikenal sekarang, melainkan seorang perempuan dan anaknya yang mati saat melahirkan dan konon terdengar meratap pada malam hari.
statement.en: In 1589 the Franciscan missionary Juan de Plasencia included the patianac among beings feared by Tagalog communities. His description does not present the familiar monster disguised as an abandoned baby but concerns a woman and child who die in childbirth and are said to be heard lamenting at night.

claims.quote: Accounts from Malolos, Malabon, Batangas, Mindoro, Pampanga, and other places describe deceptive crying, altered sight, lost time, a child on a banana leaf, uneven legs, claws, or a sudden transformation. These details sometimes overlap, but they do not form a single fixed anatomy.

statement.id: Catatan dari Malolos, Malabon, Batangas, Mindoro, Pampanga, dan tempat lain menggambarkan tangisan yang menipu, penglihatan yang berubah, waktu yang hilang, anak di atas daun pisang, kaki tak sama panjang, cakar, atau perubahan mendadak. Rincian itu kadang tumpang tindih tetapi tidak membentuk satu anatomi baku.
statement.en: Accounts from Malolos, Malabon, Batangas, Mindoro, Pampanga and other places describe deceptive crying, altered sight, lost time, a child on a banana leaf, uneven legs, claws or a sudden transformation. These details sometimes overlap but do not form a single fixed anatomy.

claims.quote: two boys found what appeared to be a naked, unusually plump newborn lying on the side of a banana leaf. ... The child changed while they fondled it. The round infant body became that of a small old man.
claims.locator: The Infant on the Banana Leaf

statement.id: Dalam satu catatan, dua anak lelaki menemukan sesuatu yang tampak seperti bayi baru lahir yang telanjang dan montok di atas daun pisang; saat mereka mengelusnya, tubuh bulat bayi itu berubah menjadi tubuh seorang kakek kecil.
statement.en: In one account two boys found what appeared to be a naked, unusually plump newborn lying on a banana leaf; while they fondled it the round infant body became that of a small old man.

claims.quote: One leg was much shorter than the other, so the being could not move with an ordinary human stride. It travelled in abrupt leaps.
claims.locator: The Infant on the Banana Leaf

statement.id: Dalam catatan yang sama, satu kaki makhluk itu jauh lebih pendek daripada yang lain sehingga ia tidak dapat melangkah seperti manusia biasa dan bergerak dengan lompatan mendadak.
statement.en: In the same account one leg of the being was much shorter than the other, so it could not move with an ordinary human stride and travelled in abrupt leaps.

claims.quote: People in the barrio suspected that the tianak had taken him. They did not search quietly. The party carried tin cans and struck them continuously, hoping that a tremendous racket would frighten the beings and force them to release their victim.

statement.id: Dalam satu kisah, warga kampung menduga tianak telah membawa seorang penjaga kolam ikan yang tua; rombongan pencari memukul kaleng timah terus-menerus dengan harapan kegaduhan itu menakuti makhluk-makhluk tersebut dan memaksa mereka melepaskan korbannya.
statement.en: In one story villagers of a barrio suspected that the tianak had taken an elderly fishpond watchman; the search party struck tin cans continuously, hoping the racket would frighten the beings and force them to release their victim.

claims.quote: The Tianak — Tagalog ... The wife held it to her breast even though she had not yet borne a child and had no milk to give. The infant fastened onto her. A moment later she cried out that it had bitten her. ... She was dead. The infant was no longer beside her. Looking into the forest, he saw it flying away among the trees.

statement.id: Dalam kisah Tagalog tentang sepasang suami istri, bayi yang mereka temukan di hutan menempel pada dada sang istri dan menggigitnya; sang istri kemudian ditemukan mati, dan suaminya melihat bayi itu terbang pergi di antara pepohonan.
statement.en: In a Tagalog tale of a young couple, the infant they found in the forest fastened onto the wife’s breast and bit her; she was later found dead and her husband saw the infant flying away among the trees.

claims.quote: The Patianak — Tagalog, Oriental Mindoro ... The baby would not stop feeding. It remained fixed at her breast while her strength drained away. She became weaker and weaker until she died. Once she was dead, the infant changed into a black bird and flew from the house.

statement.id: Dalam kisah patianak dari Mindoro Oriental, bayi yang disusui seorang ibu tidak berhenti menyusu sementara tenaga sang ibu terkuras sampai ia meninggal; setelah itu bayi tersebut berubah menjadi burung hitam dan terbang dari rumah.
statement.en: In the patianak story from Oriental Mindoro, the baby a mother nursed would not stop feeding while her strength drained until she died; the infant then changed into a black bird and flew from the house.

claims.quote: Bata and the Tianac — Tagalog ... The story closes by explaining the Tianac as a child who died without baptism. Such beings were said to wander lonely places, become visible or invisible, and mislead young people. Turning one’s clothing inside out was given as a way to break their power of deception.

statement.id: Kisah Tagalog tentang Bata menjelaskan tianac sebagai anak yang meninggal tanpa dibaptis; makhluk semacam itu dikatakan berkeliaran di tempat sunyi, dapat menampakkan diri atau tidak terlihat, dan menyesatkan anak muda. Membalik pakaian disebut sebagai cara mematahkan daya tipunya.
statement.en: The Tagalog story of Bata explains the Tianac as a child who died without baptism; such beings were said to wander lonely places, become visible or invisible and mislead young people, and turning one’s clothing inside out was given as a way to break their power of deception.

claims.quote: Vicente Meets a Crowd of Tianac — Kapampangan ... Small beings appeared around him. They were nut-brown and some floated in the air. They had large noses, wide mouths, and fierce eyes.
claims.locator: Vicente Meets a Crowd of Tianac — Kapampangan

statement.id: Dalam kisah Kapampangan, makhluk-makhluk kecil berkulit cokelat kacang muncul mengelilingi seorang lelaki; sebagian melayang di udara, berhidung besar, bermulut lebar, dan bermata garang.
statement.en: In the Kapampangan story small nut-brown beings appeared around a man; some floated in the air and they had large noses, wide mouths and fierce eyes.

claims.quote: Vicente Meets a Crowd of Tianac — Kapampangan ... An elderly servant told the narrator that Vicente had once encountered many tianac on Mount Arayat.
claims.locator: Vicente Meets a Crowd of Tianac — Kapampangan

statement.id: Menurut kisah Kapampangan, seorang lelaki bernama Vicente pernah bertemu banyak tianac di Gunung Arayat.
statement.en: In the Kapampangan story, a man named Vicente once encountered many tianac on Mount Arayat.

claims.quote: Vicente Meets a Crowd of Tianac — Kapampangan ... He removed his clothes, turned them inside out, and put them on again. The crowd vanished immediately.
claims.locator: Vicente Meets a Crowd of Tianac — Kapampangan

statement.id: Dalam kisah itu, sang lelaki melepas pakaiannya, membaliknya, lalu memakainya lagi, dan kerumunan makhluk itu langsung lenyap.
statement.en: In the story the man removed his clothes, turned them inside out and put them on again, and the crowd vanished immediately.

claims.quote: Vicente Meets a Crowd of Tianac — Kapampangan ... Only then did he learn that it was Monday. Vicente had entered the mountain on Saturday and believed that he was merely an hour late for the meeting.
claims.locator: Vicente Meets a Crowd of Tianac — Kapampangan

statement.id: Dalam kisah yang sama, Vicente baru mengetahui bahwa hari sudah Senin; ia masuk gunung pada hari Sabtu dan mengira hanya terlambat satu jam dari pertemuan.
statement.en: In the same story Vicente learned only afterwards that it was Monday; he had entered the mountain on Saturday and believed he was merely an hour late for the meeting.

claims.quote: Muntianak — a related name reported in parts of the southern Philippines; it should not be assumed to share every Tagalog detail.

statement.id: Muntianak adalah nama terkait yang dilaporkan di beberapa bagian Filipina selatan; tidak boleh diasumsikan memiliki semua rincian versi Tagalog.
statement.en: Muntianak is a related name reported in parts of the southern Philippines; it should not be assumed to share every Tagalog detail.

claims.quote: Pregnancy and labour could be dangerous, infant mortality was common, and an unexplained cry outside the settlement demanded a moral response. The listener is placed in an impossible position: ignoring a child would be cruel, but answering the cry may expose the rescuer to danger.

statement.id: Menurut artikel itu, kehamilan dan persalinan bisa berbahaya, kematian bayi lazim, dan tangisan tak dikenal di luar permukiman menuntut tanggapan moral; pendengar berada dalam posisi yang mustahil: mengabaikan anak itu kejam, tetapi menjawab tangisannya dapat membahayakan penolong.
statement.en: According to the article, pregnancy and labour could be dangerous, infant mortality was common and an unexplained cry outside the settlement demanded a moral response; the listener is placed in an impossible position, since ignoring a child would be cruel but answering the cry may expose the rescuer to danger.

claims.quote: Modern writers and artists continue to reinterpret the Tiyanak. ... Acuña proposes that the Tiyanak can be read as more than a mindless killer: the figure may also be approached as a newborn trying to understand a violent world created by adults.

statement.id: Penulis dan seniman modern terus menafsirkan ulang tiyanak; Acuña mengusulkan bahwa tiyanak dapat dibaca sebagai lebih dari pembunuh tanpa pikiran, yaitu bayi yang berusaha memahami dunia kejam ciptaan orang dewasa.
statement.en: Modern writers and artists continue to reinterpret the tiyanak; Acuña proposes that the tiyanak can be read as more than a mindless killer, as a newborn trying to understand a violent world created by adults.

claims.quote: a cry resembling that of an abandoned infant draws a traveller toward the roadside, forest, field, or swamp, where the helpless child proves to be something dangerous.

statement.id: Tangisan menyerupai bayi terlantar memikat pejalan menuju tepi jalan, hutan, ladang, atau rawa, tempat anak yang tak berdaya itu ternyata berbahaya.
statement.en: A cry resembling that of an abandoned infant draws a traveller toward the roadside, forest, field or swamp, where the helpless child proves to be something dangerous.

claims.quote: Patianac, mischievous birth-spirits that live in the woods and fields, and lead travellers astray at night.

statement.id: Catatan kaki dalam kumpulan cerita itu menjelaskan patianac sebagai roh kelahiran yang jahil, tinggal di hutan dan ladang, dan menyesatkan pejalan pada malam hari.
statement.en: A footnote in the story collection explains patianac as mischievous birth-spirits that live in the woods and fields and lead travellers astray at night.

short_description.id: Wakwak adalah makhluk mirip burung pengisap darah dalam mitologi Filipina yang konon menyambar manusia pada malam hari; namanya dikaitkan dengan bunyi kepakan sayapnya.
short_description.en: The wakwak is a vampiric, bird-like creature of Philippine mythology said to snatch humans at night; its name is linked to the sound of its flapping wings.

long_description.id: Wakwak adalah makhluk mirip burung pengisap darah dalam mitologi Filipina yang konon menyambar manusia pada malam hari sebagai mangsa, seperti manananggal dan ekek di pedesaan Filipina. Berbeda dari manananggal, ia tidak dapat memisahkan torsonya dari tubuhnya. Sebagian orang meyakininya sejenis vampir, sedangkan yang lain menganggapnya burung malam Filipina yang dikaitkan dengan penyihir.
long_description.en: The wakwak is a vampiric, bird-like creature of Philippine mythology said to snatch humans at night as prey, like the manananggal and the ekek in rural areas of the Philippines. Unlike the manananggal, it cannot separate its torso from its body. Some believe it to be a kind of vampire, while others hold it to be a Philippine night bird associated with witches.

long_description.id: Wakwak sering digambarkan bercakar panjang dan tajam serta bersayap seperti kelelawar; cakar itu dipakai untuk mencabik korban dan mengambil jantungnya. Makhluk ini diyakini dinamai menurut bunyi kepakan sayapnya, yang hanya terdengar saat ia berburu dan makin pelan ketika ia mendekat. Bunyi wakwak biasanya dikaitkan dengan kehadiran Unglu (vampir) atau Ungo (hantu atau monster), dan bunyi tuko pada malam hari pernah pula dikaitkan dengan wakwak.
long_description.en: The wakwak is often described with long sharp talons and bat-like wings, which it uses to slash victims and take their hearts. The creature is believed to be named after the sound of its flapping wings, heard only while it hunts and softer the nearer it comes. The sound is commonly tied to an Unglu (vampire) or Ungo (ghost or monster) being nearby, and a tuko's call at night was once also put down to a wakwak.

long_description.id: Catatan daerah menggambarkannya berbeda-beda. Dalam narasi Aklanon "Encounter with a Wakwak", sang tamu malam mula-mula tampak seperti kelelawar hitam yang amat besar lalu muncul sebagai perempuan berambut panjang, dan tidak ada bagian bawah tubuh yang terlepas. Seorang penulis menuturkan bahwa ibunya di Dulag, Leyte Timur, melihat burung besar kuning kecokelatan bercakar hitam dengan wajah feminin berambut ikal kuning, dan bahwa seorang kerabat ayahnya di Antique melihat wakwak terbang terbalik. Penulis yang sama menyebut bahwa di beberapa daerah Visayas penduduk menamai manananggal dengan wakwak, sedangkan ibunya membedakan keduanya.
long_description.en: Regional records describe it differently. In the Aklanon narrative "Encounter with a Wakwak" the night visitor looks at first like a very large black bat and then turns up as a woman with long hair, and no lower body comes loose. A writer recounts that his mother in Dulag, Eastern Leyte, saw a large tawny bird with black talons and a feminine face with yellow curly hair, and that a relative of his father in Antique saw a wakwak flying upside down. The same writer says that in some areas of the Visayas locals give the name wakwak to the manananggal, while his mother told the two apart.

long_description.id: Sebuah artikel jurnal tentang aswang mencatat bahwa nama seperti wakwak, kiki, atau kaskas di Negros Oriental dan Cebu adalah kata onomatope yang menirukan bunyi, dan bahwa serangan aswang sering didahului bunyi kepakan sayap di atap. Folklorwan Maximo D. Ramos menempatkan wakwak dalam kategori penyedot jeroan, dan catatan tahun 1924 dari Carcar, Cebu, serta koleksi dari Bohol memakai istilah ongo dan wakwak. Dalam catatan dari Bato-bato, ranting jeruk di bawah rumah perempuan hamil dipercaya mencegah wakwak memakannya.
long_description.en: A journal article on the aswang notes that names such as wakwak, kiki or kaskas in Negros Oriental and Cebu are onomatopoeic words imitating sounds, and that aswang attacks are often preceded by the sound of flapping wings on the roof. The folklorist Maximo D. Ramos placed the wakwak in his viscera-sucker category, and a 1924 record from Carcar, Cebu, and a collection from Bohol use the terms ongo and wakwak. In a Bato-bato account, citrus branches under the house of a pregnant woman are believed to keep a wakwak from eating her.

claims.quote: The Wakwak is a vampiric, bird-like creature in Philippine mythology. It is said to snatch humans at night as prey, similar to the manananggal and the Ekek in rural areas of the Philippines. The difference between the Manananggal and the Wakwak is that Wakwak cannot separate its torso from its body while the Manananggal can.

statement.en: The wakwak is a vampiric, bird-like creature of Philippine mythology said to snatch humans at night as prey, like the manananggal and the ekek in rural areas of the Philippines; unlike the manananggal, it cannot separate its torso from its body.

statement.en: The sound a tuko (common house gecko) makes at night when out of sight was found by an American who spent much time in the Philippines to be attributed to a wakwak.

claims.quote: Legend says the Manananggal is a pretty woman by day that transforms into a vicious, half bodied, viscera-eating monster by nightfall. ... In some areas in the Philippines particularly the Visayas, the locals call it the Wakwak. The Wakwak is so named for the sound its wing makes while hovering or flying.

statement.id: Menurut penulis ini, di beberapa daerah, terutama Visayas, penduduk menyebut manananggal (perempuan cantik di siang hari yang berubah menjadi monster pemakan jeroan berbadan separuh pada malam hari) sebagai wakwak, nama yang berasal dari bunyi sayapnya saat melayang atau terbang.
statement.en: According to this writer, in some areas, particularly the Visayas, locals call the manananggal (a pretty woman by day that becomes a half-bodied, viscera-eating monster at night) the wakwak, so named for the sound its wing makes while hovering or flying.

claims.quote: Wakwak, recorded in several Visayan traditions, may name a dangerous night-flying being or imitate its cry.
claims.locator: Manananggal, Wakwak, and Aswang: Why the Names Should Not Be Collapsed

statement.id: Wakwak, yang tercatat dalam beberapa tradisi Visayas, dapat menamai makhluk terbang malam yang berbahaya atau meniru jeritannya.
statement.en: Wakwak, recorded in several Visayan traditions, may name a dangerous night-flying being or imitate its cry.

claims.quote: Maximo D. Ramos, the Filipino folklorist whose comparative studies helped organize a very large body of Philippine material, placed the manananggal and wakwak within his “viscera-sucker” category.
claims.locator: Manananggal, Wakwak, and Aswang: Why the Names Should Not Be Collapsed

statement.id: Folklorwan Maximo D. Ramos menempatkan manananggal dan wakwak dalam kategori "penyedot jeroan" (viscera-sucker) buatannya.
statement.en: The folklorist Maximo D. Ramos placed the manananggal and wakwak within his "viscera-sucker" category.

claims.quote: the Aklanon narrative “Encounter with a Wakwak” describes a night encounter in which the being first resembles an unusually large black bat and then appears as a long-haired woman. The narrator associates it with the repeated cry wak, wak, wak. This account does not describe a detachable lower body

statement.id: Narasi Aklanon "Encounter with a Wakwak" menggambarkan pertemuan malam hari: makhluk itu mula-mula menyerupai kelelawar hitam yang sangat besar lalu tampak sebagai perempuan berambut panjang; penutur mengaitkannya dengan seruan berulang wak, wak, wak, dan kisah itu tidak menyebut bagian bawah tubuh yang dapat terlepas.
statement.en: The Aklanon narrative "Encounter with a Wakwak" describes a night encounter in which the being first resembles an unusually large black bat and then appears as a long-haired woman; the narrator associates it with the repeated cry wak, wak, wak, and the account does not describe a detachable lower body.

claims.quote: Ceferino P. Canaya’s 1924 record from Carcar, Cebu, uses ongo and wakwak. Francisco B. Reyes’s 1924 Bohol collection also records ongo and wakwak

statement.id: Catatan tahun 1924 dari Carcar, Cebu, dan koleksi tahun 1924 dari Bohol sama-sama memakai istilah ongo dan wakwak.
statement.en: A 1924 record from Carcar, Cebu, and a 1924 Bohol collection both use the terms ongo and wakwak.

claims.quote: My Mother’s account of the Wakwak ... my mother has seen one in her teens, out in the rice fields, back in her hometown of Dulag in Eastern Leyte. ... She said she saw what she thought was a large, tawny looking bird with sharp, black talons just a few feet above her head.
claims.locator: My Mother’s account of the Wakwak

statement.id: Seorang penulis menuturkan kisah ibunya, yang di masa remaja di sawah di kota asalnya, Dulag, Leyte Timur, melihat apa yang ia kira burung besar berwarna kuning kecokelatan dengan cakar hitam tajam beberapa kaki di atas kepalanya.
statement.en: A writer recounts his mother's account: in her teens, in the rice fields of her hometown of Dulag in Eastern Leyte, she saw what she thought was a large, tawny bird with sharp black talons a few feet above her head.

claims.quote: She says the thing had a pretty humanoid and feminine face with yellow curly hair. She described its face as looking “like a doll.” Its wings were that of a bird, not a bat.
claims.locator: My Mother’s account of the Wakwak

statement.id: Dalam kisah yang sama, makhluk itu berwajah mirip manusia, cantik dan feminin, berambut ikal kuning, seperti wajah boneka, dan sayapnya sayap burung, bukan kelelawar.
statement.en: In the same account the creature had a pretty humanoid, feminine face with yellow curly hair, like a doll's face, and its wings were a bird's, not a bat's.

claims.quote: In the movies it is normally portrayed as flying in an upright position. My father who grew up in Antique, in the island of Panay, says this is not so. He has a relative who saw a Wakwak flying over a bamboo grove. Dad’s kin says with all lucidity and sobriety that the thing flew upside down.

statement.id: Penulis menyebut film biasanya menggambarkan wakwak terbang tegak, tetapi menurut ayahnya, yang besar di Antique, Pulau Panay, seorang kerabatnya melihat wakwak terbang di atas rumpun bambu dalam posisi terbalik.
statement.en: The writer says films normally portray the wakwak flying upright, but his father, who grew up in Antique on the island of Panay, says a relative saw a wakwak flying over a bamboo grove upside down.

claims.quote: A Bato-bato account recommends placing citrus branches beneath a house where a pregnant woman lives so that a wakwak cannot eat her.

statement.id: Sebuah catatan dari Bato-bato menganjurkan menaruh ranting jeruk di bawah rumah tempat perempuan hamil tinggal agar wakwak tidak dapat memakannya.
statement.en: A Bato-bato account recommends placing citrus branches beneath a house where a pregnant woman lives so that a wakwak cannot eat her.

claims.quote: Tiktik and wakwak ... These names are connected with sounds interpreted as signs of a dangerous nocturnal being. The relationship between sound, bird, and aswang varies by account.

statement.id: Nama tiktik dan wakwak dikaitkan dengan bunyi yang ditafsirkan sebagai tanda makhluk malam yang berbahaya; hubungan antara bunyi, burung, dan aswang berbeda-beda menurut catatan.
statement.en: The names tiktik and wakwak are connected with sounds interpreted as signs of a dangerous nocturnal being; the relationship between sound, bird and aswang varies by account.

claims.quote: Aswang are often heard before they are seen: their attacks are presaged by bird cries emitted either by aswang themselves or their animal familiars (tiktik, kikik), or by the sound of flapping wings on the roof (wakwak or kaskas).

statement.id: Menurut artikel jurnal ini, aswang sering terdengar sebelum terlihat: serangannya didahului pekik burung atau bunyi kepakan sayap di atap (wakwak atau kaskas).
statement.en: According to this journal article, aswang are often heard before they are seen: their attacks are presaged by bird cries or by the sound of flapping wings on the roof (wakwak or kaskas).

claims.quote: Many of the aswang’s names in diverse Philippine ethnolinguistic regions are onomatopoeic words that approximate these noises (tiktik in Aklan, kikik or kakak in Bicol, wakwak, kiki, or kaskas in Negros Oriental and Cebu)

statement.id: Banyak nama aswang di berbagai wilayah etnolinguistik Filipina adalah kata onomatope yang menirukan bunyi itu; wakwak, kiki, atau kaskas dipakai di Negros Oriental dan Cebu.
statement.en: Many names of the aswang in diverse Philippine ethnolinguistic regions are onomatopoeic words approximating these noises; wakwak, kiki or kaskas are used in Negros Oriental and Cebu.

text.id: Tema seni dan legenda sejak prasejarah; laporan kucing domestik bersayap tertua yang diketahui berasal dari Juni 1842
text.en: A theme in art and legend since prehistory; the earliest known report of a winged domestic cat dates from June 1842

short_description.id: Kucing bersayap adalah felid dengan sayap seperti burung atau kelelawar, tema seni dan legenda sejak prasejarah. Kucing domestik bersayap kini dikenal sebagai legenda urban dengan penjelasan medis.
short_description.en: The winged cat is a feline with bird-like or bat-like wings, a theme in art and legend since prehistory. Winged domestic cats are now known as an urban legend with medical explanations.

long_description.id: Kucing bersayap adalah felid yang digambarkan bersayap seperti burung, kelelawar, atau makhluk terbang lain. Menurut sumber pertama, tema ini sudah ada dalam seni dan legenda sejak prasejarah, terutama pada gambaran kucing besar bersayap elang di Eurasia dan Afrika Utara.
long_description.en: The winged cat is a feline depicted with wings like those of a bird, a bat or another flying creature. According to the first source, the theme goes back to prehistory in art and legend, especially in pictures of large cats bearing eagle wings across Eurasia and North Africa.

long_description.id: Singa bersayap dan pantherin bersayap lain umum dalam seni religius dan mitologis bangsa Sumeria, Mesopotamia lain, Akkadia, Persia, dan Skithia. Aq Bars, macan tutul salju bersayap, adalah lambang berasal Turkic dan Bulgar kuno. Dalam Kitab Daniel, binatang pertama dalam penglihatan tentang binatang dari laut menyerupai singa bersayap, dan dalam Kekristenan abad pertengahan setan kadang digambarkan sebagai kucing bersayap kelelawar. Dalam gambaran Nordik, kucing-kucing dewi Freyja juga bersayap.
long_description.en: Winged lions and other winged pantherines are common in the religious and mythological art of the Sumerians, other Mesopotamians, Akkadians, Persians and Scythians. Aq Bars, the winged snow leopard, is a symbol of ancient Turkic and Bulgar origin. In the Book of Daniel, the opening beast of the vision of creatures rising from the sea looks like a winged lion, and in medieval Christianity demons were sometimes depicted as bat-winged cats. In the Norse imagery the cats of the goddess Freyja are also winged.

long_description.id: Kepercayaan akan kucing domestik bersayap bertahan sebagai legenda urban. Penampakannya dijelaskan secara medis oleh rambut kusut, kulit longgar, atau anggota tubuh tambahan di dekat bahu yang mengepak saat kucing berlari, dan tidak ada bukti sayap sungguhan seperti sayap burung atau kelelawar.
long_description.en: Belief in winged domestic cats persists as an urban legend. Sightings are explained medically by matted hair, loose skin or extra limbs near the shoulders that flap as the cat runs, and there is no evidence of true bird-like or bat-like wings.

long_description.id: Laporan tertua yang diketahui berasal dari Henry David Thoreau, yang mencatat kunjungan pada Juni 1842 ke seekor kucing yang sedang berburu di hutan. Menurut pemiliknya, bulu kucing itu menebal dan memipih di sisi tubuhnya pada musim dingin; sebagian orang mengira ia sebagian tupai terbang atau hewan liar lain. Artikel berbahasa Jepang juga mencatat penangkapan hewan berwajah kucing yang bersayap pada 1826 di Jepang.
long_description.en: The earliest known report comes from Henry David Thoreau, who recorded a visit in June 1842 to a cat that was out hunting in the woods. According to its owner, the cat's fur grew thick and flattened along its sides in winter; some thought it partly a flying squirrel or other wild animal. The Japanese-language article also records the capture of a winged, cat-faced animal in Japan in 1826.

short_description.id: Zennyo Ryūō adalah naga pembawa hujan dalam mitologi Jepang yang menurut tradisi Buddha dimunculkan Kūkai pada lomba doa hujan tahun 824 di Kyoto.
short_description.en: Zennyo Ryūō is a rain-bringing dragon of Japanese mythology that, in Buddhist tradition, Kūkai made appear in the 824 rainmaking contest in Kyoto.

long_description.id: Zennyo Ryūō (善如龍王 atau 善女龍王) adalah raja naga pembawa hujan dalam mitologi Jepang dan salah satu raja naga yang menjadi sasaran doa meminta hujan. Menurut tradisi Buddha Jepang, pendeta Kūkai memunculkannya pada tahun 824 di Istana Kekaisaran Kyoto selama lomba doa hujan yang terkenal. Kemunculannya yang paling terkenal terjadi di Shinsen'en, saat Kūkai bersaing dengan pendeta Shubin.
long_description.en: Zennyo Ryūō (善如龍王 or 善女龍王) is a rain-bringing dragon king in Japanese mythology and one of the dragon kings who are objects of rain-praying. According to Japanese Buddhist tradition, the priest Kūkai made him appear in 824 at the Kyoto Imperial Palace during a famous rainmaking contest. His best-known appearance came at the Shinsen'en, when Kūkai competed with the priest Shubin.

long_description.id: Dalam versi artikel bahasa Jepang, Shubin yang iri mengurung dewa naga seluruh negeri dalam guci, tetapi Zennyo Ryūō lolos dan dipanggil dari kolam di India lalu menurunkan hujan lebat ke seluruh negeri. Ia dikatakan keluarga Anavatapta, salah satu Delapan Raja Naga; sebagian versi menyebut ia datang dari Gunung Murō. Naskah 御遺告 tahun 835 menggambarkannya sebagai ular emas kecil yang menunggangi kepala naga yang lebih besar.
long_description.en: In the Japanese article's version, the envious Shubin shut the dragon gods of the whole land in a pitcher, but Zennyo Ryūō escaped, was summoned from a pond in India and sent heavy rain over the whole country. He is said to belong to the family of Anavatapta, one of the Eight Dragon Kings; some versions say he came from Mount Murō. The 835 text 御遺告 describes him as a small golden snake riding on the head of a larger dragon.

long_description.id: Konon Zennyo atau Zentatsu tinggal di gua naga di Gunung Murō, Prefektur Nara, tempat kuno pemujaan naga dan upacara pemanggil hujan. Dalam Genkō Shakusho, ia muncul sebagai perempuan cantik yang mengaku Naga Zennyo dan memperlihatkan cakar raksasa. Seni sering menggambarkannya sebagai naga kecil, kadang sebagai manusia berekor naga; ia dipuja di kuil di Shinsen'en.
long_description.en: Zennyo or Zentatsu supposedly lived in a dragon cave on Mount Murō, Nara Prefecture, an ancient site of dragon worship and rainmaking ceremonies. In the Genkō Shakusho he appears as a beautiful woman who names herself the Dragon Zennyo and reveals a huge claw. Art often depicts him as a small dragon, sometimes as a human with a dragon's tail; he is worshipped at a shrine in the Shinsen'en.
