claims.quote: Zennyo Ryūō (善如龍王 or 善女龍王; lit. "goodness-like dragon-king" or "goodness woman dragon-king", respectively) is a rain-god dragon in Japanese mythology.

statement.id: Zennyo Ryūō adalah dewa naga yang berkaitan dengan hujan dalam mitologi Jepang.
statement.en: Zennyo Ryūō is a rain-associated dragon deity in Japanese mythology.

claims.quote: According to Japanese Buddhist tradition, the priest Kūkai made Zennyo Ryūō appear in 824 AD during a famous rainmaking contest at the Kyoto Imperial Palace.

statement.id: Menurut tradisi Buddha Jepang, Kūkai memunculkan naga ini pada tahun 824 di Istana Kekaisaran Kyoto dalam lomba doa hujan yang terkenal.
statement.en: According to Japanese Buddhist tradition, Kūkai made the dragon appear in 824 at the Kyoto Imperial Palace in a famous rainmaking contest.

claims.quote: The dragon name Zennyo Ryūō is written in Japanese as 善 zen "good, goodness; virtuous", 女 nyo "woman; female" or 如 nyo "like; as if; be like; thus" (differentiated with the "mouth radical" 口), and 龍王 ryūō or 竜王 "dragon king".

statement.id: Namanya memuat 龍王, ungkapan yang berarti raja naga; 善 berarti baik.
statement.en: The name contains 龍王, meaning dragon king; 善 means good.

claims.quote: Zennyo is a common theme in Japanese art, usually depicted as a small dragon but sometimes as a human, either male or female, with a dragon's tail.

statement.id: Karya seni menggambarkannya sebagai naga kecil atau manusia berekor naga.
statement.en: Art represents the deity as a small dragon or as a human with a dragon’s tail.

claims.quote: The best-known appearance of Zennyo was during an 824 CE Buddhist rainmaking competition at the Shinsen'en or Shinzen'en 神泉苑 "Divine Spring Garden" in Kyoto. The scholar priest Kūkai or Kōbō-Daishi (774–835 CE), founder of Shingon "True Word" Buddhism, and his rival priest Shubin 守敏 held a rain-sutra recitation contest.

statement.id: Kemunculan Zennyo yang paling terkenal terjadi pada lomba doa hujan Buddhis tahun 824 di Shinsen'en (神泉苑, "Taman Mata Air Ilahi") di Kyoto, ketika pendeta Kūkai (Kōbō-Daishi), pendiri Buddhisme Shingon, dan saingannya Shubin (守敏) mengadakan lomba pembacaan sutra hujan.
statement.en: Zennyo's best-known appearance was at the 824 Buddhist rainmaking competition at the Shinsen'en (神泉苑, "Divine Spring Garden") in Kyoto, where the priest Kūkai (Kōbō-Daishi), founder of Shingon Buddhism, and his rival Shubin (守敏) held a rain-sutra recitation contest.

claims.quote: Zennyo is worshipped at the Zennyo Ryūō-sha 善女竜王社 Shinto shrine on an island in the Shinsen'en, reached by crossing the Hōsei-bashi 法成橋 "Dharma Completion Bridge".

statement.id: Zennyo dipuja di kuil Shinto Zennyo Ryūō-sha (善女竜王社) pada sebuah pulau di Shinsen'en, yang dicapai dengan menyeberangi Jembatan Hōsei-bashi (法成橋).
statement.en: Zennyo is worshipped at the Shinto shrine Zennyo Ryūō-sha (善女竜王社) on an island in the Shinsen'en, reached by crossing the Hōsei-bashi (法成橋) bridge.

claims.quote: The 835 CE Goyuigō 御遺告, which records Kūkai's last words, first describes Zennyo (Fowler 1997:154) as, "a golden snake measuring eight sun 寸 (approx. 24 cm) riding on the head of a dragon measuring nine shaku 尺 (approx. 2.7 m).

statement.id: 御遺告 tahun 835, yang mencatat kata-kata terakhir Kūkai, pertama kali menggambarkan Zennyo sebagai ular emas sepanjang delapan sun (sekitar 24 cm) yang menunggangi kepala naga sepanjang sembilan shaku (sekitar 2,7 m).
statement.en: The 835 御遺告 (Goyuigō), which records Kūkai's last words, first describes Zennyo as a golden snake eight sun (about 24 cm) long riding on the head of a dragon nine shaku (about 2.7 m) long.

claims.quote: Some versions of this Kūkai story record Zennyo coming from Mount Murō and others from Lake Anavatapta, which is at the center of the world in Buddhist cosmology.

statement.id: Sebagian versi kisah Kūkai ini menyebut Zennyo datang dari Gunung Murō, sedangkan yang lain dari Danau Anavatapta yang berada di pusat dunia dalam kosmologi Buddhis.
statement.en: Some versions of this Kūkai story have Zennyo coming from Mount Murō and others from Lake Anavatapta, at the center of the world in Buddhist cosmology.

claims.quote: Zennyo or Zentatsu 善達 supposedly lived in the Ryūketsu 龍穴 "Dragon Hole/Cave" on Murōyama 室生山 "Mount Murō" in Nara Prefecture, which was an ancient locale of Japanese dragon worship and rainmaking ceremonies.

statement.id: Zennyo atau Zentatsu (善達) konon tinggal di Ryūketsu (龍穴, "gua naga") di Gunung Murō (室生山) di Prefektur Nara, tempat kuno pemujaan naga dan upacara pemanggil hujan di Jepang.
statement.en: Zennyo or Zentatsu (善達) supposedly lived in the Ryūketsu (龍穴, "dragon cave") on Mount Murō (室生山) in Nara Prefecture, an ancient site of dragon worship and rainmaking ceremonies in Japan.

claims.quote: Kokan Shiren's c. 1322 CE Genkō Shakusho "the Genkō era History of Buddhism" has a story about the priest Keien 慶圓 (1143–1223 CE) encountering a beautiful woman who was actually a shapeshifting Zennyo.

statement.id: Genkō Shakusho karya Kokan Shiren (sekitar 1322) memuat kisah pendeta Keien (慶圓, 1143-1223) yang bertemu seorang perempuan cantik yang sebenarnya Zennyo yang mengubah wujud.
statement.en: Kokan Shiren's Genkō Shakusho (c. 1322) has a story of the priest Keien (慶圓, 1143-1223) meeting a beautiful woman who was in fact a shapeshifting Zennyo.

claims.quote: she answered: "I am the Dragon Zennyo". ... It proved to be a claw, more than ten shaku long, which spread a five-coloured light.

statement.id: Dalam kisah itu perempuan tersebut menjawab "Aku adalah Naga Zennyo", dan jari kelingkingnya yang terulur ternyata sebuah cakar lebih dari sepuluh shaku panjangnya yang memancarkan cahaya lima warna.
statement.en: In that story the woman answers "I am the Dragon Zennyo", and the little finger she stretches out proves to be a claw more than ten shaku long that spreads a five-coloured light.

claims.quote: 善女龍王（ぜんにょりゅうおう）は雨乞いの対象である竜王のうちの一尊。「善如龍王」とも表記される。

statement.id: Zennyo Ryūō (善女龍王) adalah salah satu raja naga yang menjadi sasaran doa meminta hujan, dan juga ditulis 「善如龍王」.
statement.en: Zennyo Ryūō (善女龍王) is one of the dragon kings who are objects of rain-praying, and is also written 「善如龍王」.

claims.quote: 調べると空海の名声を妬む守敏により国中の龍神が瓶に閉じ込められていた。しかしただ1体、善女龍王だけは守敏の手から逃れていたので天竺の無熱池（むねっち）から呼び寄せて国中に大雨を降らせたという。

statement.id: Setelah diselidiki, dewa naga seluruh negeri ternyata dikurung dalam guci oleh 守敏 yang iri pada nama baik 空海; hanya Zennyo Ryūō yang lolos dari tangan 守敏, sehingga ia dipanggil dari kolam 無熱池 di India dan konon menurunkan hujan lebat ke seluruh negeri.
statement.en: On investigation, the dragon gods of the whole land had been shut in a pitcher by 守敏, who envied 空海's fame; only Zennyo Ryūō had escaped 守敏's hand, so he was summoned from the pond 無熱池 in India and is said to have sent heavy rain over the whole country.

claims.quote: この弘法（空海）の雨乞いの際にやってきた善女龍王は、八大竜王のひとり阿那婆達多龍王の一族で、阿耨達池（あのくだっち）より阿那婆達多によって連れてこられたとされる。

statement.id: Zennyo Ryūō yang datang pada doa hujan 弘法 (空海) disebut keluarga 阿那婆達多龍王, salah satu dari Delapan Raja Naga, dan dikatakan dibawa dari kolam 阿耨達池 oleh 阿那婆達多.
statement.en: The Zennyo Ryūō who came at 弘法 (空海)'s rain-praying is said to belong to the family of 阿那婆達多龍王, one of the Eight Dragon Kings, and to have been brought from the pond 阿耨達池 by 阿那婆達多.

claims.quote: 「善女」とあるが、像容は男神像で表現されることもあり女神であるとは限らない。

statement.id: Meski disebut 「善女」, rupanya kadang digambarkan sebagai dewa laki-laki, jadi belum tentu seorang dewi.
statement.en: Although it says 「善女」, its image is sometimes shown as a male deity, so it is not necessarily a goddess.

short_description.id: Balāha adalah kuda terbang dalam legenda Buddha, wujud bodhisattva yang menyelamatkan para pedagang dari pulau rakshasa.
short_description.en: Balāha is a flying horse of Buddhist legend, a bodhisattva's form that rescues merchants from an island of rākshasas.

long_description.id: Balāha adalah kuda terbang legendaris dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Buddha, dengan versi berbahasa Tionghoa dan India. Seorang bodhisattva datang dalam wujud kuda terbang yang dapat berbicara, sering putih, kadang bersayap atau berkepala gagak, untuk menyelamatkan para pedagang yang terdampar di pulau rakshasa pemakan manusia. Para pedagang berpegangan pada sisinya seperti pada kapal untuk menyeberangi laut.
long_description.en: Balāha is a legendary flying horse of Buddhist mythology and folklore, with versions in Chinese and Indian languages. A bodhisattva comes in the form of a flying horse that can speak, often white, sometimes winged or crow-headed, to deliver merchants stranded on an island of man-eating rakshasas. The merchants cling to its sides as to a ship to cross the sea.

long_description.id: Dalam Valāhassa Jātaka kuda itu calon Buddha sendiri; versi lebih baru mengaitkannya dengan Avalokiteshvara, dan pulau itu menjadi Sri Lanka.
long_description.en: In the Valāhassa Jātaka the horse is the future Buddha himself; a more recent version attributes the transformation to Avalokiteshvara, and the island becomes the future Ceylon.

long_description.id: Teks Jātaka 196 menggambarkan Bodhisatta sebagai kuda terbang putih berparuh seperti gagak, berambut seperti rumput muñja, yang mampu terbang. Kisahnya berlatar pulau Ceylon, tempat kota Yakkha Sirīsavatthu dihuni para Yakkhini. Kuda itu tiga kali bertanya dengan suara manusia siapa yang ingin pulang, lalu membawa dua ratus lima puluh pedagang ke negeri mereka. Di akhir kisah sang Guru menyatakan bahwa ia sendiri adalah kuda itu.
long_description.en: The text of Jātaka 196 describes the Bodhisatta as a white flying horse beaked like a crow, with hair like muñja grass, able to fly through the air. The story is set on the island of Ceylon, where the Yakkha town Sirīsavatthu is peopled by Yakkhinis. The horse thrice asks in human speech who wants to go home, then conveys two hundred and fifty merchants to their own country. At the end the Teacher declares that he himself was the horse.

long_description.id: Victor Goloubew (1927) menyebut kelompok arca kuda terbang Balâha sebagai yang paling mengesankan di antara arca dari penggalian Nâk Pân di Angkor, dan menafsirkan kuda batu itu sebagai lambang makhluk yang mendambakan pembebasan.
long_description.en: Victor Goloubew (1927) calls the flying-horse group Balâha the most remarkable of the sculptures from the Nâk Pân excavations at Angkor, and interprets the stone horse as a symbol of beings aspiring to deliverance.

claims.quote: Balāha est un cheval volant légendaire de la mythologie et du folklore bouddhiques. Son histoire existe en différente versions, notamment en langue chinoise et en langue indienne.

statement.id: Balāha adalah kuda terbang legendaris dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Buddha, yang kisahnya ada dalam berbagai versi, terutama berbahasa Tionghoa dan India.
statement.en: Balāha is a legendary flying horse of Buddhist mythology and folklore, whose story exists in various versions, notably in Chinese and Indian languages.

claims.quote: Un bodhisattva vient, sous la forme d'un cheval volant doué de parole et de raison (souvent blanc, parfois ailé ou encore à tête de corneille) délivrer des marchands hindous échoués sur une île, qui ont par erreur fait confiance à des rākshasas, démons anthropophages.

statement.id: Seorang bodhisattva datang dalam wujud kuda terbang yang dapat berbicara dan berpikir, sering putih, kadang bersayap atau berkepala gagak, untuk menyelamatkan para pedagang yang terdampar di pulau setelah keliru memercayai rakshasa pemakan manusia.
statement.en: A bodhisattva comes as a flying horse gifted with speech and reason, often white, sometimes winged or crow-headed, to rescue merchants stranded on an island who mistakenly trusted man-eating rākshasas.

claims.quote: Dans les Jātaka Valāhassa, ce cheval est le futur Bouddha lui-même, dans l'une de ses précédentes incarnations. Une version plus récente attribue cette métamorphose à Avalokiteshvara, et l'île devient la future Ceylan .

statement.id: Dalam Valāhassa Jātaka kuda itu adalah calon Buddha sendiri dalam salah satu kelahiran sebelumnya; versi yang lebih baru mengaitkan perubahan wujud ini dengan Avalokiteshvara, dan pulau itu menjadi Sri Lanka (Ceylon).
statement.en: In the Valāhassa Jātaka the horse is the future Buddha himself in a previous birth; a later version ascribes the transformation to Avalokiteshvara, and the island becomes the future Ceylon.

claims.quote: Tous les marchands s'accrochent aux flancs du cheval comme à ceux d'un navire pour s'échapper et traverser la mer.

statement.id: Semua pedagang berpegangan pada sisi kuda itu seperti pada kapal untuk melarikan diri menyeberangi laut.
statement.en: All the merchants cling to the horse's flanks as if to a ship to escape across the sea.

statement.id: Artikel bahasa Khmer juga menyebut Balāha kuda terbang dalam legenda Buddha.
statement.en: The Khmer article likewise calls Balāha a flying horse of Buddhist legend.

claims.quote: Now at that time, the Bodhisatta had come into the world as a flying horse ... white all over, and beaked like a crow, with hair like muñja grass ... possessed of Supernormal Powers, able to fly through the air.

statement.id: Dalam Valāhassajātaka (Ja 196) Bodhisatta lahir sebagai kuda terbang, putih seluruhnya, berparuh seperti gagak, berambut seperti rumput muñja, memiliki kekuatan adiduniawi dan mampu terbang di udara.
statement.en: In the Valāhassajātaka (Ja 196) the Bodhisatta had come into the world as a flying horse, white all over, beaked like a crow, with hair like muñja grass, possessed of supernormal powers and able to fly through the air.

claims.quote: In the past, there was in the island of Ceylon a Yakkha town called Sirīsavatthu, peopled by Yakkhinis.

statement.id: Menurut Jātaka ini, di pulau Ceylon ada kota Yakkha bernama Sirīsavatthu yang dihuni para Yakkhini.
statement.en: According to the Jātaka, in the island of Ceylon there was a Yakkha town called Sirīsavatthu, peopled by Yakkhinis.

claims.quote: As he passed on thus, he thrice uttered human speech filled with mercy, saying: “Who wants to go home? Who wants to go home?”

statement.id: Saat terbang melintasi Ceylon, kuda itu tiga kali berucap dengan suara manusia penuh welas asih: "Siapa yang ingin pulang? Siapa yang ingin pulang?"
statement.en: As he flew over Ceylon the horse thrice uttered human speech filled with mercy: 'Who wants to go home? Who wants to go home?'

claims.quote: Then the Bodhisatta took up even those who stood still saluting him, and conveyed all of them, even two hundred and fifty, to their own country

statement.id: Bodhisatta membawa seluruh dua ratus lima puluh pedagang, termasuk yang berdiri memberi hormat, kembali ke negeri mereka sendiri.
statement.en: The Bodhisatta conveyed all two hundred and fifty merchants, even those who stood saluting him, to their own country.

claims.quote: The Buddha’s followers were the two hundred and fifty who followed the advice of the horse, and I was the horse myself.

statement.id: Pada penutup Jātaka, sang Guru menyatakan bahwa dua ratus lima puluh pedagang itu adalah para pengikut Buddha, dan bahwa ia sendiri adalah kuda itu.
statement.en: At the close of the Jātaka the Teacher declares that the two hundred and fifty merchants who followed the horse's advice were the Buddha's followers, and that he himself was the horse.

claims.quote: Nâk Pân, à l'Est du Práh Khan d'Ankor, la plus remarquable est le groupe du cheval volant Balâha

statement.id: Victor Goloubew (1927) menyebut kelompok arca kuda terbang Balâha sebagai yang paling mengesankan di antara arca yang ditemukan dalam penggalian Nâk Pân, di timur Práh Khan di Angkor.
statement.en: Victor Goloubew (1927) calls the flying-horse group Balâha the most remarkable of the sculptures found in the excavations at Nâk Pân, east of Práh Khan at Angkor.

claims.quote: C'est vers elle que le cheval de pierre hâtait sa course, symbole matériel de tout être qui, à travers ses renaissances multiples, aspire à la délivrance.

statement.id: Menurut Goloubew, kuda batu itu bergegas menuju arca di sel kuil, sebagai lambang material setiap makhluk yang, melalui kelahiran kembali yang berulang, mendambakan pembebasan.
statement.en: According to Goloubew, the stone horse hastened toward the image in the temple cella, a material symbol of every being who, through multiple rebirths, aspires to deliverance.

short_description.id: Champ atau Champy adalah monster danau dalam cerita rakyat Amerika yang dikatakan hidup di Danau Champlain di antara New York dan Vermont, digambarkan sebagai ular laut berkepala kuda.
short_description.en: Champ, or Champy, is a lake monster of American folklore said to live in Lake Champlain between New York and Vermont, described as a sea serpent with a horse's head.

long_description.id: Champ, juga disebut Champy atau Tatoskok, adalah makhluk air yang konon menghuni Danau Champlain, perairan tawar yang dibagi antara New York dan Vermont dan sebagian masuk ke Quebec. Ia digambarkan sebagai ular laut sepanjang sekitar 20 kaki berkepala kuda, dan telah ada lebih dari 300 laporan penampakan. Cerita aslinya dikaitkan dengan legenda Iroquois tentang ular raksasa yang oleh bangsa Mohawk disebut Onyare'kowa.
long_description.en: Champ, also called Champy or Tatoskok, is a water creature said to inhabit Lake Champlain, a body of fresh water shared by New York and Vermont and reaching into Quebec. It is described as a sea serpent about 20 feet long with a horse's head, and more than 300 sightings have been reported. The original story is tied to Iroquois legends of giant snakes that the Mohawk called Onyare'kowa.

long_description.id: Penjelajah Samuel de Champlain sering dikatakan sebagai orang Eropa pertama yang melihat Champ pada 1609, tetapi tidak ada bukti ia mengatakan hal itu, dan ia hanya mencatat ikan-ikan besar; para kriptozoolog menyimpulkan ia menggambarkan ikan gar. Laporan 1819 menyebut Crum melihat monster sepanjang sekitar 187 kaki, dan pada 1883 Sheriff Nathan H. Mooney mengaku melihat ular air. P. T. Barnum menawarkan hadiah pada 1873 dan 1887.
long_description.en: Explorer Samuel de Champlain is often said to have been the first European to see Champ in 1609, but there is no evidence he said so and he only recorded large fish; cryptozoologists conclude he described a gar. An 1819 report has Crum seeing a monster about 187 feet long, and in 1883 Sheriff Nathan H. Mooney claimed to have seen a water serpent. P. T. Barnum offered rewards in 1873 and 1887.

long_description.id: Pada 1977 Sandra Mansi mengambil foto yang tampak memperlihatkan hewan berleher panjang muncul dari danau; keluarga Mansi melaporkan makhluk berkepala kecil dan berpunuk. Teluk tempat foto itu diambil tidak lebih dalam dari 14 kaki, dan Joe Nickell menilai makhluk raksasa tak mungkin berenang apalagi bersembunyi di sana. Penentang menyebut danau terlalu kecil dan tidak ada bukti fisik, dengan penjelasan berupa tipuan, salah kenal benda mati, dan salah identifikasi hewan.
long_description.en: In 1977 Sandra Mansi took a photograph that appears to show a long-necked animal emerging from the lake, and the Mansis reported a creature with a small head and a humped back. The bay where it was taken is no deeper than 14 feet, and Joe Nickell judged that a giant creature could hardly swim, let alone hide, there. Skeptics cite a lake too small and no physical proof, offering explanations of hoax, confusion with inanimate objects, and misidentified animals.

long_description.id: Pada awal 1980-an Vermont dan New York sama-sama mengesahkan undang-undang yang melindungi habitat dan kehidupan Champ. Legendanya dianggap daya tarik wisata di sekitar Burlington, Vermont, dan Plattsburgh, New York, dan desa Port Henry mendirikan model raksasa serta menggelar Champ Day tiap Agustus.
long_description.en: Vermont and New York both enacted laws in the early 1980s to protect Champ's habitat and life. The legend is considered a tourist draw around Burlington, Vermont, and Plattsburgh, New York, and the village of Port Henry has erected a giant model and holds Champ Day each August.

cultural_context.id: Legenda Champ dianggap daya tarik wisata di wilayah Burlington dan Plattsburgh dan telah menjadi atraksi yang menghasilkan pendapatan.
cultural_context.en: The Champ legend is considered a draw for tourism in the Burlington and Plattsburgh areas and has become a revenue-generating attraction.

statement.en: In 1977 the Mansi photograph surfaced, which appeared to be documented proof of Champ's existence; in the early 1980s both Vermont and New York passed laws protecting the habitat and life of Champ.

claims.quote: The theories that attempt to disprove Champ’s existence rely on the facts that the lake is not large enough for a creature of Champ’s size to hide and survive; ... and that there is no physical proof of Champ’s existence.

statement.en: The theories that attempt to disprove Champ's existence rely on the facts that the lake is not large enough for a creature of Champ's size to hide and survive, and that there is no physical proof of Champ's existence.

claims.quote: There are several possible explanations that are posited to explain the nature of the photographs, video, and testimony for Champ. The three major categories of explanations are hoaxes, confusion with inanimate objects, and misidentification of other animals.

statement.en: Several explanations are posited for the photographs, video, and testimony for Champ; the three major categories are hoaxes, confusion with inanimate objects, and misidentification of other animals.

short_description.id: Guhuoniao adalah burung legenda Tiongkok yang dapat berubah menjadi perempuan dan dikisahkan mengambil bayi orang untuk diasuh sebagai anaknya.
short_description.en: Guhuoniao is a legendary Chinese bird that can change into a woman and is said to take other people's infants to raise as its own.

long_description.id: Guhuoniao adalah burung legenda dalam cerita rakyat Tiongkok. Xuan Zhong Ji memuat gambaran yang kemudian dirujuk Bencao Gangmu.
long_description.en: Guhuoniao is a legendary bird in Chinese folklore. The Xuan Zhong Ji contains descriptions later consulted by the Bencao Gangmu.

long_description.id: Nama alternatif meliputi rumuniao atau burung ibu susu dan yexing younu atau perempuan pengelana malam. Makhluk ini dapat berubah dari burung menjadi perempuan dengan melepas bulu atau pakaian bulunya. Kisah mengaitkan burung ini dengan penculikan bayi yang diasuh sebagai anaknya.
long_description.en: Alternative names include rumuniao, milk-mother bird, and yexing younu, night-traveling woman. It changes from bird to woman by removing its down or feather garment. The tale associates this bird with kidnapping infants to raise as its own.

long_description.id: Bencao Gangmu mengutip Xuanzhong Ji bahwa Guhuoniao tergolong makhluk gaib: memakai bulu ia menjadi burung terbang dan menanggalkannya menjadi perempuan. Ia dikatakan berasal dari perempuan yang meninggal saat bersalin, gemar mengambil anak orang, dan dapat merenggut jiwa orang; menurut Li Shizhen, burung ini seluruhnya betina dan terbang pada malam hari di bulan ketujuh dan kedelapan.
long_description.en: The Bencao Gangmu quotes the Xuanzhong Ji that the Guhuoniao belongs to the class of spirits: wearing feathers it is a flying bird and shedding them it becomes a woman. It is said to come from a woman who died in childbirth, likes to take other people's children, and can take away people's souls; according to Li Shizhen, the bird is entirely female and flies at night in the seventh and eighth months.

long_description.id: Rumah yang punya anak kecil dianjurkan tidak menjemur pakaian di luar pada malam hari, karena burung ini menandai dengan darah sehingga anak jatuh sakit kejang dan gizi buruk. Bencao Gangmu juga menyamakan 夭鳥 dalam Zhouli, yang dipanah dengan busur dan anak panah penyelamat matahari dan bulan, dengan burung ini.
long_description.en: Homes with small children are advised not to leave clothing out at night, because the bird marks it with blood so the child falls ill with convulsions and wasting. The Bencao Gangmu also identifies the 夭鳥 of the Zhouli, shot with the bow and arrows for rescuing the sun and moon, with this bird.

description.en: Wearing feathers it is a flying bird; shedding them it becomes a woman.

claims.quote: The Guhuo・niao (Chinese: 姑獲鳥, "wench bird") is a legendary bird from Chinese folklore.

statement.id: Guhuoniao adalah burung legenda dalam cerita rakyat Tiongkok.
statement.en: Guhuoniao is a legendary bird in Chinese folklore.

claims.quote: It is described in such texts as the Western Jin natural history work Xuan Zhong Ji ... and consulted by the Ming period pharmacopoeia Bencao Gangmu ... which collates information from various works.

statement.id: Xuan Zhong Ji memuat gambaran yang kemudian dirujuk Bencao Gangmu.
statement.en: The Xuan Zhong Ji contains descriptions later consulted by the Bencao Gangmu.

claims.quote: The guhuoniao (姑獲鳥, "wench bird") has had several aliases, such as rumuniao (乳母鳥, "mother's milk bird", or in Japanese, ubadori "wetnurse bird"), yexing younu (夜行遊女; "nighttime traveling girl"), tiandi shaonu (天帝少女; "celestial emperor's young girl"), wuguniao (無辜鳥; "innocent bird"),  yinfei (隠飛; "hidden flying"), Gou xing (鈎星; 鉤星; "hook star[?]"); gu niao (鬼鳥; "demon bird"), yi xi (譩譆).

statement.id: Nama alternatif meliputi rumuniao atau burung ibu susu dan yexing younu atau perempuan pengelana malam.
statement.en: Alternative names include rumuniao, milk-mother bird, and yexing younu, night-traveling woman.

claims.quote: It can transform from bird to human woman by shedding its "hair" (or down, i.e., removing its feather garment).

statement.id: Makhluk ini dapat berubah dari burung menjadi perempuan dengan melepas bulu atau pakaian bulunya.
statement.en: It changes from bird to woman by removing its down or feather garment.

claims.quote: It has the habit of kidnapping infants to raise it as its own. It flies by night and marks the child with a drop of its blood. This will cause the child to fall ill and develop convulsions, in an illness condition called "innocent's gan" (無辜疳; wugugan, roughly translatable as "innocent's malnutrition" or "wasting-away" illness).

statement.id: Kisah mengaitkan burung ini dengan penculikan bayi yang diasuh sebagai anaknya.
statement.en: The tale associates this bird with kidnapping infants to raise as its own.

claims.quote: 藏器曰︰姑獲能收人魂魄。《玄中記》云︰姑獲鳥，鬼神類也。衣毛為飛鳥，脫毛為女人。
claims.locator: Bencao Gangmu (本草綱目), bagian Burung bab 4, entri 姑獲鳥

statement.id: Bencao Gangmu mengutip Chen Zangqi (藏器) bahwa 姑獲 dapat merenggut roh dan jiwa orang, serta Xuanzhong Ji (玄中記) bahwa burung ini tergolong makhluk gaib (鬼神類): memakai bulu ia menjadi burung terbang, menanggalkan bulu ia menjadi perempuan.
statement.en: The Bencao Gangmu quotes Zangqi (藏器) that 姑獲 can take away people's souls, and the Xuanzhong Ji (玄中記) that the bird belongs to the class of spirits (鬼神類): wearing feathers it is a flying bird, shedding them it becomes a woman.

claims.quote: 凡有小兒家，不可夜露衣物。此鳥夜飛，以血點之為志。兒輒病驚癇及疳疾，謂之無辜疳也。
claims.locator: Bencao Gangmu (本草綱目), bagian Burung bab 4, entri 姑獲鳥

statement.id: Menurut kutipan itu, rumah yang punya anak kecil tidak boleh menjemur pakaian di luar pada malam hari, sebab burung ini terbang malam dan menandai dengan setetes darah; anak yang ditandai jatuh sakit kejang dan gizi buruk, penyakit yang disebut 無辜疳.
statement.en: According to the quotation, homes with small children should not leave clothing out at night, because this bird flies by night and marks it with blood; the child then falls ill with convulsions and wasting, an illness called 無辜疳.

claims.quote: 脫毛為女人。云是產婦死後化作，故胸前有兩乳，喜取人子養為己子。
claims.locator: Bencao Gangmu (本草綱目), bagian Burung bab 4, entri 姑獲鳥

statement.id: Kutipan itu menyebut burung ini dikatakan berasal dari perempuan yang meninggal saat bersalin, sehingga ada dua payudara di dadanya, dan ia gemar mengambil anak orang untuk diasuh sebagai anaknya.
statement.en: The quotation says the bird is said to be formed from a woman who died in childbirth, hence two breasts on its chest, and it likes to take other people's children to raise as its own.

claims.quote: 時珍曰︰昔人言此鳥產婦所化，陰慝為妖，故有諸名。 ... 時珍曰︰此鳥純雌無雄，七八月夜飛，害人尤毒也。
claims.locator: Bencao Gangmu (本草綱目), bagian Burung bab 4, entri 姑獲鳥

statement.id: Li Shizhen (時珍) menulis bahwa orang dahulu mengatakan burung ini berasal dari perempuan yang meninggal saat bersalin, bahwa burung ini seluruhnya betina tanpa jantan, terbang pada malam hari di bulan ketujuh dan kedelapan, dan sangat berbisa dalam mencelakai orang.
statement.en: Li Shizhen (時珍) writes that people of old said this bird came from a woman who died in childbirth, that it is entirely female with no males, flies at night in the seventh and eighth months, and is especially venomous in harming people.

claims.quote: 荊州多有之。亦謂之鬼鳥。《周禮》庭氏「以救日之弓，救月之矢，射夭鳥」，即此也。
claims.locator: Bencao Gangmu (本草綱目), bagian Burung bab 4, entri 姑獲鳥

statement.id: Bencao Gangmu menyamakan 夭鳥 dalam Zhouli (周禮) yang dipanah oleh pejabat Tingshi (庭氏) dengan busur dan anak panah penyelamat matahari dan bulan, dengan burung ini.
statement.en: The Bencao Gangmu identifies the 夭鳥 in the Zhouli (周禮), shot by the official Tingshi (庭氏) with the bow and arrows for rescuing the sun and moon, with this bird.

claims.quote: 荊州多有之。亦謂之鬼鳥。《周禮》庭氏「以救日之弓，救月之矢，射夭鳥」，即此也。
claims.locator: Bencao Gangmu (本草綱目), bagian Burung bab 4, entri 姑獲鳥

statement.id: Kutipan Bencao Gangmu menyebut burung ini banyak terdapat di Jingzhou (荊州) dan juga disebut 鬼鳥.
statement.en: The Bencao Gangmu quotation says the bird is common in Jingzhou (荊州) and is also called 鬼鳥.

text.en: Appears in European folklore since the Middle Ages; the Sleepy Hollow version was published in 1820

short_description.id: Penunggang Kuda Tanpa Kepala adalah arketipe tokoh mitos dalam cerita rakyat Eropa sejak Abad Pertengahan, digambarkan sebagai penunggang kuda yang kehilangan kepalanya.
short_description.en: The Headless Horseman is an archetype of mythical figure in European folklore since the Middle Ages, depicted as a rider on horseback who has lost his head.

long_description.id: Penunggang Kuda Tanpa Kepala adalah arketipe tokoh mitos yang muncul dalam cerita rakyat di seluruh Eropa sejak Abad Pertengahan. Tokoh-tokoh itu secara tradisional digambarkan sebagai penunggang kuda yang tidak berkepala. Bergantung pada legendanya, sang Penunggang membawa kepalanya atau sama sekali kehilangannya, dan mungkin sedang mencarinya.
long_description.en: The Headless Horseman is a mythical archetype found in European folklore since the Middle Ages. Such figures are traditionally shown as riders on horseback who lack their heads. Depending on the legend, the Horseman either carries his head or has lost it altogether, and may be searching for it.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Irlandia, dullahan adalah peri iblis tanpa kepala yang biasanya menunggang kuda dan membawa kepalanya di bawah lengan. Ia memakai cambuk dari tulang punggung mayat; ketika ia berhenti berkuda, terjadi kematian, dan ketika ia menyerukan sebuah nama, orang itu langsung mati. Dalam versi lain ia kusir kereta hitam, dan sosok serupa, gan ceann, dapat ditakuti pergi dengan benda emas. Sebagian versi menyebut dullahan sebagai roh Crom Dubh, dewa Celtic.
long_description.en: In Irish folklore the dullahan is a demonic, headless fairy who usually rides a horse with his head tucked under one arm. He wields a whip made from a corpse's spine; when he stops riding a death occurs, and when he calls out a name that person immediately dies. In another version he drives a black carriage, and a similar figure, the gan ceann, can be frightened away with a gold object. In some versions the dullahan is the spirit of Crom Dubh, a Celtic god.

long_description.id: Kisah Skotlandia yang paling menonjol menyangkut Ewen, yang dipenggal dalam pertempuran klan di Pulau Mull; di Cape Breton, melihat atau mendengar penunggang tanpa kepala dianggap pertanda kematian dalam keluarga. Di Rhineland, penunggang itu membunuh dengan sentuhan, atau sebagai Der Kopflose Reiter memperingatkan orang hidup dan menghukum orang jahat. Di Texas selatan, 'El Muerto' menggantungkan kepalanya di pelana dan kudanya memercikkan petir.
long_description.en: The most prominent Scottish tale concerns Ewen, decapitated in a clan battle on the Isle of Mull; in Cape Breton, seeing or hearing a headless rider is regarded as an omen of death in the family. In the Rhineland the horsemen killed by touch, or as Der Kopflose Reiter warned the living and punished the wicked. In southern Texas 'El Muerto' dangles his head from his saddle and his horse produces lightning.

long_description.id: Dalam The Legend of Sleepy Hollow karya Washington Irving, roh yang menghantui wilayah itu adalah penampakan sosok berkuda tanpa kepala, yang menurut sebagian orang adalah hantu prajurit Hessian yang kepalanya terbawa bola meriam dalam Perang Revolusi. Hantunya berkuda setiap malam mencari kepalanya dan terburu-buru kembali ke pemakaman sebelum fajar. Dalam kisah Brouwer, sang Penunggang tiba-tiba menjadi kerangka dan melesat dengan gelegar petir, dan dalam kisah Brom Bones ia lenyap dalam kilatan api di jembatan gereja.
long_description.en: In Washington Irving's The Legend of Sleepy Hollow the spirit that haunts the region is the apparition of a figure on horseback without a head, held by some to be the ghost of a Hessian trooper decapitated by a cannon-ball in a nameless Revolutionary War battle. The ghost rides nightly in quest of his head and hurries back to the churchyard before daybreak. In Brouwer's tale the Horseman suddenly turns into a skeleton and leaps away with a clap of thunder, and in Brom Bones's tale he vanishes in a flash of fire at the church bridge.

cultural_context.id: Mitos penunggang tanpa kepala telah mengilhami banyak kisah dan tokoh di seluruh dunia, dan sejak terbit pada 1820 Penunggang Kuda Tanpa Kepala karya Irving menjadi bagian integral cerita rakyat Amerika.
cultural_context.en: These myths have inspired many stories and characters worldwide, and Irving's Headless Horseman, published in 1820, has become an integral part of American folklore.

description.id: Penunggang yang membunuh dengan sentuhan atau memperingatkan orang hidup akan bahaya dan menghukum orang jahat.
description.en: A rider who killed by touch or warned the living of danger and punished the wicked.

description.id: Sosok yang menggantungkan kepalanya di pelana, dengan kuda yang dikatakan memercikkan petir.
description.en: A figure who dangles his head from his saddle, with a horse said to produce lightning.

description.id: Penampakan sosok berkuda tanpa kepala yang menurut sebagian orang adalah hantu prajurit Hessian.
description.en: The apparition of a figure on horseback without a head said by some to be the ghost of a Hessian trooper.

title.en: The tale of Brouwer and the Horseman

role.id: Penunggang yang menculik dan melempar Brouwer.
role.en: The Horseman who carries off and throws Brouwer.

summary.id: Brouwer, penentang hantu, bertemu sang Penunggang dan terpaksa naik di belakangnya; di jembatan sang Penunggang menjadi kerangka, melempar Brouwer ke sungai, dan melesat dengan gelegar petir.
summary.en: Brouwer, a disbeliever in ghosts, meets the Horseman and is obliged to get up behind him; at the bridge the Horseman becomes a skeleton, throws Brouwer into the brook, and leaps away with a clap of thunder.

role.id: Prajurit tengah malam yang diajak adu pacu.
role.en: The midnight trooper challenged to a race.

summary.id: Brom Bones menegaskan bahwa ia disusul prajurit tengah malam itu dan mengajaknya adu pacu; di jembatan gereja sang Hessian kabur dan lenyap dalam kilatan api.
summary.en: Brom Bones affirmed that the midnight trooper overtook him and that he offered a race; at the church bridge the Hessian veered off and disappeared in a burst of flame.

description.id: Lembah tempat Penunggang Kuda Tanpa Kepala menghantui dalam cerita Irving.
description.en: The valley haunted by the Headless Horseman in Irving's story.

description.id: Tempat sang Penunggang konon menambatkan kudanya di antara makam dan kembali sebelum fajar.
description.en: Where the Horseman was said to tether his horse among the graves and to which he returns before daybreak.

note.en: The black carriage driven by the headless dullahan in another version.

description.en: The Horseman is the ghost of a murderous Hessian mercenary summoned by Lady Van Tassel to eliminate her enemies.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa gambaran penunggang tanpa kepala muncul di begitu banyak tradisi dengan peran berbeda, dari pertanda maut hingga penghukum orang jahat?
learning_questions.en: Why does the image of a headless rider appear in so many traditions with different roles, from death omen to punisher of the wicked?

claims.quote: The Headless Horseman is an archetype of mythical figure that has appeared in folklore around Europe since the Middle Ages.

statement.id: Penunggang Kuda Tanpa Kepala adalah arketipe tokoh mitos yang muncul dalam cerita rakyat di seluruh Eropa sejak Abad Pertengahan.
statement.en: The Headless Horseman is an archetype of mythical figure that has appeared in folklore around Europe since the Middle Ages.

claims.quote: The figures are traditionally depicted as riders on horseback who are missing their heads.

statement.id: Sosok-sosok ini secara tradisional digambarkan sebagai penunggang kuda yang kehilangan kepala.
statement.en: The figures are traditionally depicted as riders on horseback who are missing their heads.

claims.quote: These myths have since inspired a number of stories and characters in culture around the world, including The Legend of Sleepy Hollow.

statement.id: Mitos ini mengilhami banyak kisah termasuk The Legend of Sleepy Hollow.
statement.en: These myths have since inspired a number of stories and characters in culture around the world, including The Legend of Sleepy Hollow.

claims.quote: Some versions of the story claim the dullahan is the spirit of Crom Dubh, a Celtic god worshipped in Ireland until the arrival of Christian missionaries in the 6th century.

statement.id: Sebagian versi cerita menyatakan dullahan adalah roh Crom Dubh, dewa Keltik di Irlandia.
statement.en: Some versions of the story claim the dullahan is the spirit of Crom Dubh, a Celtic god worshipped in Ireland until the arrival of Christian missionaries in the 6th century.

claims.quote: Depending on the legend, the Horseman is either carrying his head, or is missing his head altogether, and may be searching for it.

statement.id: Bergantung pada legendanya, sang Penunggang entah membawa kepalanya atau sama sekali kehilangan kepala dan mungkin sedang mencarinya.
statement.en: Depending on the legend, the Horseman is either carrying his head or is missing his head altogether, and may be searching for it.

claims.quote: In Irish folklore ... The dullahan or dulachán ("dark man") is a headless, demonic fairy, usually riding a horse and carrying his head under his arm.

statement.id: Dullahan atau dulachán ('pria gelap') adalah peri iblis tanpa kepala yang biasanya menunggang kuda dan membawa kepalanya di bawah lengan.
statement.en: The dullahan or dulachán ('dark man') is a headless, demonic fairy, usually riding a horse and carrying his head under his arm.

claims.quote: The dullahan or dulachán ("dark man") is a headless, demonic fairy ... He wields a whip made from a human corpse's spine. When the dullahan stops riding, a death occurs. The dullahan calls out a name, at which point the named person immediately dies.

statement.id: Dullahan menggunakan cambuk dari tulang punggung mayat manusia; ketika dullahan berhenti berkuda, terjadi kematian, dan ketika ia menyerukan sebuah nama, orang yang disebut langsung mati.
statement.en: The dullahan wields a whip made from a human corpse's spine; when the dullahan stops riding, a death occurs, and when he calls out a name, the named person immediately dies.

claims.quote: In another version, he is the headless driver of a black carriage, the Cóiste Bodhar. A similar figure, the gan ceann ("without a head"), can be frightened away by wearing a gold object or putting one in his path.

statement.id: Dalam versi lain, ia adalah kusir tanpa kepala dari kereta hitam, Cóiste Bodhar; sosok serupa, gan ceann ('tanpa kepala'), dapat ditakuti pergi dengan mengenakan benda emas atau meletakkannya di jalurnya.
statement.en: In another version he is the headless driver of a black carriage, the Cóiste Bodhar; a similar figure, the gan ceann ('without a head'), can be frightened away by wearing a gold object or putting one in his path.

claims.quote: The most prominent Scottish tale of the headless horseman concerns a man named Ewen decapitated in a clan battle at Glen Cainnir on the Isle of Mull.

statement.id: Kisah penunggang kuda tanpa kepala Skotlandia yang paling menonjol menyangkut seorang pria bernama Ewen yang dipenggal dalam pertempuran klan di Glen Cainnir, Pulau Mull.
statement.en: The most prominent Scottish tale of the headless horseman concerns a man named Ewen decapitated in a clan battle at Glen Cainnir on the Isle of Mull.

claims.quote: Among the Highland Scottish diaspora in Cape Breton, Nova Scotia, seeing the image or hearing the sound of a horse or headless rider is traditionally regarded as an omen of an imminent death within the family.

statement.id: Di kalangan diaspora Highland Skotlandia di Cape Breton, Nova Scotia, melihat bayangan atau mendengar suara kuda atau penunggang tanpa kepala secara tradisional dianggap pertanda kematian dalam keluarga yang segera terjadi.
statement.en: Among the Highland Scottish diaspora in Cape Breton, Nova Scotia, seeing the image or hearing the sound of a horse or headless rider is traditionally regarded as an omen of an imminent death within the family.

claims.quote: In Germany, headless-horseman stories come mostly from the Rhineland. Rather than using decapitation, the headless horsemen killed their victims simply by touching them. They were revenants who had to wander the earth until they had atoned for their sins

statement.id: Di Jerman, kisah penunggang kuda tanpa kepala kebanyakan berasal dari Rhineland; penunggang itu membunuh korban hanya dengan menyentuh mereka, dan mereka adalah arwah yang harus mengembara di bumi sampai menebus dosa.
statement.en: In Germany, headless-horseman stories come mostly from the Rhineland; the headless horsemen killed their victims simply by touching them and were revenants who had to wander the earth until they had atoned for their sins.

claims.quote: Another version of the legend spoke of Der Kopflose Reiter (the headless horseman), who would warn the living of impending danger and chase down and punish the wicked.

statement.id: Versi lain legenda itu menyebut Der Kopflose Reiter (penunggang kuda tanpa kepala), yang memperingatkan orang hidup akan bahaya yang mengancam serta mengejar dan menghukum orang jahat.
statement.en: Another version of the legend spoke of Der Kopflose Reiter (the headless horseman), who would warn the living of impending danger and chase down and punish the wicked.

claims.quote: In southern Texas, stories of a figure known as "El Muerto" have circulated since the mid-1800s. El Muerto is said to dangle his head from his saddle, and his horse is variably said to produce lightning from its hooves as they strike the ground.

statement.id: Di Texas selatan, kisah tentang sosok bernama 'El Muerto' beredar sejak pertengahan 1800-an; ia dikatakan menggantungkan kepalanya di pelana, dan kudanya dikatakan memercikkan petir dari kukunya ketika menghentak tanah.
statement.en: In southern Texas, stories of a figure known as 'El Muerto' have circulated since the mid-1800s; El Muerto is said to dangle his head from his saddle, and his horse is variably said to produce lightning from its hooves as they strike the ground.

claims.quote: Washington Irving's short story The Legend of Sleepy Hollow features a character known as the Headless Horseman. It may have been inspired, at least in part, by the rumored discovery of a headless corpse in the area after the Revolutionary War Battle of White Plains

statement.id: Cerita pendek Washington Irving The Legend of Sleepy Hollow menampilkan tokoh bernama Penunggang Kuda Tanpa Kepala; tokoh itu mungkin terinspirasi, setidaknya sebagian, oleh kabar penemuan mayat tanpa kepala di daerah itu setelah Pertempuran White Plains dalam Perang Revolusi.
statement.en: Washington Irving's short story The Legend of Sleepy Hollow features a character known as the Headless Horseman, which may have been inspired, at least in part, by the rumored discovery of a headless corpse in the area after the Revolutionary War Battle of White Plains.

claims.quote: Then again, Irving was probably familiar with the European folklore in which the figure of a headless rider has appeared since the Middle Ages. In any case, since its publication in 1820, Irving's Headless Horseman has become an integral part of American folklore.

statement.id: Namun Irving mungkin akrab dengan cerita rakyat Eropa tempat sosok penunggang tanpa kepala muncul sejak Abad Pertengahan; bagaimanapun, sejak terbit pada 1820, Penunggang Kuda Tanpa Kepala karya Irving menjadi bagian integral cerita rakyat Amerika.
statement.en: Irving was probably familiar with the European folklore in which the figure of a headless rider has appeared since the Middle Ages; in any case, since its publication in 1820, Irving's Headless Horseman has become an integral part of American folklore.

claims.quote: The Headless Horseman appears in "The Legend of Sleepy Hollow" segment of the 1949 film The Adventures of Ichabod and Mr. Toad.

statement.id: Penunggang Kuda Tanpa Kepala muncul dalam segmen 'The Legend of Sleepy Hollow' pada film The Adventures of Ichabod and Mr. Toad (1949).
statement.en: The Headless Horseman appears in 'The Legend of Sleepy Hollow' segment of the 1949 film The Adventures of Ichabod and Mr. Toad.

claims.quote: While the original story implies that the Horseman was merely Brom Bones in disguise, the film depicts him as an actual ghost.

statement.id: Sementara cerita aslinya menyiratkan bahwa sang Penunggang hanyalah Brom Bones yang menyamar, film itu menggambarkannya sebagai hantu sungguhan.
statement.en: While the original story implies that the Horseman was merely Brom Bones in disguise, the film depicts him as an actual ghost.

claims.quote: In the 1999 Tim Burton film Sleepy Hollow, the Headless Horseman is the ghost of a murderous Hessian mercenary (performed by Ray Park in Headless Horseman form and portrayed by Christopher Walken in his true form) summoned by Katrina Van Tassel's stepmother Lady Van Tassel to eliminate her enemies

statement.id: Dalam film Sleepy Hollow karya Tim Burton (1999), Penunggang Kuda Tanpa Kepala adalah hantu tentara bayaran Hessian pembunuh yang dipanggil Lady Van Tassel, ibu tiri Katrina Van Tassel, untuk melenyapkan musuh-musuhnya.
statement.en: In the 1999 Tim Burton film Sleepy Hollow, the Headless Horseman is the ghost of a murderous Hessian mercenary summoned by Katrina Van Tassel's stepmother Lady Van Tassel to eliminate her enemies.

claims.quote: The dominant spirit, however, that haunts this enchanted region, and seems to be commander-in-chief of all the powers of the air, is the apparition of a figure on horseback, without a head. It is said by some to be the ghost of a Hessian trooper, whose head had been carried away by a cannon-ball, in some nameless battle during the Revolutionary War

statement.id: Roh dominan yang menghantui wilayah terpesona itu, tampaknya panglima semua kekuatan udara, adalah penampakan sosok berkuda tanpa kepala, yang oleh sebagian orang dikatakan hantu seorang prajurit Hessian yang kepalanya terbawa bola meriam dalam pertempuran tanpa nama selama Perang Revolusi.
statement.en: The dominant spirit that haunts this enchanted region, seemingly commander-in-chief of all the powers of the air, is the apparition of a figure on horseback without a head, said by some to be the ghost of a Hessian trooper whose head had been carried away by a cannon-ball in some nameless battle during the Revolutionary War.

claims.quote: allege that the body of the trooper having been buried in the churchyard, the ghost rides forth to the scene of battle in nightly quest of his head, and that the rushing speed with which he sometimes passes along the Hollow, like a midnight blast, is owing to his being belated, and in a hurry to get back to the churchyard before daybreak.

statement.id: Menurut para penutur setempat, jasad prajurit itu dikubur di pemakaman gereja, dan hantunya berkuda ke medan pertempuran setiap malam mencari kepalanya; kecepatan menderunya di Hollow, seperti embusan angin tengah malam, karena ia terlambat dan terburu-buru kembali ke pemakaman sebelum fajar.
statement.en: According to local historians, the trooper's body was buried in the churchyard and the ghost rides forth to the scene of battle in nightly quest of his head; the rushing speed with which he passes along the Hollow like a midnight blast is owing to his being belated and in a hurry to get back to the churchyard before daybreak.

claims.quote: the spectre is known at all the country firesides, by the name of the Headless Horseman of Sleepy Hollow.

statement.id: Hantu itu dikenal di semua perapian pedesaan dengan nama Penunggang Kuda Tanpa Kepala dari Sleepy Hollow.
statement.en: The spectre is known at all the country firesides by the name of the Headless Horseman of Sleepy Hollow.

claims.quote: the Headless Horseman, who had been heard several times of late, patrolling the country; and, it was said, tethered his horse nightly among the graves in the churchyard.

statement.id: Penunggang Kuda Tanpa Kepala beberapa kali terdengar berpatroli di pedesaan dan konon menambatkan kudanya setiap malam di antara makam di pemakaman gereja.
statement.en: The Headless Horseman had been heard several times of late patrolling the country and, it was said, tethered his horse nightly among the graves in the churchyard.

claims.quote: The tale was told of old Brouwer, a most heretical disbeliever in ghosts, how he met the Horseman returning from his foray into Sleepy Hollow, and was obliged to get up behind him; ... when the Horseman suddenly turned into a skeleton, threw old Brouwer into the brook, and sprang away over the tree-tops with a clap of thunder.

statement.id: Dikisahkan tentang Brouwer tua, penentang hantu, yang bertemu Penunggang sepulang dari serangannya ke Sleepy Hollow dan terpaksa naik di belakangnya; sang Penunggang tiba-tiba berubah menjadi kerangka, melempar Brouwer ke sungai, dan melesat di atas pucuk pohon dengan gelegar petir.
statement.en: The tale was told of old Brouwer, a heretical disbeliever in ghosts, who met the Horseman returning from his foray into Sleepy Hollow and was obliged to get up behind him; the Horseman suddenly turned into a skeleton, threw Brouwer into the brook, and sprang away over the tree-tops with a clap of thunder.

claims.quote: Brom Bones, who made light of the Galloping Hessian as an arrant jockey. He affirmed that on returning one night from the neighboring village of Sing Sing, he had been overtaken by this midnight trooper; ... but just as they came to the church bridge, the Hessian bolted, and vanished in a flash of fire.

statement.id: Brom Bones, yang menganggap enteng sang Hessian Berderap sebagai joki ulung, menegaskan bahwa sepulang dari desa Sing Sing ia disusul prajurit tengah malam itu; tepat saat mereka tiba di jembatan gereja, sang Hessian kabur dan lenyap dalam kilatan api.
statement.en: Brom Bones, who made light of the Galloping Hessian as an arrant jockey, affirmed that returning one night from the village of Sing Sing he was overtaken by this midnight trooper; just as they came to the church bridge, the Hessian bolted and vanished in a flash of fire.

short_description.id: Imbunche adalah monster legendaris dalam cerita rakyat Pulau Chiloé di Chili selatan: manusia cacat berkepala terpelintir ke belakang yang menjaga pintu masuk gua seorang penyihir.
short_description.en: In the folklore of Chiloé Island in southern Chile, the imbunche is a legendary monster: a deformed human with a backward-twisted head that guards the entrance to a warlock's cave.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat dan mitologi Chilote dari Pulau Chiloé di Chili selatan, imbunche adalah monster legendaris yang menjaga pintu masuk gua seorang penyihir (brujo). Namanya berasal dari kata Mapudungun ifünche; satu sumber mengartikannya "orang pendek", sedangkan sumber lain "orang cacat bentuk". Di Chiloé makhluk ini juga disebut Machucho, Butamacho, atau Chivato.
long_description.en: In the Chilote folklore and mythology of Chiloé Island in southern Chile, the imbunche is a legendary monster that guards the entrance to a warlock's cave (a brujo). Its name comes from the Mapudungun word ifünche; one source translates it as "short person", another as "deformed person". In Chiloé it is also called Machucho, Butamacho or Chivato.

long_description.id: Imbunche digambarkan sebagai manusia cacat dengan kepala terpelintir ke belakang, juga lengan, jari, hidung, mulut, dan telinga yang terpelintir. Ia berjalan dengan satu kaki atau tiga kaki (satu kaki dan dua tangan) karena salah satu kakinya melekat di belakang leher; kulitnya biru dan giginya tajam. Ia tidak dapat berbicara dan hanya mengeluarkan bunyi parau yang tidak enak didengar. Sebuah kumpulan folklor menyebutnya mengembik seperti anak kambing, dan sumber itu juga menggambarkannya sebagai hewan yang berjalan dengan dua tangan dan satu kaki hanya pada malam hari.
long_description.en: The imbunche is pictured as a deformed human whose head is twisted backwards, along with twisted arms, fingers, nose, mouth and ears. It moves on one foot or three (one leg and two hands) because one leg is attached to the back of its neck; its skin is blue and its teeth are sharp. It cannot talk and only makes guttural, rough, unpleasant sounds. A folklore collection says it bleats like a young goat, and the same source also describes it as an animal that walks on two hands and one foot only at night.

long_description.id: Menurut legenda, imbunche adalah anak sulung berusia kurang dari sembilan hari yang diculik oleh atau dijual orangtuanya kepada seorang Brujo Chilote. Sang penyihir mengubahnya menjadi monster berbulu dengan mematahkan kaki kanannya dan memelintirnya ke punggung; pada usia tiga bulan lidahnya dibelah, giginya meruncing, dan kulitnya membiru, lalu krim ajaib dioleskan agar bulu tebal tumbuh. Menurut salah satu sumber, kepalanya juga dipipihkan dengan dua papan dan lidahnya dibelah menyerupai lidah ular. Sumber-sumber berbeda tentang makanannya, dari susu kucing hitam hingga daging dan darah bayi.
long_description.en: In the legend an imbunche starts out as a firstborn baby, not yet nine days old, who is abducted by a Brujo Chilote or handed over to one by the parents. The warlock makes it a hairy monster by breaking its right leg and twisting it over its back; at three months its tongue is forked, its teeth sharpen and its skin turns blue, and a magic cream is rubbed in so that thick hair grows. According to one source its head is also flattened between two boards and its tongue split like a serpent's. Sources differ on its food, from black cat's milk to the flesh and blood of infants.

long_description.id: Selain menjaga pintu gua, imbunche dipakai para penyihir sebagai alat balas dendam atau kutukan, dan kadang menjadi penasihat karena pengetahuan gaib yang diperolehnya selama menjaga gua. Ia hanya keluar dalam keadaan tertentu, misalnya saat gua dihancurkan atau ditemukan dan penyihir pindah ke gua lain; saat dibawa keluar ia meronta dan berteriak sehingga menakuti warga dan menandakan nasib buruk. Menurut legenda, perkumpulan para penyihir bekerja dari gua Cueva de Quicaví atau Casa Grande yang dijaga oleh imbunche.
long_description.en: Besides guarding the cave entrance, the imbunche is used by warlocks for revenge or curses and sometimes acts as an adviser because of the magical knowledge it gains while on guard. It leaves its post only rarely, for instance when the cave is wrecked or found and the warlock relocates; when it is taken out it struggles and shouts, frightening the townspeople and announcing misfortune. According to legend, the warlocks' society worked from the Cueva de Quicaví, or Casa Grande, which the imbunche guarded.

literal_meaning.id: Menurut satu sumber berarti "orang pendek"; menurut sumber lain "orang cacat bentuk".
literal_meaning.en: Translated as "short person" in one source and as "deformed person" in another.

who.id: Monster legendaris berupa manusia cacat, penjaga gua para penyihir Chiloé.

origin.id: Cerita rakyat Pulau Chiloé di Chili selatan.

famous_for.id: Tubuhnya yang sengaja dicacatkan: kepala terpelintir ke belakang dan satu kaki melekat di belakang leher.

claims.quote: In the Chilote folklore and Chilote mythology of Chiloé Island in southern Chile, the imbunche (Mapudungun: ifünche, lit. "short person") is a legendary monster that protects the entrance to a warlock's cave.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat dan mitologi Chilote dari Pulau Chiloé di Chili selatan, imbunche (Mapudungun: ifünche, "orang pendek") adalah monster legendaris yang melindungi pintu masuk gua seorang penyihir.
statement.en: In the Chilote folklore and mythology of Chiloé Island in southern Chile, the imbunche (Mapudungun: ifünche, "short person") is a legendary monster that protects the entrance to a warlock's cave.

claims.quote: The imbunche is a deformed human with its head twisted backwards, along with having twisted arms, fingers, nose, mouth and ears.

statement.id: Imbunche adalah manusia cacat dengan kepala terpelintir ke belakang serta anggota tubuh yang bengkok.
statement.en: The imbunche is a deformed human with head twisted backwards and twisted limbs.

claims.quote: According to legend, the imbunche is a first-born child less than nine days old that was kidnapped by, or sold by their parents to, a Brujo Chilote

statement.id: Menurut legenda, imbunche adalah bayi sulung yang diculik atau dijual kepada penyihir Brujo Chilote.
statement.en: According to lore, it is a newborn child kidnapped by or sold to a Brujo Chilote warlock.

claims.quote: The creature walks on one foot or on three feet (actually one leg and two hands) because one of its legs is attached to the back of its neck. It has blue skin and sharp teeth.

statement.id: Makhluk ini berjalan dengan satu kaki atau tiga kaki (sebenarnya satu kaki dan dua tangan) karena salah satu kakinya melekat di belakang lehernya. Kulitnya biru dan giginya tajam.
statement.en: The creature walks on one foot or three feet (actually one leg and two hands) because one of its legs is attached to the back of its neck. It has blue skin and sharp teeth.

claims.quote: The imbunche cannot talk, and communicates only by guttural, rough and unpleasant sounds.

statement.id: Imbunche tidak dapat berbicara dan hanya berkomunikasi dengan bunyi parau, kasar, dan tidak enak didengar.
statement.en: The imbunche cannot talk and communicates only through guttural, rough and unpleasant sounds.

claims.quote: The Brujo chilote transforms the child into a deformed hairy monster by breaking their right leg and twisting it over their back. When the child is three months old their tongue is forked, their teeth turn sharp, their skin turns blue, and the warlock applies a magic cream over the child's back to cause thick hairs.

statement.id: Brujo chilote mengubah anak itu menjadi monster cacat berbulu dengan mematahkan kaki kanannya dan memelintirnya ke punggung. Pada usia tiga bulan lidahnya dibelah, giginya meruncing, kulitnya membiru, dan sang penyihir mengoleskan krim ajaib di punggungnya agar tumbuh bulu tebal.
statement.en: The Brujo chilote turns the child into a deformed hairy monster by breaking its right leg and twisting it over its back. At three months its tongue is forked, its teeth become sharp, its skin turns blue, and the warlock applies a magic cream to its back to make thick hair grow.

claims.quote: Besides guarding the entrance to the warlock's cave, the imbunche is used by warlocks as an instrument for revenge or curses. And, because it has acquired magical knowledge over its lifetime spent guarding the cave, even if the imbunche is not initiated into wizardry, it sometimes acts as the warlock's advisor.

statement.id: Selain menjaga pintu masuk gua penyihir, imbunche dipakai para penyihir sebagai alat balas dendam atau kutukan. Karena memperoleh pengetahuan gaib selama menjaga gua, ia kadang menjadi penasihat sang penyihir meski tidak diinisiasi dalam ilmu sihir.
statement.en: Besides guarding the entrance to the warlock's cave, the imbunche is used by warlocks as an instrument of revenge or curses. Because it gains magical knowledge while guarding the cave, it sometimes acts as the warlock's advisor even though it is not initiated into wizardry.

claims.quote: The imbunche leaves the cave only in certain circumstances, such as when the cave is destroyed or discovered and the warlock moves to another cave, or when the warlocks have need of it and carry it thrashing and yelling, scaring the townspeople and announcing misfortune to come.

statement.id: Imbunche meninggalkan gua hanya dalam keadaan tertentu, misalnya saat gua dihancurkan atau ditemukan dan sang penyihir pindah ke gua lain, atau saat para penyihir membutuhkannya dan membawanya keluar sambil meronta dan berteriak, menakuti warga dan menandakan nasib buruk yang akan datang.
statement.en: The imbunche leaves the cave only in certain circumstances, such as when the cave is destroyed or discovered and the warlock moves to another cave, or when the warlocks need it and carry it out thrashing and yelling, frightening the townspeople and announcing misfortune to come.

claims.quote: During its first months the imbunche is fed on black cat's milk and goat flesh, and when old enough, with human corpses from cemeteries.

statement.id: Pada bulan-bulan pertama imbunche diberi susu kucing hitam dan daging kambing, dan setelah cukup besar diberi mayat manusia dari pemakaman.
statement.en: During its first months the imbunche is fed black cat's milk and goat flesh and, when old enough, human corpses from cemeteries.

claims.quote: José Donoso's magical realist novel The Obscene Bird of Night reinterprets imbunche folklore as a way to bind a male child in a sack to prevent escape and bodily growth.

statement.id: Novel realisme magis José Donoso, The Obscene Bird of Night, menafsir ulang cerita rakyat imbunche sebagai cara mengikat anak laki-laki dalam karung untuk mencegah pelarian dan pertumbuhan tubuh.
statement.en: José Donoso's magical realist novel The Obscene Bird of Night reinterprets imbunche folklore as a way of binding a male child in a sack to prevent escape and bodily growth.

claims.quote: El invunche o imbunche (del mapudungun ifünche: "persona deforme") es un ser de la mitología mapuche y de la mitología chilota. En Chiloé también recibe el nombre de Machucho, Butamacho o Chivato.

statement.id: Invunche atau imbunche (dari kata Mapudungun ifünche, "persona deforme" atau orang cacat bentuk) adalah makhluk dari mitologi Mapuche dan mitologi Chilote. Di Chiloé ia juga disebut Machucho, Butamacho, atau Chivato.
statement.en: The invunche or imbunche (from Mapudungun ifünche, "persona deforme", a deformed person) is a being of Mapuche and Chilote mythology. In Chiloé it is also called Machucho, Butamacho or Chivato.

claims.quote: se aplastaría su cabeza con un par de tablas y torcerían su cabeza en el proceso para darle una forma alargada. Por último le partirían la lengua en dos, para imitar la lengua de las serpientes.

statement.id: Kepalanya dipipihkan dengan dua papan dan dipelintir sehingga berbentuk memanjang; terakhir lidahnya dibelah dua untuk meniru lidah ular.
statement.en: Its head would be flattened with a pair of boards and twisted in the process to give it an elongated shape; finally its tongue would be split in two to imitate the tongue of snakes.

claims.quote: Después de este ritual, deben alimentar al nuevo Invunche de una manera especial; primeramente le darían leche de gata negra o leche de una nodriza indígena, luego cuando tiene dientes, le darían carne de "cabrito" (refiriéndose a carne de niño recién nacido), y cuando es más adulto le darían carne de "chivo" (refiriéndose a carne de persona adulta).

statement.id: Setelah ritual itu, imbunche baru diberi makan secara khusus: pertama susu kucing hitam atau susu inang Pribumi, lalu setelah bergigi daging "cabrito" (maksudnya daging bayi baru lahir), dan setelah lebih dewasa daging "chivo" (maksudnya daging orang dewasa).
statement.en: After this ritual the new Invunche must be fed in a special way: first black cat's milk or the milk of an indigenous wet nurse, then, once it has teeth, "cabrito" meat (meaning the flesh of a newborn child), and when it is older "chivo" meat (meaning the flesh of an adult person).

claims.quote: ser humano que se sostiene en un pie y el otro lo lleva pegado a la espalda; por esta causa, anda a saltitos. Tiene los brazos torcidos y la cara vuelta hacia

statement.id: Imbunche adalah manusia yang bertumpu pada satu kaki sementara kaki lainnya melekat di punggung, sehingga ia berjalan melompat-lompat kecil. Lengannya terpelintir dan wajahnya menghadap ke belakang.
statement.en: The Imbunche is a human being who stands on one foot while the other is stuck to the back, so it moves in little hops. Its arms are twisted and its face is turned backward.

claims.quote: No habla, bala como un chivato, pero en una forma extraordinaria. ... el nombre de Chivato de la cueva.

statement.id: Imbunche tidak berbicara; ia mengembik seperti anak kambing dengan cara yang luar biasa. Ia juga dinamai Chivato de la cueva.
statement.en: It does not speak; it bleats like a young goat in an extraordinary way. It is also called Chivato de la cueva.

claims.quote: Para lograr esta figura humana, los brujos emplean un ... de corta edad, y a medida que va creciendo se le acomodan los ... hasta que quedan dispuestos para su finalidad. Lo alimentan con carne y sangre de

statement.id: Untuk memperoleh sosok manusia ini, para penyihir memakai seorang anak kecil; seiring ia tumbuh, organ-organnya ditata hingga sesuai tujuannya. Ia diberi makan daging dan darah bayi yang baru lahir.
statement.en: To obtain this human figure the warlocks use a young child, and as it grows its organs are arranged until they suit its purpose. It is fed with the flesh and blood of a newborn child.

claims.quote: Unicamente sale cuando ... se cambia o ha sido destruida. Generalmente, es llevado en hombros, cuando hay traslado.

statement.id: Imbunche hanya keluar ketika gua dipindahkan atau telah dihancurkan; umumnya ia dipanggul di bahu ketika terjadi pemindahan.
statement.en: It leaves only when the cave is changed or has been destroyed; it is generally carried on shoulders when there is a move.

claims.quote: El Imbunche, o Invunche, es, ... Vuta o Vutamacho y algunos lo llaman Machucho, pero lo describen como un animal que bala como cabro y que anda con las dos manos y un pie, ... por la noche.

statement.id: Imbunche atau Invunche juga disebut Vuta atau Vutamacho, dan sebagian menyebutnya Machucho, tetapi mereka menggambarkannya sebagai hewan yang mengembik seperti kambing dan berjalan dengan dua tangan dan satu kaki, hanya pada malam hari.
statement.en: The Imbunche, or Invunche, is also Vuta or Vutamacho, and some call it Machucho, but describe it as an animal that bleats like a goat and walks on two hands and one foot, only at night.

claims.quote: The seat of the King was in the Cueva de Quicaví or Casa Grande, in the surroundings of Quicaví, in the commune of Quemchi. According to legend, the society worked out of a cave that was guarded by a deformed being, the Imbunche.

statement.id: Menurut legenda, perkumpulan para penyihir bekerja dari sebuah gua, Cueva de Quicaví atau Casa Grande, yang dijaga oleh makhluk cacat bernama Imbunche.
statement.en: According to legend, the warlocks' society worked out of a cave, the Cueva de Quicaví or Casa Grande, which was guarded by a deformed being, the Imbunche.

ONE original square premium painterly cinematic Mythics illustration of Imbunche, the deformed blue-skinned hairy guardian of the warlock cave in Chilote folklore.
ANATOMY: one backwards-facing twisted head, two eyes, sharp teeth and forked tongue; exactly two twisted arms with hands on ground, one supporting left leg, the right leg bent over its back and attached behind the neck; blue skin and thick back hair; opaque ragged waist covering [imbunche-c02,imbunche-c04,imbunche-c06]
MOMENT: REAR THREE-QUARTER VIEW: the creature crouches FACING AWAY from the camera toward the cave. Its broad hairy BACK AND DISTINCT SHOULDER BLADES face the viewer, no chest or belly facing camera. Its human head is twisted a full 180 DEGREES BACKWARD so its face looks BACK OVER ITS OWN SPINE directly at the viewer. Show the neck twist explicitly between the shoulder blades. Two hands and its left foot support the body. The RIGHT THIGH starts at its hip and bends upward across the furry back, the right shin runs up its spine, and the right FOOT ENDS ATTACHED BEHIND THE NECK beside the backwards face. No extra feet, no normal head orientation, no front-facing torso. The creature growls and braces to turn its body toward the viewer.
POWER: No visible magic; claws scrape wet stone and its mouth opens in a guttural warning [imbunche-c05]
SCALE & CAMERA: extreme low angle; close dramatic foreshortening; subject fills almost the entire square frame, distinguishable anatomy immediately readable; no invented giant size.
LIGHT & WEATHER: one dominant moonlight source, strong rim light, deep walnut shadows and antique gold highlights, airborne spray or dust only where physical action causes it.
SURFACE: tactile rough fur, feather, scale, fabric or wet skin appropriate to the stated anatomy; strong painterly material detail, never plastic.
SETTING: the Cueva de Quicavi warlock cave entrance on Chiloe [imbunche-c01,imbunche-c19]
MOOD: dangerous and imposing or respectfully awe-inspiring for sacred beings; decisive action, never cute, calm or decorative.
HARD CONSTRAINTS: no text, lettering, logo, border, frame or watermark; no extra heads, limbs or fingers; no design borrowed from film, game, anime or comic; no nudity or explicit gore; no generic glow aura, neon outline, energy ribbons or floating runes. Output one square PNG at least 1024x1024.
TARGETED ANATOMY EDIT OF REFERENCE: Keep the creature with BACK facing the viewer and both hands plus one foot on ground. MIRROR the whole body arrangement horizontally so the raised bound leg is the creatures anatomical RIGHT LEG, on the RIGHT side of a rear view; the supporting left leg is on the left. Then rotate ONLY the head a full 180 degrees so the FACE LOOKS STRAIGHT BACK AT THE VIEWER, centered between shoulder blades, with TWO EYES FULLY VISIBLE and no side profile. The chest must still face away. Show the twisted neck continuously joined to the body and one foot attached behind that neck. Keep exactly two arms, two legs, one head; keep blue skin, sharp teeth, forked tongue, hairy back, opaque loincloth and the cave. No gore or injury depiction. Head-on face on a back-facing body is the crucial identity.

text.id: Dikaitkan dengan masa Kerajaan Kutai; Raja Mulawarman, yang menurut kepercayaan menunggangi lembuswana secara spiritual, memerintah sekitar 1.500 tahun silam.
text.en: Associated with the Kutai kingdom; King Mulawarman, said to ride the lembuswana spiritually, ruled about 1,500 years ago.

cultural_context.id: Lembuswana dipandang sebagai simbol keperkasaan dan kekuasaan Raja Kutai; menurut arsip keluarga yang dikutip jurnal, belalai dan gading gajahnya bermakna bahwa raja harus berwibawa dan disegani rakyat. Ia memiliki falsafah Paksi Liman Jonggo Yokso, yaitu bahwa seseorang seharusnya bersifat mulia sebagai pengayom rakyat; mahkotanya dapat diartikan sebagai kekuasaan dan belalainya menggambarkan Dewa Ganesha, dewa kecerdasan.
cultural_context.en: The lembuswana is seen as a symbol of the might and power of the King of Kutai; according to a family archive cited in a journal, its elephant trunk and tusks mean that a king must have authority and be respected by his people. It carries the philosophy Paksi Liman Jonggo Yokso: one should be noble as protector of the people; its crown can be read as power and its trunk represents the god Ganesha, god of intelligence.

short_description.id: Lembuswana adalah satwa mitologi rakyat Kutai yang berwujud lembu keemasan bermahkota, berbelalai gajah, bersayap garuda, bertaji ayam, dan bersisik naga, lambang Kerajaan Kutai hingga Kesultanan Kutai Kartanegara.
short_description.en: The lembuswana is a mythical beast of the Kutai people, a golden crowned bull with an elephant's trunk, garuda wings, rooster spurs and dragon scales, emblem of the Kutai kingdom through the Sultanate of Kutai Kartanegara.

long_description.id: Lembuswana adalah satwa dalam mitologi kuno rakyat Kutai yang kemudian menjadi lambang sejak masa Kerajaan Kutai, kerajaan Hindu tertua, hingga Kesultanan Kutai Kartanegara Ing Martadipura. Ia dianggap suci karena dipercaya sebagai tunggangan Dewa Wishnu, dan menurut artikel jurnal, ia merupakan simbol keperkasaan dan kekuasaan Raja Kutai. Namanya disebut berasal dari bahasa Sansekerta: lembu, yang berarti sapi, dan svarna, yang berarti emas; arsip keluarga yang dikutip sebuah jurnal menafsirkan "lembu" dan "suwana" dengan makna lain.
long_description.en: The lembuswana is a creature of the ancient mythology of the Kutai people that became an emblem from the time of the Kutai kingdom, the oldest Hindu kingdom, to the Sultanate of Kutai Kartanegara Ing Martadipura. It is considered sacred because it is believed to be the mount of the god Vishnu, and according to a journal article it is a symbol of the might and power of the King of Kutai. Its name is said to come from Sanskrit: lembu, meaning cow, and svarna, meaning gold; a family archive cited in a journal reads "lembu" and "suwana" differently.

long_description.id: Lembuswana berwarna keemasan dan berwujud lembu yang bermahkota, berbelalai dan bergading seperti gajah, bersayap seperti garuda, berkuku dan bertaji seperti ayam jantan, serta bersisik seperti naga. Penggambaran lain menyebutnya bertaring seperti harimau dan bertubuh seperti kuda. Hewan ini diyakini memiliki kekuatan luar biasa dan dapat hidup di darat, air, maupun udara; dalam riwayat yang dikutip jurnal, ia dapat terbang secepat kilat di angkasa. Menurut kepercayaan masyarakat, ia adalah kendaraan Batara Guru sekaligus kendaraan spiritual Raja Mulawarman. Seorang penulis karya tugas akhir menyimpulkan bahwa ia adalah tunggangan sakral para dewa yang patuh, abdi yang setia, serta kuat dan perkasa.
long_description.en: The lembuswana is golden and bull-shaped, wearing a crown, with an elephant's trunk and tusks, wings like a garuda, a rooster's claws and spurs and scales like a dragon. Other descriptions give it fangs like a tiger and a body like a horse. The animal is believed to have extraordinary power and to be able to live on land, in water and in the air; in the account cited in a journal it can fly as fast as lightning through the sky. By popular belief it is the vehicle of Batara Guru and the spiritual vehicle of King Mulawarman. The author of a final-project paper concludes that it is a sacred steed of the gods, docile, a faithful servant, strong and mighty.

long_description.id: Lembuswana dipercaya menjaga Sungai Mahakam dari bahaya, memastikan airnya tetap bersih, dan membantu nelayan menemukan tempat menangkap ikan. Legenda kemunculannya dari dasar sungai dihubungkan dengan kelahiran Putri Karang Melenuyang. Dalam De Kroniek van Koetai, seorang anak berbaring di atas gong yang dijunjung seekor naga, dan naga itu dijunjung Lembusuana yang berdiri di atas batu. Dalam cerita rakyat Kutai, naga itu disebut Ular Lembu, dan peristiwa itu digelar kembali setiap tahun pada upacara Erau.
long_description.en: The lembuswana is believed to guard the Mahakam River from danger, keep its water clean and help fishermen find fishing spots. The legend of its emergence from the river bed is tied to the birth of Princess Karang Melenuyang. In De Kroniek van Koetai, a child lies on a gong carried by a dragon, and the dragon is carried by Lembusuana standing on a rock. In Kutai folk tales the dragon is called Ular Lembu, and the event is re-enacted every year at the Erau ceremony.

long_description.id: Lembuswana memiliki falsafah Paksi Liman Jonggo Yokso, yaitu bahwa seseorang seharusnya bersifat mulia sebagai pengayom rakyat; mahkotanya dapat diartikan sebagai kekuasaan dan belalainya menggambarkan Dewa Ganesha. Menurut Dr. W. Kern, Lembusuana diukir berwarna di atas kulit kerbau yang disimpan di keraton Kutai sebagai pusaka. Patung lembuswana berdiri di halaman depan Museum Mulawarman di Tenggarong, tempat sepasang arca Lembusuana dari gangsa keemasan juga dapat dilihat. Menurut sebuah artikel jurnal, patung-patung lembuswana dibuat di Birma pada 1850, lalu sampai di istana Kutai Kartanegara pada 1900. Patung lembuswana raksasa karya I Nyoman Nuarta juga berdiri di Pulau Kumala; konon patung duduk di sana dianggap merusak filosofi Lembusuana yang berdiri gagah berani.
long_description.en: The lembuswana carries the philosophy Paksi Liman Jonggo Yokso: one should be noble as protector of the people; its crown can be read as power and its trunk represents the god Ganesha. According to Dr. W. Kern, Lembusuana was carved in colour on buffalo hide kept in the Kutai palace as a heirloom. A lembuswana statue stands in front of the Mulawarman Museum in Tenggarong, where a pair of golden-bronze Lembusuana statues can also be seen. A journal article says the statues were made in Burma in 1850 and reached the Kutai Kartanegara palace in 1900. A giant lembuswana statue by I Nyoman Nuarta also stands on Pulau Kumala; it is said that a seated statue there was seen as damaging the philosophy of Lembusuana, who stands bravely.
