short_description.id: Naga berperan penting dalam kisah legenda, sastra, mitologi, dan agama Meitei di Manipur, dari naga-singa penjaga Kangla Sha hingga naga-ular seperti Poubi Lai dan Taoroinai.
short_description.en: Dragons play a significant role in the legends, literature, mythology and religion of the Meitei of Manipur, from the guardian dragon lion Kangla Sha to dragon serpents such as Poubi Lai and Taoroinai.

long_description.id: Naga memiliki peran penting dalam kisah legenda, sastra, mitologi, dan agama Meitei di Manipur. Tradisi ini mengenal beberapa tokoh naga: Kangla Sha, naga-singa penjaga Istana Kangla yang biasanya digambarkan berpasangan; Nongshaba, naga-singa yang selalu tetap berwujud makhluk mitos; Poubi Lai, naga-ular tiran dari Danau Loktak; dan Taoroinai, naga-ular di samudra kosmik yang menurunkan telur langit ilahi ke bumi.
long_description.en: Dragons play a significant role in the legendary accounts, literature, mythology and religion of the Meitei in Manipur. The tradition knows several dragon figures: Kangla Sha, the guardian dragon lion of the Kangla Palace, usually depicted in pairs; Nongshaba, a dragon lion that always remains in the form of the mythical beast; Poubi Lai, the tyrant dragon serpent of Loktak Lake; and Taoroinai, a dragon serpent of the cosmic ocean that brought the divine celestial egg down to earth.

long_description.id: Pakhangba, putra bungsu Leimarel Sidabi, diberi takhta alam semesta oleh ayahnya Atingkok dan dapat mengubah dirinya menjadi naga berbentuk ular maupun manusia. Sebuah sumber menyebut legenda bahwa ia dapat berubah menjadi ular, dan catatan lain menyebut kepercayaan bahwa ia masih kadang menampakkan diri kepada manusia dalam wujud ular. Karena kekuatan ilahinya untuk bergerak pada malam hari sebagai naga, ia juga dikenal sebagai Sanahing Pakhangba. Catatan sejarah juga memuliakan Pakhangba sebagai raja-dewa Manipur. Dalam kutipan catatan lama di salah satu sumber, ular Pakung-ba disebut dewa khusus raja yang diklaim sebagai leluhur keluarga kerajaan, dan ukurannya yang besar dianggap tanda ia tidak senang, sedangkan wujud kecil menandakan suasana hatinya baik.
long_description.en: Pakhangba, youngest son of Leimarel Sidabi, was given the throne of the universe by his father Atingkok and could change himself into both a serpentine dragon and a human. One source reports legends that he could change his shape into a snake, and another reports a belief that he still sometimes appears to men in the form of a snake. Because of his divine power to move about at night as a dragon he is also known as Sanahing Pakhangba. Historical records also glorify Pakhangba as a God-king of Manipur. In an older account quoted in one source, the Pakung-ba snake is the Raja's peculiar god from which the royal family claims descent, and its appearing of great size is taken as a sign of displeasure while a small form means good humour.

long_description.id: Lambang naga juga hadir dalam kehidupan kerajaan. Raja-raja Manipur menggunakan naga untuk melambangkan lambang kerajaan, dan patung Kangla-Sha di pintu masuk istana menjadi tempat kehormatan bagi upacara kerajaan. Naga-naga batu bernama Nongsha pernah berdiri di depan Kangla atau Balai Penobatan. Perahu pacu Hiyang Hiren sering dibuat berbentuk naga, dan banyak legenda menyebutnya memiliki kekuatan spiritual.
long_description.en: The dragon image also appears in royal life. The kings of Manipur used the dragon to represent the royal insignia, and statues of Kangla-Sha at the palace entrance were a place of pride for royal ceremonies. Stone dragons called the Nongsha once stood before the Kangla or Coronation Hall. The Hiyang Hiren race boat is often built in the shape of a dragon, and many legends say it possesses spiritual powers.

short_description.id: Ratoshikamuy adalah kamuy gurita raksasa dalam cerita rakyat Ainu, yang beradu kekuatan dengan burung raksasa Huri di muara Sungai Ishikari.
short_description.en: Ratoshikamuy is a giant octopus kamuy in Ainu folktales that contested its strength with the giant bird Huri at the mouth of the Ishikari River.

long_description.id: Ratoshikamuy (ラートシカムイ) adalah gurita raksasa dalam cerita rakyat Ainu, ditulis juga Rādoshikamuy. Namanya berarti "dewa yang memiliki banyak ekor". Kisah tentangnya diwariskan sebagai legenda asal nama tempat yang berkaitan dengan Ishikari.
long_description.en: Ratoshikamuy (ラートシカムイ) is a giant octopus in Ainu folktales, also written Rādoshikamuy. Its name means "the god with many tails". The tale about it is handed down as a place-name legend connected with Ishikari.

long_description.id: Menurut kisah itu, yang terkuat di laut adalah Ratoshikamuy dan yang terkuat di darat adalah burung raksasa Huri yang satu sayapnya sepanjang tujuh ri. Keduanya berseteru karena saling membanggakan kekuatan, lalu bertemu di muara Sungai Ishikari. Gurita itu menyemburkan tinta dan melotot marah, sedangkan Huri membentangkan sayap, mematuk tentakel yang muncul di atas air, dan mencoba menariknya dari laut tanpa membuat kepalanya muncul.
long_description.en: According to the tale, the strongest in the sea was Ratoshikamuy and the strongest on land was the giant bird Huri, one of whose wings is seven ri long. They were at odds because each boasted of its strength, and they met at the mouth of the Ishikari River. The octopus spat ink and glared in anger, while Huri spread its wings, pecked at the tentacles above the water and tried to haul it out of the sea without its head ever surfacing.

long_description.id: Kemudian gurita itu menarik balik dengan menekuk tentakelnya, tetapi burung itu bertahan, dan kekuatan keduanya seimbang sehingga tidak ada yang menang. Dikatakan bahwa ketika Huri hampir tertarik ke dalam laut, ia menggerakkan bulu ekornya (isi) ke kiri dan kanan (kari) untuk bertahan, sehingga laut di sekitar situ disebut Ishikari.
long_description.en: Then the octopus pulled back by bending its tentacles, but the bird held its ground, and the two were evenly matched so that neither prevailed. It is handed down that when Huri was almost drawn into the sea it braced itself by moving its tail feathers (ishi) left and right (kari), and so the sea there came to be called Ishikari.

cultural_context.id: Kisah Ratoshikamuy dan Huri Kamuy diwariskan sebagai legenda asal nama tempat yang berkaitan dengan Ishikari.
cultural_context.en: The tale of Ratoshikamuy and Huri Kamuy is handed down as a place-name legend connected with Ishikari.

claims.quote: こんどは蛸が押収して、触手を折り曲げて引っ張ったが、鳥はふんばって耐えた（詳細は、「石狩」地名由来とまとめて後述）。けっきょく力は両者とも互角で、決着がつくことはなかったという。

statement.id: Kemudian gurita itu menarik balik dengan menekuk tentakelnya, tetapi burung itu bertahan; kekuatan keduanya seimbang dan pertandingan tidak berakhir dengan pemenang.
statement.en: Then the octopus pulled back by bending its tentacles, but the bird held its ground; the two were evenly matched and the contest was never settled.

claims.quote: 石狩にまつわる地名伝説として、ラートシカムイと巨鳥フリカムイ（原文では「フリー」）の力比べ

statement.id: Adu kekuatan antara Ratoshikamuy dan burung raksasa Huri Kamuy (dalam teks aslinya "Furi") diceritakan sebagai legenda asal nama tempat yang berkaitan dengan Ishikari.
statement.en: A contest of strength between Ratoshikamuy and the giant bird Huri Kamuy (written "Furi" in the original text) is told as a place-name legend connected with Ishikari.

claims.quote: ラートシカムイ（ラードシカムイ）は、アイヌ民話に伝わる巨大な蛸。 ... ラートシカムイは「尾がたくさんある神」の意。

statement.id: Ratoshikamuy (juga ditulis Radoshikamuy / ラードシカムイ) adalah gurita raksasa dalam kisah rakyat Ainu, dan namanya berarti "dewa yang memiliki banyak ekor" (尾がたくさんある神).
statement.en: Ratoshikamuy (also written Radoshikamuy / ラードシカムイ) is a giant octopus in Ainu folktales, and its name means "the god with many tails" (尾がたくさんある神).

claims.quote: フリカムイが海中に引き込まれた際、尾羽（アイヌ語でイシ）を左右に動かして（アイヌ語でカリ）ふんばったため、その付近の海を石狩（いしかり）と呼ぶようになったと言い伝わる。

statement.id: Dikatakan bahwa ketika Huri Kamuy hampir tertarik ke dalam laut, ia menggerakkan bulu ekornya (isi dalam bahasa Ainu) ke kiri dan kanan (kari) untuk bertahan, sehingga laut di sekitar situ disebut Ishikari (石狩).
statement.en: It is handed down that when Huri Kamuy was pulled into the sea it braced itself by moving its tail feathers (ishi in Ainu) left and right (kari), and so the sea in that area came to be called Ishikari (石狩).

claims.quote: A giant octopus also occurs in Ainu lore under the name of Rātoshikamui (ラートシカムイ, Ainu romanization unverified, but meaning "many-tailed god" in Ainu).

statement.id: Wikipedia bahasa Inggris, dalam artikel Akkorokamui, mencatat bahwa seekor gurita raksasa juga muncul dalam tradisi Ainu dengan nama Rātoshikamui, yang berarti "dewa berekor banyak" dalam bahasa Ainu (romanisasi Ainu-nya belum diverifikasi).
statement.en: English Wikipedia, in its Akkorokamui article, notes that a giant octopus also occurs in Ainu lore under the name Rātoshikamui, meaning "many-tailed god" in Ainu (the Ainu romanization is unverified).

claims.quote: The Rādoshikamui (ラードシカムイ, variant pronunciation) purported to be the strongest being of the sea, while the land champion, the  huri bird measured 7 ri (27.5km), and they were at odds with each other over their boast.

statement.id: Wikipedia bahasa Inggris mencatat ucapan varian Rādoshikamui (ラードシカムイ) sebagai makhluk yang mengaku terkuat di laut, sedangkan juara di darat adalah burung huri yang lebarnya 7 ri (27,5 km), dan keduanya berseteru karena saling membanggakan diri.
statement.en: English Wikipedia records the variant pronunciation Rādoshikamui (ラードシカムイ), which claimed to be the strongest being of the sea, while the land champion was the huri bird measuring 7 ri (27.5 km), and the two were at odds over their boasts.

claims.quote: An onomastic tale concerning Ishikari explains that the name derived from the effort the huri put out with its tail-feathers in a match of strength against the giant octopus monster Rātoshikamui (ラートシカムイ; Ainu romanization unverified).

statement.id: Wikipedia bahasa Inggris, dalam artikel Huri, mencatat kisah asal nama Ishikari: nama itu berasal dari usaha huri mengerahkan bulu ekornya dalam adu kekuatan melawan gurita raksasa Rātoshikamui.
statement.en: English Wikipedia, in its Huri article, records an onomastic tale of Ishikari explaining that the name derived from the effort the huri put out with its tail-feathers in a match of strength against the giant octopus Rātoshikamui.

gaps.searched: Belum ada berkas Wikimedia Commons yang diperiksa untuk entri ini.

Dicari: Kotobank (tidak ada entri ラートシカムイ; entri フリカムイ hanya membahas burungnya), Yokai.com (tidak ada), situs resmi Kota Ishikari (tidak membahas kisah ini), Batchelor "The Ainu and their folk-lore" di archive.org (tidak memuat nama Ratoshikamuy; hanya satu kisah "devil-fish" tanpa nama), Wikipedia bahasa Inggris (artikel Akkorokamui dan Huri, dipakai). Sumber primer kisah ini, Sarashina Genzō "Ainu Densetsushū" (1971), tidak bisa dibaca terbuka.
Romanisasi bahasa Ainu nama ini belum diverifikasi (Wikipedia bahasa Inggris mencatat hal yang sama); hanya ejaan katakana yang dipakai.

short_description.id: Sundel bolong adalah hantu perempuan dalam mitos Nusantara: berambut panjang hitam, bergaun putih, dan berlubang tembus di punggungnya.
short_description.en: The sundel bolong is a female ghost of Indonesian lore with long black hair, a white dress, and a hole pierced through her back.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Indonesia, sundel bolong adalah hantu perempuan dari Nusantara yang digambarkan cantik, berambut panjang hitam, dan bergaun putih panjang, mirip pontianak. Ciri pembedanya adalah lubang besar di punggungnya yang tembus ke depan sehingga organ perut terlihat; lubang itu sedikit tertutup rambut panjangnya. Banyak orang menyangkanya sama dengan kuntilanak, dan mitosnya juga menjadi umum di Malaysia setelah dibawa para pendatang dari Nusantara. Di Belitung ia disebut Buruk Punggung.
long_description.en: In Indonesian mythology, the sundel bolong is a female ghost of the archipelago, pictured as a beautiful woman with long black hair and a long white dress, similar to the pontianak. What sets her apart is a large hole in her back that goes through to the front so that abdominal organs are visible; the hole is slightly covered by her long hair. Many people think she is the same as the kuntilanak, and her myth also became common in Malaysia after migrants from the archipelago brought it. In Belitung she is called Buruk Punggung.

long_description.id: Namanya berasal dari sundal, yang berarti pelacur, dan bolong, kata Jawa yang berarti berlubang tembus. Satu sumber menyebut letak lubang itu bergantung pada luka terakhir saat ia meninggal, sedangkan kisah lain menjelaskan bahwa lubang itu terbentuk karena bayi keluar dari punggungnya saat ia bersalin.
long_description.en: Her name comes from sundal, meaning prostitute, and bolong, a Javanese word meaning pierced through. One source says the position of the hole depends on the last wound at death, while another account explains the hole as formed when the baby came out of her back in childbirth.

long_description.id: Menurut cerita rakyat, sundel bolong adalah arwah perempuan yang meninggal saat hamil di luar nikah sehingga melahirkan di dalam kubur, atau yang meninggal saat bersalin. Versi lain menyebutnya arwah penasaran perempuan yang mati karena diperkosa lalu melahirkan di kubur. Korbannya terutama laki-laki dan anak-anak; ia dikatakan mengebiri laki-laki yang menolaknya dan mengambil bayi baru lahir sebagai pengganti anaknya yang hilang.
long_description.en: In folklore, the sundel bolong is the spirit of a woman who died pregnant outside marriage and so gave birth in her grave, or who died in childbirth. Another version describes her as the restless spirit of a woman who died after being raped and then gave birth in the grave. Her victims are mainly men and children; she is said to castrate men who reject her and to take newborns to replace her lost child.

long_description.id: Hantu ini dikatakan sering menjelma sebagai wanita cantik yang berjalan sendirian di jalan sunyi, dan menurut mitos ia sangat malu pada lubang di badannya serta selalu berusaha menutupinya. Ia sering menampakkan diri kepada laki-laki di tempat ia dibunuh sebagai peringatan. Ada pula dugaan bahwa mitos ini disebarkan untuk melindungi perempuan yang berjalan sendirian pada malam hari di pedesaan dari laki-laki berniat jahat.
long_description.en: The ghost is said to often appear as a beautiful woman walking alone on a quiet road, and according to the myth she is deeply ashamed of the hole in her body and always tries to cover it. She often appears to men at the place where she was killed, as a warning. Some also suggest the myth was spread to protect women walking alone at night in the countryside from ill-intentioned men.

long_description.id: Kisah sundel bolong tidak diketahui penulisnya karena bagian dari sastra lisan, dan dianggap sebagai salah satu kisah paling populer di Indonesia. Sundel bolong sangat dipopulerkan film horor, terutama Sundelbolong (1981) karya Sisworo Gautama Putra yang dibintangi Suzanna. Kajian akademik menyoroti bahwa film dan animasi tentang sundel bolong sering menormalisasi kekerasan terhadap perempuan.
long_description.en: The story of the sundel bolong has no known author because it belongs to oral literature, and it is regarded as one of the most popular stories in Indonesia. The sundel bolong was strongly popularized by horror films, especially Sundelbolong (1981) by Sisworo Gautama Putra, starring Suzanna. Academic studies highlight that films and animations about her often normalize violence against women.

cultural_context.id: Mitos sundel bolong diduga berfungsi sebagai peringatan sosial untuk melindungi perempuan yang berjalan sendirian di malam hari.
cultural_context.en: The sundel bolong myth is thought to act as a social warning protecting women walking alone at night.

statement.id: Sundel bolong umumnya digambarkan sebagai wanita cantik berambut panjang dan bergaun putih panjang, dengan punggung berlubang tembus yang sedikit tertutup rambut sehingga organ perut terlihat.
statement.en: The sundel bolong is generally pictured as a beautiful woman with long hair and a long white dress, with a back pierced through that is slightly covered by her hair so that abdominal organs are visible.

claims.quote: The term Sundel Bolong comes from two Javanese words: Sundel, meaning prostitute or immoral woman, and Bolong, meaning hole. Her defining trait is a large hole in her back that exposes her internal organs from behind through to the front.

statement.id: Istilah sundel bolong berasal dari dua kata Jawa: sundel (pelacur atau perempuan tak bermoral) dan bolong (lubang); cirinya yang utama adalah lubang besar di punggung yang memperlihatkan organ dalam dari belakang hingga depan.
statement.en: The term sundel bolong comes from two Javanese words, sundel (prostitute or immoral woman) and bolong (hole); her defining trait is a large hole in her back exposing her internal organs from back to front.

claims.quote: The name ‘Sundel Bolong’ is derived from two words: ‘sundal’ (a prostitute) and ‘bolong’ (a hole). This name itself hints at a symbolic meaning that this form of ghost is depicted negatively, not as a good woman, but as a prostitute who has a hole in her back full of maggots and blood, emphasizing a repugnant body.

statement.id: Nama sundel bolong berasal dari sundal (pelacur) dan bolong (lubang). Menurut kajian ini, nama itu menyiratkan bahwa sosok hantu ini digambarkan secara negatif: pelacur dengan lubang di punggung yang penuh belatung dan darah, yang menekankan tubuh yang menjijikkan.
statement.en: The name sundel bolong derives from sundal (prostitute) and bolong (hole). The study reads the name as hinting that this ghost form is depicted negatively: a prostitute with a hole in her back full of maggots and blood, emphasizing a repugnant body.

statement.en: The study analyses SB (1981), an Indonesian movie about a woman named Alisa who used to be a commercial sex worker.

claims.quote: After Alisa died, she became a ghost named Sundel Bolong to avenge herself by haunting people who hurt her when she was alive. Sundel Bolong seduces and kills all men that rape.

statement.id: Dalam film itu, setelah Alisa meninggal ia menjadi hantu bernama Sundel Bolong untuk membalas dendam dengan menghantui orang yang menyakitinya semasa hidup; Sundel Bolong menggoda dan membunuh semua laki-laki yang memerkosa.
statement.en: In that movie, after Alisa died she became a ghost named Sundel Bolong to avenge herself by haunting those who hurt her in life; Sundel Bolong seduces and kills all men who rape.

claims.quote: Sundel Bolong is also depicted as physically strong. She can among other things move a car, make a building crack, and push over a fence.

statement.id: Dalam film yang dianalisis, sundel bolong digambarkan kuat secara fisik: ia, antara lain, dapat menggerakkan mobil, membuat bangunan retak, dan merobohkan pagar.
statement.en: In the movie analysed, the sundel bolong is depicted as physically strong: she can, among other things, move a car, make a building crack, and push over a fence.

claims.quote: She also makes fun of these men by first seducing them in the form of a beautiful woman, and after she seduces these men, she changes her appearance to the Sundel Bolong ghost.

statement.id: Dalam film yang dianalisis, ia mula-mula menggoda laki-laki dalam rupa perempuan cantik, lalu setelah menggoda mereka ia berubah ke rupa hantu sundel bolong.

claims.quote: At the end of the story, a group of men consisting of Hendarto, Alisa’s husband, a Muslim preacher (Kiai), police, and village people, calmed Sundel Bolong (the ghost of Alisa) by saying prayers. Sundel Bolong left after being calmed by this group of men led by a kiai and did not haunt people anymore.

statement.en: At the end of the movie’s story, a group of men made up of Hendarto (Alisa’s husband), a kiai, police and villagers calmed the sundel bolong by saying prayers; she left once calmed and no longer haunted people.

short_description.id: Ao Bing adalah pangeran naga dalam novel klasik Fengshen Yanyi.
short_description.en: Ao Bing is a dragon prince in the classical novel Fengshen Yanyi.

long_description.id: Ao Bing adalah pangeran naga dalam novel klasik Fengshen Yanyi. Ia disebut putra ketiga Ao Guang, Raja Naga Laut Timur, dan tinggal di Istana Kristal bersama kakak-kakaknya Ao Jia dan Ao Yi. Ia menjadi antagonis dalam kisah Nezha. Semula ia dihormati sebagai dewa hujan, tetapi seiring waktu ayahnya menjadi korup dan rakyat hidup dalam ketakutan.
long_description.en: Ao Bing is a dragon prince in the classical novel Fengshen Yanyi. He is identified as the third son of Ao Guang, the East Sea Dragon King, and dwells in the Crystal Palace with his older brothers Ao Jia and Ao Yi. He serves as an antagonist in the Nezha tale. He was originally revered as a rain god, but over time his father became corrupt and the people lived in fear.

long_description.id: Dalam teks novel itu, Ao Bing tampil sebagai putra ketiga Raja Naga, menyebut dirinya demikian, lalu mengerahkan pasukan naga dan keluar menunggangi binatang pendorong air dengan tombak berhias. Nezha menggulungnya dengan selendang Hun Tian, menginjak lehernya, dan memukulnya dengan Cincin Qiankun sehingga wujud nagaya tampak, lalu mencabut uratnya. Ao Guang yang dilapori berseru bahwa putranya adalah dewa yang membuat awan dan hujan. Setelah kekalahan Shang, ia diangkat sebagai dewa Huagai xing.
long_description.en: In the novel's text, Ao Bing appears as the third prince of the Dragon King, declares himself so, then musters dragon soldiers and goes out riding a water-forcing beast with a painted halberd. Nezha wraps him in the Hun Tian scarf, steps on his neck, and strikes him with the Qiankun Ring so that his dragon form shows, then pulls out his sinews. Ao Guang, told of it, cries that his son is a god who makes clouds and rain. After the Shang defeat, he becomes the god of Huagai xing.

long_description.id: Menurut cerita rakyat, Nezha membunuh naga putih Ao Bing dengan Cincin Semesta, tetapi sang abadi Taiyi Zhenren kemudian menghidupkannya kembali. Dalam tradisi Tao dan kepercayaan rakyat ia dipuja sebagai dewa rakyat di sejumlah kuil Raja Naga Empat Laut. Dalam film animasi Ne Zha (2019) dan Ne Zha 2 (2025) ia menjadi tokoh utama.
long_description.en: According to folklore, Nezha killed the white dragon Ao Bing with the Universe Ring, but the immortal Taiyi Zhenren later revived him. In Taoist traditions and folk beliefs he is worshiped as a folk deity in some temples of the Dragon Kings of the Four Seas. He is a leading figure in the animated movie Ne Zha (2019) and its 2025 sequel, Ne Zha 2.

statement.id: Dalam teks klasik ini, putra ketiga Raja Naga (龍王三太子) Ao Bing (敖丙) tampil dan berkata kepada ayahnya bahwa ia akan menangkap pelakunya; ia mengerahkan pasukan naga, menunggangi binatang pendorong air (逼水獸) dengan tombak bergagang berhias (畫杆戟), dan keluar dari Istana Kristal (水晶宮).
statement.en: In this classical text, the third prince of the Dragon King (龍王三太子) Ao Bing (敖丙) steps forward and tells his father he will go and seize the culprit; he musters dragon soldiers, rides a water-forcing beast (逼水獸) with a painted halberd (畫杆戟), and goes out of the Crystal Palace (水晶宮).

claims.quote: 敖丙曰：「孤乃東海龍君三太子敖丙是也。」哪吒笑曰：「你原來是敖光之子。你妄自尊大。

statement.id: Dalam teks klasik ini Ao Bing (敖丙) menyebut dirinya sebagai putra ketiga (三太子) Raja Naga Laut Timur (東海龍君); Nezha (哪吒) menanggapi bahwa ia putra Ao Guang (敖光) dan sombong (妄自尊大).
statement.en: In this classical text Ao Bing (敖丙) declares himself the third prince (三太子) of the Dragon Lord of the East Sea (東海龍君); Nezha (哪吒) replies that he is Ao Guang's (敖光) son and is arrogant (妄自尊大).

claims.quote: 哪吒急了，把七尺混天綾望空一展，似火塊千團，往下一裹，將三太子裹下逼水獸來。哪吒搶一步趕上去，一腳踏住敖丙的頸項，提起乾坤圈，照頂門一下，把三太子的元身打出，是一條龍，在地上挺直。

statement.id: Dalam teks klasik ini, Nezha (哪吒) membentangkan selendang Hun Tian (七尺混天綾) yang seperti seribu gumpal api dan menggulung sang pangeran jatuh dari binatangnya; ia lalu menginjak leher Ao Bing (敖丙) dan memukul ubun-ubunnya dengan Cincin Qiankun (乾坤圈), sehingga wujud asli sang pangeran terlihat sebagai seekor naga yang terbujur di tanah.
statement.en: In this classical text, Nezha (哪吒) spreads his seven-foot Hun Tian scarf (七尺混天綾), like a thousand lumps of fire, and wraps the prince off his beast; he then steps on Ao Bing's (敖丙) neck and strikes his crown with the Qiankun Ring (乾坤圈), so that the prince's original body shows as a dragon lying stretched on the ground.

claims.quote: 把三太子的元身打出，是一條龍，在地上挺直。哪吒曰：「打出這小龍的本像來了。也罷，把他的筋抽去，做一條龍筋絛與俺父親束甲。」哪吒把三太子的筋抽了，逕帶進關來。

short_description.id: Dalam mitologi Aztec, Cipactli adalah monster laut purba, sebagian buaya, ikan, dan kodok, yang selalu lapar; dari tubuhnya para dewa menciptakan bumi.
short_description.en: In Aztec mythology Cipactli was a primeval sea monster, part crocodilian, fish, and toad, always hungry; the gods made the earth from its body.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Aztec, Cipactli adalah monster laut purba yang sebagian buaya, sebagian ikan, dan sebagian kodok. Ia selalu lapar, dan setiap sendi tubuhnya dihiasi mulut tambahan. Dalam beberapa versi, Cipactli disebut Tlaltecuhtli, dewa yang dijuluki 'monster bumi'; sumber lain menyebut Cipactl atau 'si berduri' sebagai nama makhluk yang ditemukan duduk mengangkangi samudra itu.
long_description.en: Aztec myth casts Cipactli as a primeval monster of the sea, a blend of crocodile, fish, and toad or frog. It was always hungry, and every joint of its body bore an extra mouth. Some versions identify Cipactli with Tlaltecuhtli, the deity nicknamed the 'earth monster'; another source gives Cipactl, or 'spiny one', as the name of the creature found sitting astride the ocean.

long_description.id: Tezcatlipoca mengorbankan sebuah kakinya sebagai umpan untuk menarik monster itu mendekat, lalu bersama Quetzalcoatl menciptakan bumi dari tubuhnya. Dalam penuturan lain, kedua dewa berubah menjadi ular raksasa, bergumul dengan monster bertaring besar yang bermulut di siku dan lututnya, dan merobeknya menjadi dua; bagian atas menjadi langit dan bagian bawah menjadi bumi. Kulitnya menjadi rumput, rambutnya pepohonan, matanya mata air, hidungnya gunung kecil, dan mulutnya gua dan sungai.
long_description.en: Tezcatlipoca sacrificed a foot as bait to draw the monster nearer, then created the earth with Quetzalcoatl from its body. In another telling the two gods turned into gigantic snakes, wrestled the large-fanged monster with mouths at its elbows and knees, and ripped it in two; the upper half became the sky and the lower half the earth. Its skin became grasses, its hair the trees, its eyes springs, its nose the smaller mountains, and its mouth the caves and rivers.

long_description.id: Makhluk itu tetap dianggap lapar akan jantung korban kurban; nafsunya harus dipenuhi agar ia tidak berhenti menyuburkan bumi. Ia juga dianggap menelan matahari setiap malam dan memuntahkannya saat fajar. Cipactli adalah hari pertama dalam hitungan ramalan tonalpohualli, dan buaya melambangkan bumi yang mengapung di perairan purba.
long_description.en: The creature was still thought to hunger for the hearts of sacrificial victims; its appetite had to be met so it would not stop nourishing the earth. It was also thought to swallow the sun each evening and give it back at dawn. Cipactli was the first day of the tonalpohualli divinatory count, and the crocodile symbolized the earth floating in the primeval waters.

long_description.id: Karl A. Taube mencatat bahwa buaya di kalangan Olmec dan Maya diidentifikasi dengan angin pembawa hujan, dan nama iblis gempa Zipacna dalam Popol Vuh tampaknya berasal dari Cipactli. Menurut satu tradisi Aztec, Teocipactli 'Buaya Ilahi' adalah penyintas banjir yang kembali mengisi bumi dengan manusia.
long_description.en: Karl A. Taube noted that among the Olmec and Maya crocodilians were identified with rain-bringing wind, and the name of the earthquake demon Zipacna in the Popol Vuh apparently derives from Cipactli. According to one Aztec tradition, Teocipactli, 'Divine Crocodile', was a survivor of the flood who repopulated the earth.

short_description.id: Damballa adalah salah satu loa (roh) terpenting dalam Vodun Afrika Barat dan Voodoo Haiti, digambarkan sebagai ular besar putih atau hitam yang dihormati sebagai pencipta purba.
short_description.en: Damballa is among the foremost loa (spirits) of West African Vodun and Haitian Voodoo, pictured as a great white or black serpent and honoured as a primordial creator.

long_description.id: Damballa, yang juga dieja Damballah atau Danbala, adalah salah satu loa terpenting dalam Vodun Afrika Barat, Voodoo Haiti, dan tradisi diaspora Afrika lain seperti Obeah. Asalnya dikaitkan dengan kota Wedo (Whydah atau Ouidah) di wilayah Benin modern. Ia secara tradisional digambarkan sebagai ular besar putih atau hitam, dan di Haiti dipandang sebagai loa tertinggi yang berwujud ular.
long_description.en: Damballa, also written Damballah or Danbala, ranks among the chief loa of West African Vodun, Haitian Voodoo and other African diaspora faiths such as Obeah. His origin is traced to the city of Wedo (Whydah or Ouidah) in present-day Benin. He is customarily imagined as a huge serpent, white or black, and in Haiti he is regarded as the supreme loa in snake form.

long_description.id: Ia disebut bapa langit dan pencipta purba segala kehidupan, atau ciptaan pertama Bondye. Dalam komunitas Vodou yang memandangnya sebagai pencipta, ia membentuk bintang, planet, bukit, dan lembah dengan 7000 lilitannya, dan dengan berganti kulit ia menciptakan semua perairan di bumi. Sumber ketiga juga menyebutnya sebagai loa yang dianggap menciptakan dunia dan para dewa lain.
long_description.en: He is called the sky father and first creator of all living things, or else the first being the Bondye made. Where Vodou communities treat him as creator, his 7000 coils shaped stars, planets, hills and valleys, and the skin he shed became every body of water on Earth. The third source likewise credits this loa with making the world and every other god.

long_description.id: Damballa dipandang baik hati, sabar, dan bijak, tetapi berjarak dari urusan sehari-hari manusia. Karena kebijaksanaannya ia tidak berbicara, hanya bersiul atau mendesis pelan. Istrinya, Ayida Wédo, juga digambarkan sebagai ular pelangi, meski di sebagian komunitas Vodou ia dianggap saudarinya atau bahkan Damballa sendiri dalam rupa lain.
long_description.en: Damballa is regarded as kindly, patient and wise, though aloof from everyday human struggles. Being so wise, he never speaks, only whistling or hissing softly. His wife Ayida Wédo is also shown as a rainbow serpent, although some Vodou communities treat her as his sister or even as Damballa in another guise.

long_description.id: Dalam upacara, pemuja yang dirasuki Damballa bergerak di lantai seperti ular. Persembahannya antara lain susu, makanan dan bunga putih, nasi, kelapa, sirup orgeat, serta telur, yang menurut kepercayaan di Haiti ia remukkan dengan giginya. Ia biasanya disinkretiskan dengan Santo Patrick atau Musa (Moses); Santo Patrick dipilih karena biasa digambarkan bersama ular.
long_description.en: During ceremonies, a devotee possessed by Damballa crawls on the floor like a snake. His offerings include milk, white foods and flowers, rice, coconut, orgeat syrup and eggs, which in Haiti he is believed to crush with his teeth. He is usually syncretized with Saint Patrick or Moses, the saint being chosen because he is so often depicted with snakes.

statement.en: Damballa is said to be the sky father and primordial creator of all life, or the first thing created by the Bondye.

claims.quote: In those Vodou societies that view Damballa as the primordial creator, he created the cosmos by using his 7000 coils to form the stars and the planets in the heavens and to shape the hills and valleys on Earth.

statement.id: Dalam komunitas Vodou yang memandangnya sebagai pencipta purba, ia menciptakan kosmos dengan 7000 lilitannya: membentuk bintang dan planet serta bukit dan lembah di bumi.
statement.en: In Vodou societies that see him as primordial creator, he made the cosmos with his 7000 coils, forming the stars and planets and shaping the hills and valleys of Earth.

claims.quote: Damballa is seen as benevolent and patient, wise and kind, yet detached and removed from the trials and tribulations of daily human life.

claims.quote: As a serpent, and due to his extreme wisdom, he does not speak, but may whistle or make a soft, hissing sound.

statement.en: Damballah (also Damballa, Danbala, Dam Ballah) is the serpent-shaped highest loa (schlangenförmige oberste Loa) in the Haitian religion of Voodoo.

claims.quote: Gemeinsam mit seiner ebenfalls als Schlange (Regenbogenschlange) dargestellten Frau Ayida Wédo steht er für das absolut Göttliche in seiner männlich-weiblichen Dualität.

statement.id: Bersama istrinya Ayida Wédo (Frau Ayida Wédo), yang juga digambarkan sebagai ular pelangi, ia melambangkan keilahian mutlak dalam dualitas laki-laki dan perempuan.
statement.en: Together with his wife Ayida Wédo (Frau Ayida Wédo), also shown as a rainbow serpent, he stands for the absolute divine in its male-female duality.

claims.quote: Man opfert Damballah in Haiti in Ritualen ein Ei, das er als Schlange mit seinen Zähnen zerdrückt.

statement.en: In Haiti, Damballah is offered an egg (Ei) in rituals, which he as a serpent crushes with his teeth.

claims.quote: Der Legende nach lebt Damballah in Schlangengestalt auf einem Baum in der Nähe einer Quelle oder er fährt in ein Becken, das man für ihn erbaut hat.

claims.quote: Damballah is the loa who is credited with the creation of the world and all other gods.

statement.id: Damballah adalah loa yang dianggap menciptakan dunia dan semua dewa lain.
statement.en: Damballah is the loa credited with creating the world and all other gods.

short_description.id: Flathead Lake Monster ("Flessie") adalah monster danau dari legenda Kutenai dan cerita rakyat Montana yang konon hidup di Flathead Lake [flathead-lake-monster-c01, flathead-lake-monster-c06].
short_description.en: The Flathead Lake Monster ("Flessie") is a lake monster of Kutenai legend and Montana folklore said to live in Flathead Lake [flathead-lake-monster-c01, flathead-lake-monster-c06].

long_description.id: Flathead Lake Monster adalah monster danau yang konon hidup di Flathead Lake, Montana [flathead-lake-monster-c01]. Kisahnya berasal dari legenda Kutenai [flathead-lake-monster-c02], yang menceritakan kepala monster bertanduk raksasa muncul dari es [flathead-lake-monster-c03] dan separuh suku tenggelam [flathead-lake-monster-c04].
long_description.en: The Flathead Lake Monster is said to live in Flathead Lake, Montana [flathead-lake-monster-c01]. Its story comes from a Kutenai legend [flathead-lake-monster-c02], in which a monster's antlered head burst through the ice [flathead-lake-monster-c03] and half the tribe drowned [flathead-lake-monster-c04].

long_description.id: Laporan pertama konon berasal dari Kapten James C. Kerr pada tahun 1889 [flathead-lake-monster-c05]. Warga menamainya "Flessie" meniru "Nessie" [flathead-lake-monster-c06] dan menggambarkannya seperti belut besar sepanjang dua puluh hingga empat puluh kaki [flathead-lake-monster-c07].
long_description.en: The first report supposedly came from Captain James C. Kerr in 1889 [flathead-lake-monster-c05]. Locals named it "Flessie" after "Nessie" [flathead-lake-monster-c06] and describe a large eel-shaped creature twenty to forty feet long [flathead-lake-monster-c07].

long_description.id: Flathead Beacon menulis bahwa kemungkinan catatan modern pertama yang dipercaya datang pada 1889 dari James Kerr, kapten kapal uap U.S. Grant [flathead-lake-monster-c08]. Kerr mengira ia melihat kayu gelondongan besar, tetapi "kayu" sepanjang lebih dari 20 kaki itu mulai bergerak di air [flathead-lake-monster-c09]. Kebanyakan laporan lain, selain penampakan ikan besar, menggambarkannya panjang, seperti belut, bulat, 30 sampai 40 kaki, dengan mata hitam besar [flathead-lake-monster-c11]; sebagian lain menyebut ikan besar sepanjang 6 sampai 10 kaki, mungkin sturgeon [flathead-lake-monster-c17].
long_description.en: The Flathead Beacon says the first modern report to be taken seriously may be the one James Kerr, captain of the steamboat U.S. Grant, made in 1889 [flathead-lake-monster-c08]. Kerr thought he saw a large log, but the "log", more than 20 feet long, began to move through the water [flathead-lake-monster-c09]. Most other reports, apart from large-fish sightings, describe it as long, eel-shaped and round, 30 to 40 feet long, with large black eyes [flathead-lake-monster-c11]; some instead name a massive fish 6 to 10 feet long, possibly a sturgeon [flathead-lake-monster-c17].

long_description.id: Penjelasan alternatif muncul dari waktu ke waktu. Sebagian penampakan dikaitkan dengan imajinasi, kelakar, ombak, bayangan, kayu gelondongan, atau hewan [flathead-lake-monster-c10]. Pada 1955, sturgeon putih tangkapan C. Leslie Griffith dipajang di museum dan memicu teori bahwa sturgeon menjadi penyebab [flathead-lake-monster-c13], tetapi menurut Beacon, penjaringan, penyetruman, dan kapal selam kecil tidak menemukan tanda sturgeon atau makhluk lain [flathead-lake-monster-c12].
long_description.en: Alternative explanations have appeared over time. Some sightings have been attributed to imagination, pranks, waves, shadows, logs or animals [flathead-lake-monster-c10]. In 1955 a white sturgeon caught by C. Leslie Griffith was displayed in a museum and fuelled theories that sturgeon were responsible [flathead-lake-monster-c13], but according to the Beacon, netting, electro-shocking and small submarines have found no sign of sturgeon or other creatures [flathead-lake-monster-c12].

long_description.id: Sebuah kelompok pelestarian danau setempat mencatat versi lisan Kootenai dari tetua Catherine dan Louise Andrew: istri seekor burung memberi buah huckleberry kepada makhluk danau yang ramah, dan suaminya yang cemburu membunuh monster itu [flathead-lake-monster-c14]. Tubuh makhluk itu menjadi Sullivan Hill dekat Elmo di tepi barat danau [flathead-lake-monster-c15]. Pada 2024 kota Polson memasang patung perunggu setinggi 25 kaki makhluk itu di Sacajawea Park [flathead-lake-monster-c16].
long_description.en: A local lake-conservation group records a Kootenai oral version from elders Catherine and Louise Andrew: a bird's wife fed huckleberries to a friendly lake creature, and her jealous husband killed the monster [flathead-lake-monster-c14]. The creature's body became Sullivan Hill near Elmo on the western shore [flathead-lake-monster-c15]. The city of Polson put up a 25-foot bronze statue of the creature in Sacajawea Park in 2024 [flathead-lake-monster-c16].

claims.quote: The Flathead Lake Monster is a lake monster of Indigenous legend and Montana folklore that is purported to dwell in Flathead Lake in northwestern Montana, United States.

statement.id: Flathead Lake Monster adalah monster danau dari legenda pribumi dan cerita rakyat Montana yang konon hidup di Flathead Lake, Montana barat laut, Amerika Serikat.
statement.en: The Flathead Lake Monster is a lake monster of Indigenous legend and Montana folklore said to live in Flathead Lake, northwestern Montana, United States.

claims.quote: The story of a monster in Flathead Lake originates in a Kutenai traditional legend.

statement.id: Kisah monster di Flathead Lake berasal dari legenda tradisional Kutenai.
statement.en: The story originates in a Kutenai traditional legend.

claims.quote: The frozen surface of the lake split open around them, and the head of a monster appeared through the ice, shaking its giant antlers.

statement.id: Dalam legenda itu, permukaan danau yang beku terbelah dan kepala monster bertanduk rusa raksasa muncul dari balik es.
statement.en: In the legend, the frozen lake split open and a monster's head with giant antlers rose through the ice.

claims.quote: but half of the tribe drowned in the lake, which is said to be the reason why there are so few Kutenai people.

statement.id: Separuh suku tenggelam di danau, yang konon menjadi alasan jumlah orang Kutenai sedikit.
statement.en: Half the tribe drowned, said to be why there are so few Kutenai people.

claims.quote: It was supposedly first reported in 1889 by Captain James C. Kerr of the lake steamboat U.S. Grant.

statement.id: Monster ini konon pertama kali dilaporkan pada tahun 1889 oleh Kapten James C. Kerr dari kapal uap U.S. Grant.
statement.en: It was supposedly first reported in 1889 by Captain James C. Kerr of the steamboat U.S. Grant.

claims.quote: Fugleberg notes that local residents have named the purported lake monster "Flessie", inspired by Loch Ness' "Nessie".

statement.id: Menurut Fugleberg, warga setempat menamainya "Flessie", terilhami "Nessie" dari Loch Ness.
statement.en: According to Fugleberg, locals named it "Flessie", inspired by Loch Ness's "Nessie".

claims.quote: The monster is usually described as a large, round, eel-shaped creature with a wavy body like a snake about twenty to forty feet (6.1 to 12.2 m) long, having brownish to bluish-black skin and grayish-black eyes.

statement.id: Ia biasanya digambarkan seperti belut besar bertubuh bergelombang seperti ular, panjang sekitar dua puluh hingga empat puluh kaki, berkulit cokelat hingga hitam kebiruan.
statement.en: It is usually described as a large eel-shaped creature with a wavy, snake-like body about twenty to forty feet long and brownish to bluish-black skin.

claims.quote: possibly the first modern account to gain credence came in 1889 from James Kerr, the captain of the U.S. Grant, a steam-driven boat that ferried passengers and freight up and down the lake.

statement.id: Menurut Flathead Beacon, kemungkinan catatan modern pertama yang dipercaya datang pada 1889 dari James Kerr, kapten U.S. Grant, kapal uap yang mengangkut penumpang dan barang di danau itu.
statement.en: According to the Flathead Beacon, possibly the first modern account to gain credence came in 1889 from James Kerr, captain of the U.S. Grant, a steam-driven boat that ferried passengers and freight on the lake.

claims.quote: Kerr reported seeing what he initially thought was a large log. As the boat got closer, the “log,” estimated at more than 20 feet in length, began to move through the water.

statement.id: Kerr melaporkan melihat sesuatu yang semula disangkanya kayu gelondongan besar; saat kapal mendekat, "kayu" itu, diperkirakan lebih dari 20 kaki panjangnya, mulai bergerak di air.
statement.en: Kerr reported seeing what he first thought was a large log; as the boat got closer, the "log", estimated at more than 20 feet long, began to move through the water.

claims.quote: Some of the sightings have been attributed to hyperactive imaginations, playful pranks, natural phenomena such as wave action, shadows, lighting effects, logs and a large number of animals

statement.id: Dalam kutipan dari sebuah kolom yang dimuat Beacon, sebagian penampakan dikaitkan dengan imajinasi berlebihan, kelakar, fenomena alam seperti ombak, bayangan, dan efek cahaya, kayu gelondongan, serta banyak hewan.
statement.en: In a quotation from a column carried by the Beacon, some sightings have been attributed to hyperactive imaginations, playful pranks, natural phenomena such as wave action, shadows and lighting effects, logs and a large number of animals.

claims.quote: Most, other than large fish sightings, describe it as long and eel-shaped, round, 30 to 40 feet in length with large black eyes

short_description.id: Hatmehit adalah dewi ikan Mesir kuno dari kawasan Delta Nil di sekitar Mendes, digambarkan sebagai ikan atau perempuan dengan ikan di kepalanya.
short_description.en: Hatmehit is an ancient Egyptian fish goddess of the Nile Delta around Mendes, shown as a fish or as a woman with a fish on her head.

long_description.id: Hatmehit adalah dewi Mesir yang sudah dikenal sebagai dewi ikan sejak Dinasti Keempat dan menjadi dewi nome ke-16 Mesir Hilir. Ia digambarkan sebagai perempuan dengan ikan mirip lele di kepalanya, yang dikenakan di atas diadem uraeus, atau sebagai ikan pada jimat. Menurut World History Encyclopedia, ia berasal dari lambang totem nome di sekitar Mendes, yaitu seekor ikan.
long_description.en: Hatmehit is an Egyptian goddess attested as a fish goddess from the Fourth Dynasty and a goddess of the 16th nome of Lower Egypt. She is depicted as a woman with a catfish-like fish on her head, which she wears over a uraeus diadem, or as a fish on amulets. According to World History Encyclopedia, she arose from the totemic symbol of the nome around Mendes, which was a fish.

long_description.id: Hatmehit dipuja terutama di Mendes, dan gambarannya juga ditemukan di kuil Amun di Hibis serta di kuil dan makam lain di Mesir. Bersama dewa Banebdjedet (Domba Mendes) dan Harpocrates, ia membentuk triad Mendes. Karena Mendes menjadi pusat pembuatan parfum, ia juga dikaitkan dengan aroma harum.
long_description.en: Hatmehit was worshipped mainly at Mendes, and depictions of her are also found in Amun's temple at Hibis and in other temples and tombs in Egypt. With the god Banebdjedet (the Ram of Mendes) and Harpocrates she forms the Mendes triad. Because Mendes was a centre of perfume production, she was also associated with good scents.

long_description.id: Namanya biasanya diterjemahkan "Yang Terdepan di Antara Ikan", meskipun kadang juga dipahami sebagai "Yang Terdepan dari Banjir". Pada periode kemudian ia mengambil ikonografi Isis dan Hathor, dan sejak Periode Peralihan Ketiga Isis mulai mengambil perannya dalam kultus setempat.
long_description.en: Her name is usually translated "Foremost of the Fish", although it is sometimes also understood as "Foremost of the Inundation". In later periods she takes on the iconography of Isis and Hathor, and from the Third Intermediate Period Isis began to take her role in the local cult.

short_description.id: Sirena adalah putri duyung dalam cerita rakyat Filipina, bertubuh atas perempuan dan berekor ikan, yang dengan nyanyiannya memikat nelayan hingga tenggelam.
short_description.en: The sirena is the mermaid of Philippine folklore, with a woman's upper body and a fish's tail, whose song lures fishermen to drown.

long_description.id: Sirena adalah makhluk laut mitos dalam budaya Filipina. Ia bertubuh atas perempuan dan berekor ikan dari pinggang ke bawah, dan tergolong engkanto, padanan Filipina bagi putri duyung. Sirena termasuk bantay tubig, penjaga perairan, bersama siyokoy, kataw, dan ugkoy; versi laki-lakinya disebut sireno. Ia digambarkan cantik, berambut panjang mengalir yang sering ikal atau bergelombang.
long_description.en: The sirena is a mythical sea creature of Filipino culture. She has a woman's upper body and a fish's tail from the waist down, and is an engkanto, the Filipino counterpart of the mermaid. The sirena belongs to the bantay tubig, guardians of the waters, together with the siyokoy, kataw and ugkoy; the male version is called the sireno. She is pictured as beautiful, with long, flowing, often curly or wavy hair.

long_description.id: Sirena bersuara indah yang memikat dan menghipnotis laki-laki, terutama nelayan. Ia bernyanyi dari antara batu di tepi pantai hingga para pelaut lalai, terjatuh dari kapal, atau kapalnya karam. Menurut sebagian tradisi, korbannya dibawa ke bawah laut dan dipersembahkan kepada dewa-dewa air; cerita lain menyebut ia berpura-pura perlu diselamatkan dari tenggelam.
long_description.en: The sirena has a beautiful, enchanting voice that lures and hypnotizes men, especially fishermen. She sings from among the rocks on the shore until sailors grow careless, fall from their decks or are shipwrecked. In some traditions her victims are carried under the sea and sacrificed to water deities; other stories say she pretends to need rescuing from drowning.

long_description.id: Banyak mitos Pangasinan menceritakan sirena yang menenggelamkan nelayan dan prajurit pemuja Apo Laki, dan dalam beberapa cerita sirena menjaga perairan "asin-palan" dari perampok bertato dari Visayas. Dalam kisah Iloko yang diingat Maximo Ramos, seorang anak melihat wanita cantik mandi di tepi sungai yang ternyata sirena, dan informan Ramos mengatakan sirena membuat air naik menelan korban. Orang Visayas menyebut makhluk serupa kataw, yang bernyanyi dari atas batu lalu menenggelamkan perahu nelayan.
long_description.en: Many Pangasinan myths tell of sirenas who drown fishermen and warriors who worship Apo Laki, and in some stories sirenas guard the waters of "asin-palan" from tattooed raiders from the Visayas. In an Iloko tale Maximo Ramos recalled, a boy sees a beautiful woman bathing at the river bank who proves to be a sirena, and Ramos's informants said the sirena made the water rise to engulf victims. The Visayans call a similar being kataw, who sings from a rock and then sinks fishermen's boats.

long_description.id: Cerita Ilokano memberi gambaran lebih beragam. Dalam The Mermaid Queen, sirena adalah wanita baik hati berkekuatan supernatural yang menuntun nelayan pulang saat badai dan menyelamatkan anak dari tenggelam; dalam kisah sungai Amburayan, sirena mengubah dirinya menjadi manusia tetapi bau amisnya membuat pria incarannya pingsan; dan litao, anito air laki-laki, disebut suami sirena di Vigan.
long_description.en: Ilokano tales give a more varied picture. In The Mermaid Queen the sirena is a kind lady with supernatural powers who guides fishermen home in a storm and saves a child from drowning; in the Amburayan river tale the sirena turns human but her fishy odor makes the man she pursues faint; and the litao, a male water anito, is called the husband of the sirena in Vigan.

long_description.id: Menurut seorang penulis Aswang Project yang memakai Beyer Ethnographic Series, cerita sirena terutama ditemukan dalam naskah Ilokano, dan kata sirena berasal dari bahasa Spanyol tanpa padanan Ilokano; sirena disebut padanan Spanyol bagi putri duyung yang tampaknya menggeser banyak istilah daerah. Ia mengaitkan cerita itu dengan arus kuat di sungai-sungai Ilocos. Dalam budaya modern, serial Marina (2004) dan adaptasi televisi Dyesebel (2008) menampilkan putri duyung.
long_description.en: According to an Aswang Project writer drawing on the Beyer Ethnographic Series, sirena stories are found mainly in the Ilokano papers, and the word sirena is Spanish with no Ilokano equivalent; sirena is described as the Spanish equivalent of mermaid that appears to have driven out many vernacular terms. She links the stories to the strong currents of the Ilocos rivers. In modern culture the series Marina (2004) and the television adaptation of Dyesebel (2008) feature mermaids.

claims.quote: In Philippine mythology, the Sirena is a mythological aquatic legendary creature with the head and torso of a human female from waist down and the tail of a fish. The Sirena is an Engkanto –' the Filipino counterpart of English mermaids.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Filipina, sirena adalah makhluk air legendaris berkepala dan bertubuh atas perempuan dengan ekor ikan dari pinggang ke bawah; sirena adalah engkanto, padanan Filipina bagi putri duyung Inggris.
statement.en: In Philippine mythology, the sirena is a legendary water creature with a woman's head and torso and a fish's tail from the waist down; she is an engkanto, the Filipino counterpart of the English mermaid.

claims.quote: Engkantos are classified as one of the Bantay Tubig, (guardian of a body of water) a Filipino term for mythical guardians of the water. In addition to the Sirena, other examples of Bantay Tubig are Siyokoy, Kataw, and Ugkoy. The male version of a Sirena is called a Sireno. Sometimes, Sirena are paired with Siyokoy.

statement.id: Sirena termasuk bantay tubig (penjaga perairan), bersama siyokoy, kataw, dan ugkoy; versi laki-lakinya disebut sireno, dan sirena kadang dipasangkan dengan siyokoy.
statement.en: The sirena is one of the bantay tubig (water guardians), with the siyokoy, kataw and ugkoy; the male version is the sireno, and sirenas are sometimes paired with siyokoy.

claims.quote: The Sirena has a beautiful and enchanting voice that can attract and hypnotize males, especially fishermen. Sirena sing to sailors and enchant them, distracting them from their work and causing them to walk off ship decks or cause shipwrecks.

statement.id: Sirena bersuara indah yang memikat dan menghipnotis laki-laki, terutama nelayan; ia bernyanyi kepada pelaut hingga mereka lalai, terjatuh dari geladak, atau kapalnya karam.
statement.en: The sirena's beautiful voice lures and hypnotizes men, especially fishermen; she sings to sailors until they neglect their work, walk off decks or are shipwrecked.

claims.quote: Some folk traditions claim that the Sirena carry their victims under the sea, sacrificing them to water deities.

statement.id: Menurut sebagian tradisi rakyat, sirena membawa korbannya ke bawah laut dan mempersembahkan mereka kepada dewa-dewa air.
statement.en: Some folk traditions claim that the sirena carries her victims under the sea, sacrificing them to water deities.

claims.quote: Many Pangasinan myths describe Sirena who drown fishermen and warriors who worship Apo laki.

statement.id: Banyak mitos Pangasinan menceritakan sirena yang menenggelamkan nelayan dan prajurit pemuja Apo Laki.
statement.en: Many Pangasinan myths tell of sirenas drowning fishermen and warriors who worship Apo Laki.

claims.quote: Using the 160 volumes of the Beyer Ethnographic Series, I was amazed that the maiden of the waters was predominantly unique to the Ilokano volumes.

statement.id: Menurut penulis di Aswang Project yang memakai 160 jilid Beyer Ethnographic Series, cerita sirena terutama ditemukan dalam jilid-jilid Ilokano.
statement.en: According to the Aswang Project writer using the 160 volumes of the Beyer Ethnographic Series, sirena tales appear mainly in the Ilokano volumes.

claims.quote: besides the word sirena is a Spanish word and has no Ilokano equivalent.

statement.id: Kata sirena berasal dari bahasa Spanyol dan tidak punya padanan dalam bahasa Ilokano.
statement.en: The word sirena is Spanish and has no Ilokano equivalent.

claims.quote: Marina was a fantasy series that featured a mermaid. It aired from February 23, 2004, to November 12, 2004, featuring Claudine Barretto.

statement.id: Marina adalah serial fantasi tentang putri duyung yang ditayangkan dari 23 Februari hingga 12 November 2004 dengan Claudine Barretto.
statement.en: Marina was a fantasy series featuring a mermaid, aired from February 23 to November 12, 2004, featuring Claudine Barretto.

claims.quote: They sing with enchanting voices while hiding among the rocks by the shore. When the men hear these songs, they are hypnotized and abducted by the Sirena.

statement.id: Sirena bernyanyi dengan suara memikat sambil bersembunyi di antara batu di tepi pantai; ketika para pria mendengar lagu itu, mereka terhipnotis dan diculik oleh sirena.
statement.en: Sirena sing with enchanting voices while hiding among the rocks by the shore; when men hear the songs they are hypnotized and abducted by the sirena.

claims.quote: Other stories claim that the Sirena pretend to need rescuing from drowning, luring men into the sea, but then to squeeze the life out of any man who falls prey to their hoax.

statement.id: Cerita lain mengatakan sirena berpura-pura perlu diselamatkan dari tenggelam untuk memancing pria ke laut, lalu meremas habis nyawa pria yang termakan tipuannya.
statement.en: Other stories claim that sirena pretend to need rescuing from drowning, luring men into the sea and then squeezing the life out of any man who falls for the hoax.

claims.quote: A malevolent Sirena may tease and attract human males with its spellbinding songs. Occasional reports had Sirena grabbing seemingly hypnotized humans and drowning them or taking them underwater.

statement.id: Sirena yang jahat dapat menggoda dan menarik pria dengan lagu yang memukau; ada laporan sesekali tentang sirena yang menangkap manusia yang tampak terhipnotis dan menenggelamkan atau membawa mereka ke bawah air.
statement.en: A malevolent sirena may tease and attract men with spellbinding songs; occasional reports had sirena grabbing seemingly hypnotized humans and drowning them or taking them underwater.

claims.quote: Sirena are beautiful sea creatures with the upper body of a human with long, flowing hair that is often curly or wavy and the lower body of a fish or a tail of a fish. In pre-Hispanic Philippines, Sirena were regarded as beautiful aquatic creatures.

statement.id: Sirena adalah makhluk laut yang cantik, bertubuh atas manusia dengan rambut panjang mengalir yang sering ikal atau bergelombang dan bertubuh bawah ikan atau berekor ikan; pada Filipina prakolonial mereka dipandang sebagai makhluk akuatik yang indah.
statement.en: Sirena are beautiful sea creatures with a human upper body and long, flowing, often curly or wavy hair, and a fish's lower body or tail; in pre-Hispanic Philippines they were regarded as beautiful aquatic creatures.

claims.quote: In some stories, they are guardians of the waters of "asin-palan," shielding it from the tattooed raiders from the Visayas.

statement.id: Dalam beberapa cerita, sirena adalah penjaga perairan "asin-palan" yang melindunginya dari perampok bertato dari Visayas.
statement.en: In some stories, sirena are guardians of the waters of "asin-palan", shielding it from the tattooed raiders from the Visayas.

claims.quote: The first TV series adaptation of Dyesebel was broadcast on GMA Network in 2008. It originally aired on April 28, 2008, and ended on October 17, 2008, completing 125 episodes.

statement.id: Adaptasi serial televisi pertama Dyesebel disiarkan di GMA Network pada 2008, tayang dari 28 April hingga 17 Oktober 2008 sebanyak 125 episode.
statement.en: The first TV series adaptation of Dyesebel was broadcast on GMA Network in 2008, airing from April 28 to October 17, 2008, for 125 episodes.

claims.quote: The sirena or mermaid and the facts surrounding this mythical creature are of Spanish origin.

statement.id: Menurut penulis Aswang Project, sirena atau putri duyung dan fakta-fakta seputar makhluk mitos ini berasal dari Spanyol.
statement.en: According to the Aswang Project writer, the sirena or mermaid and the facts surrounding this mythical creature are of Spanish origin.

claims.quote: The different rivers in the Ilocos region although calm and pristine on the surface have strong currents and undertows beneath. ... having no other explanation for this phenomena the early Spaniards told the natives it might have been a mermaid or sirena.

statement.id: Menurut neneknya, penulis diberi tahu bahwa sungai-sungai di wilayah Ilocos tenang di permukaan tetapi berarus dan berpusaran kuat di bawah, dan karena tak ada penjelasan lain, orang Spanyol awal mengatakan kepada penduduk asli bahwa itu mungkin putri duyung atau sirena.
statement.en: According to the author's grandmother, the rivers of the Ilocos region are calm on the surface but have strong currents and undertows beneath, and with no other explanation the early Spaniards told the natives it might have been a mermaid or sirena.

claims.quote: The Ilokano term litao – the male deity of the waters, supports the Ilokano traditions and dialects

statement.id: Istilah Ilokano litao, dewa air laki-laki, mendukung tradisi dan dialek Ilokano.
statement.en: The Ilokano term litao, the male deity of the waters, supports Ilokano traditions and dialects.

claims.quote: The Mermaid Queen “ is one of the oldest stories in the Ilokano volumes, dating back to the 1600’s; The sirena is described as a kind lady with supernatural powers rather than a half human –fish creature.

statement.id: Dalam "The Mermaid Queen", salah satu cerita tertua dalam jilid Ilokano, sirena digambarkan sebagai wanita baik hati berkekuatan supernatural, bukan makhluk setengah manusia setengah ikan.
statement.en: In "The Mermaid Queen", one of the oldest stories in the Ilokano volumes, the sirena is described as a kind lady with supernatural powers rather than a half human-fish creature.

claims.quote: Thank you for guiding my fishermen back into shore during a storm, for rescuing Datu Angat’s only son from drowning and leaving a string of pearls to Datu’ Bakat’s widow after he was killed by raiding Tirong pirates.

statement.id: Dalam sebuah cerita, seorang penguasa berterima kasih kepada putri duyung karena menuntun nelayannya pulang saat badai, menyelamatkan putra tunggal Datu Angat dari tenggelam, dan meninggalkan seuntai mutiara bagi janda Datu Bakat yang dibunuh perompak Tirong.
statement.en: In a story, a ruler thanks the mermaid for guiding his fishermen back to shore in a storm, rescuing Datu Angat's only son from drowning and leaving a string of pearls to the widow of Datu Bakat, killed by raiding Tirong pirates.

claims.quote: This story is about the siren living in the Amburayan river in Tagudin. ... That same evening, the mermaid was intent in making the American her husband, changed herself into a human and knocked on his door.
claims.locator: The American and the Sirena of Amburayan

statement.id: Dalam kisah "The American and the Sirena of Amburayan", sirena yang tinggal di sungai Amburayan di Tagudin, ingin menjadikan seorang Amerika suaminya, mengubah dirinya menjadi manusia dan mengetuk pintunya.
statement.en: In "The American and the Sirena of Amburayan", the siren living in the Amburayan river in Tagudin, intent on making an American her husband, changed herself into a human and knocked on his door.

claims.quote: the rotten fishlike odor permeating from the mermaid’s skin made him sick to the stomach, causing him to pass out. ... The mermaid seeing the panic in his eyes grabbed his legs and tried to drag him towards the water’s edge.
claims.locator: The American and the Sirena of Amburayan

statement.id: Dalam kisah itu, bau amis busuk dari kulit putri duyung membuat sang pria mual dan pingsan; melihat kepanikannya, putri duyung menangkap kakinya dan mencoba menyeretnya ke tepi air.
statement.en: In that tale the rotten fishlike odor from the mermaid's skin made the man sick to the stomach and pass out; seeing his panic, the mermaid grabbed his legs and tried to drag him to the water's edge.

claims.quote: Long ago, the beautiful Serena lived with her mother by the sea. ... The litao explained she would have to drink a potion mixed with his blood to transform her into an immortal half-human and half fish creature like himself.

statement.id: Dalam sebuah kisah, Serena yang cantik tinggal bersama ibunya di tepi laut; litao menjelaskan bahwa ia harus meminum ramuan bercampur darahnya untuk berubah menjadi makhluk abadi setengah manusia setengah ikan seperti dirinya.
statement.en: In one story, the beautiful Serena lived with her mother by the sea; the litao explained that she would have to drink a potion mixed with his blood to transform her into an immortal half-human, half-fish creature like himself.

claims.quote: In an Iloko tale which Maximo Ramos recalled his mother used to tell, a boy playing at the river bank saw a beautiful woman bathing and she proved to be a sirena. He was attracted by her long hair and her charming smile and he walked to her.

statement.id: Dalam kisah Iloko yang diingat Maximo Ramos dari ibunya, seorang anak yang bermain di tepi sungai melihat wanita cantik mandi yang ternyata sirena; ia tertarik pada rambut panjang dan senyumnya dan berjalan mendekat.
statement.en: In an Iloko tale Maximo Ramos recalled his mother telling, a boy playing at the river bank saw a beautiful woman bathing who proved to be a sirena; attracted by her long hair and charming smile, he walked to her.

claims.quote: Informants from Zambales and elsewhere told Ramos that the sirena made the water rise quickly and engulfed her victim

statement.id: Informan dari Zambales dan tempat lain memberi tahu Ramos bahwa sirena membuat air naik cepat dan menelan korbannya.
statement.en: Informants from Zambales and elsewhere told Ramos that the sirena made the water rise quickly and engulfed her victim.

claims.quote: Sirena is the Spanish equivalent of mermaid, and the term appears to have driven many of the vernacular terms out of use.

statement.id: Sirena adalah padanan Spanyol untuk putri duyung, dan istilah ini tampaknya telah menggeser banyak istilah daerah hingga tak dipakai lagi.
statement.en: Sirena is the Spanish equivalent of mermaid, and the term appears to have driven many of the vernacular terms out of use.

claims.quote: LITAO – (Ilokano) Described in Isabelo de los Reyes’ book, El Folk-lore Filipino, the litao is a male anito of the waters. In Vigan, it is a small man that lives in the branches of bamboo trees along river banks and is the husband of the sirena.

statement.id: Litao (Ilokano), dijelaskan dalam buku El Folk-lore Filipino karya Isabelo de los Reyes, adalah anito air laki-laki; di Vigan ia pria kecil yang tinggal di dahan bambu di tepi sungai dan suami sirena.
statement.en: The litao (Ilokano), described in Isabelo de los Reyes' book El Folk-lore Filipino, is a male anito of the waters; in Vigan it is a small man living in bamboo branches along river banks and the husband of the sirena.

claims.quote: KATAW – (Cebuano, Hiligaynon) The Visayans call her kataw. Her name means that she looks like a person. She is a pretty woman from head to waist. She is a fish with shiny scales below the waist.

statement.id: Kataw (Cebuano, Hiligaynon): orang Visayas menyebutnya kataw; ia wanita cantik dari kepala hingga pinggang dan berupa ikan bersisik mengilap di bawah pinggang.
statement.en: The kataw (Cebuano, Hiligaynon): the Visayans call her kataw; she is a pretty woman from head to waist and a fish with shiny scales below the waist.

claims.quote: She sits on a rock drying her long hair. She sings a sweet, sad song as she sits there. She makes the fisherman row his boat to her. Then she sinks his boat and gets him.

statement.id: Kataw duduk di batu mengeringkan rambut panjangnya dan menyanyikan lagu manis yang sedih; ia membuat nelayan mendayung perahunya ke arahnya, lalu menenggelamkan perahunya dan menangkapnya.
statement.en: The kataw sits on a rock drying her long hair and sings a sweet, sad song; she makes the fisherman row his boat to her, then sinks his boat and gets him.

claims.quote: Dingdong Dantes and Marian Rivera topbill Dyesebel, GMA-7's fantaserye about the world of mermaids and underwater creatures.

statement.id: Dingdong Dantes dan Marian Rivera menjadi bintang utama Dyesebel, fantaserye GMA-7 tentang dunia putri duyung dan makhluk bawah laut.
statement.en: Dingdong Dantes and Marian Rivera topbill Dyesebel, GMA-7's fantaserye about the world of mermaids and underwater creatures.

claims.quote: For the past decades, the story of Dyesebel was shown on the big screen with five beautiful ladies portraying the role of the mermaid—Edna Luna, Vilma Santos, Alma Moreno, Alice Dixon, and Charlene Gonzales.

statement.id: Selama beberapa dekade, kisah Dyesebel ditampilkan di layar lebar dengan lima aktris memerankan putri duyung itu: Edna Luna, Vilma Santos, Alma Moreno, Alice Dixon, dan Charlene Gonzales.
statement.en: For decades the story of Dyesebel was shown on the big screen with five actresses playing the mermaid: Edna Luna, Vilma Santos, Alma Moreno, Alice Dixon and Charlene Gonzales.

claims.quote: Mars Ravelo's Dyesebel begins when the human Lucia ... delivers a beautiful baby girl. Unlike other normal babies, Lucia's child is half-human, half-fish.

statement.id: Dyesebel karya Mars Ravelo dimulai ketika Lucia, seorang manusia, melahirkan bayi perempuan cantik yang setengah manusia, setengah ikan.
statement.en: Mars Ravelo's Dyesebel begins when the human Lucia ... delivers a beautiful baby girl who, unlike other babies, is half-human, half-fish.

short_description.id: Dalam budaya Navajo, skin-walker (yee naaldlooshii) adalah penyihir berbahaya yang dapat berubah menjadi, merasuki, atau menyamar sebagai hewan.
short_description.en: In Navajo culture, a skin-walker (yee naaldlooshii) is a harmful witch who can turn into, possess, or disguise himself or herself as an animal.

long_description.id: Dalam budaya Navajo, skin-walker (yee naaldlooshii) adalah jenis penyihir berbahaya yang mampu menjelma, merasuki, atau menyamar menjadi hewan; sebutan itu tidak pernah dipakai bagi para penyembuh. Nama yee naaldlooshii diterjemahkan 'dengan perantaraannya, ia berjalan dengan empat kaki'. Penyihir ini dipandang sebagai kebalikan nilai-nilai Navajo, yang menjalankan upacara jahat dan sihir manipulatif, berlawanan dengan karya baik para dukun penyembuh. Mereka dianggap jenis penyihir paling berbahaya, dan penyihir dipandang bukan sebagai makhluk gaib melainkan pihak yang memanfaatkan kekuatan jahat.
long_description.en: In Navajo culture a skin-walker (yee naaldlooshii) is a kind of harmful witch able to become, possess, or pose as an animal; the term is never applied to healers. The name yee naaldlooshii is translated 'by means of it, it goes on all fours'. These witches are seen as the opposite of Navajo values, performing malevolent ceremonies and manipulative magic in contrast to the beneficial works of medicine people. They are regarded as the most dangerous type of witch, and witches are not seen as supernatural beings but as harnessing the power of evil.

long_description.id: Menurut penuturan tradisional, mereka adalah penyihir sakti yang memperoleh kemampuan berubah menjadi hewan sesuka hati setelah melakukan berbagai perbuatan keji; sumber lain menyebut penyihir harus membunuh anggota keluarga dekat dalam ritus inisiasi rahasia, dan dalam sebagian kisah para penyihir itu semula adalah penyembuh atau pemandu rohani. Mereka biasanya tampil sebagai beruang, puma, koyote, anjing, rubah, atau serigala, dan memilih wujud menurut kemampuan yang dibutuhkan. Mereka disebut skinwalker karena mengenakan kulit hewan yang menjadi wujud mereka, dan karena itu mengenakan kulit hewan pemangsa dianggap tabu dalam budaya Navajo.
long_description.en: Traditional accounts describe them as powerful sorcerers who, after a series of wicked deeds, acquire the power to turn into animals whenever they wish; another source says the witch must kill a close family member in a secret initiation rite, and in some stories such witches began as healers or spiritual guides. They usually appear as bears, cougars, coyotes, dogs, foxes, or wolves, choosing a shape for the abilities they need. The name comes from their wearing the skins of the animals they become, which is why wearing the pelt of any predatory animal is taboo in Navajo culture.

long_description.id: Skin-walker dikatakan dapat menguasai korban dengan beradu tatap, membaca pikiran, menimbulkan penyakit atau kematian, mengendalikan makhluk nokturnal, memanggil roh orang mati, dan menghidupkan kembali mayat. Mereka sering mengetuk jendela dan pintu atau menimbulkan bunyi menggores. Ketakutan terhadap mereka memicu Pembersihan Penyihir Navajo tahun 1878, yang menewaskan empat puluh orang yang dicurigai sebagai penyihir.
long_description.en: Skin-walkers are said to be able to hold victims in their power by locking eyes, read minds, cause illness or death, control nocturnal creatures, call up the spirits of the dead, and reanimate corpses. They often rap on windows and doors or make scraping noises. Dread of them contributed to the Navajo Witch Purge of 1878, which killed forty suspected witches.

long_description.id: Legenda skin-walker tertanam dalam tradisi Navajo dan jarang dibicarakan dengan orang luar, sebagian karena tabu budaya dan kurangnya pemahaman konteks oleh orang non-Navajo.
long_description.en: The skin-walker legend is rooted deep in Navajo tradition and seldom shared with outsiders, partly from cultural taboos and partly because non-Navajos lack the context.

cultural_context.id: Penyihir skin-walker dipandang sebagai kebalikan nilai-nilai Navajo, berlawanan dengan karya baik para dukun penyembuh; legendanya jarang dibicarakan dengan orang luar.
cultural_context.en: Skin-walker witches are seen as the antithesis of Navajo values, in contrast to the beneficial works of medicine people; the legend is rarely discussed with outsiders.

short_description.id: Thunderbird adalah roh menyerupai burung dalam sejarah dan budaya masyarakat Pribumi Amerika Utara. Ia dianggap makhluk gaib yang berkuasa dan kuat, dan dikaitkan dengan guntur dan petir.
short_description.en: The thunderbird is a birdlike spirit in the history and culture of North American Indigenous peoples. It is considered a supernatural being of power and strength, and is linked with thunder and lightning.

long_description.id: Thunderbird adalah roh menyerupai burung dalam sejarah dan budaya masyarakat Pribumi Amerika Utara dan dianggap sebagai makhluk gaib yang berkuasa dan kuat. Ia sering digambarkan dalam seni, lagu, dan sejarah lisan banyak budaya Pesisir Barat Laut Pasifik, tetapi juga ditemukan dalam berbagai bentuk di antara sebagian masyarakat di Barat Daya Amerika, Pesisir Timur AS, Danau-Danau Besar, dan Dataran Besar. Di berbagai budaya, thunderbird umumnya digambarkan sebagai burung pemangsa atau campuran manusia dan burung, dan perannya berbeda-beda dalam tiap tradisi.
long_description.en: The thunderbird is a birdlike spirit in the history and culture of North American Indigenous peoples and is considered a supernatural being of power and strength. It features often in the art, songs, and spoken histories of many Pacific Northwest Coast cultures and also appears in other forms among some peoples of the American Southwest, the US East Coast, the Great Lakes, and the Great Plains. Thunderbirds are usually pictured as birds of prey or as human-bird hybrids, and the figure plays varying roles in different traditions.

long_description.id: Dalam penuturan Algonquian, thunderbird menciptakan guntur dengan mengepakkan sayap; dalam penuturan Algonquian dan Iroquois ia menciptakan petir dengan mengerjapkan mata. Dalam mitologi Algonquian, thunderbird menguasai dunia atas sementara dunia bawah dikuasai panter bawah air atau Ular Bertanduk Besar. Ia melemparkan sambaran petir kepada makhluk dunia bawah itu. Sumber lain menyebut bahwa dalam tradisi lain thunderbird memburu paus dengan sayap yang melepaskan anak panah, dan bahwa di antara sebagian Bangsa Pertama Dataran badai petir adalah pertarungan melawan ular derik raksasa.
long_description.en: In Algonquian tellings the thunderbird creates thunder by flapping its wings; in Algonquian and Iroquois tellings it creates lightning by flashing its eyes. In Algonquian mythology the thunderbird rules the upper world, while the underwater panther or Great Horned Serpent rules the underworld, and the thunderbird hurls lightning bolts at the creatures below. Another source adds that in other traditions the thunderbird hunts whales using its wings to shoot arrows, and that among some Plains First Nations thunderstorms are a contest against a huge rattlesnake.

long_description.id: Thunderbird sering dipandang sebagai pelindung yang kadang turun tangan membela manusia, tetapi mengharapkan penghormatan, doa, dan persembahan. Versi Ojibwe menyatakan thunderbird diciptakan oleh Nanabozho untuk melawan roh bawah air dan juga menghukum manusia yang melanggar aturan moral. Dalam tradisi Ho-Chunk, pria yang mendapat penglihatan tentang thunderbird saat berpuasa menyendiri akan menjadi kepala perang. Orang yang selamat dari sambaran petir sering menjadi syaman karena dianggap menerima kekuatan burung itu.
long_description.en: Thunderbirds are often seen as protectors who sometimes step in for people, yet expect veneration, prayers, and gifts. In the Ojibwe version Nanabozho made the thunderbirds to battle the underwater spirits, and they also punished people who broke moral rules. In Ho-Chunk tradition, a man granted a thunderbird vision while fasting alone becomes a war chief. People who survived being struck by lightning often became shamans because they were thought to have received the power of the bird.

long_description.id: Sumber lain menggambarkan thunderbird sebagai burung raksasa yang menurut banyak suku di barat laut cukup besar untuk membawa paus pembunuh dalam cakarnya. Di sebagian suku ia dianggap kekuatan alam yang sangat suci, di suku lain sekadar makhluk kuat dalam dunia hewan. Dalam tradisi Gros Ventre, ialah yang memberikan pipa suci kepada rakyat, dan pada sebagian budaya thunderbird menjadi hewan klan serta lambang di tiang totem Pesisir Barat Laut.
long_description.en: A further source describes the thunderbird as an enormous bird that, according to many Northwestern tribes, could carry a killer whale in its talons. In some tribes it is an extremely sacred force of nature, in others merely a powerful member of the animal kingdom. In Gros Ventre tradition it gave the sacred pipe to the people, and in some cultures the thunderbird is a clan animal and a totem pole crest on the Northwest Coast.
