claims.quote: The thunderbird is a mythological birdlike spirit in North American Indigenous peoples' history and culture.

statement.id: Thunderbird adalah roh serupa burung mitologis dalam sejarah dan kebudayaan masyarakat pribumi Amerika Utara.
statement.en: The thunderbird is a mythological birdlike spirit in North American Indigenous peoples' history and culture.

claims.quote: The thunderbird is a mythological birdlike spirit in North American Indigenous peoples' history and culture. It is considered a supernatural being of power and strength.

statement.id: Thunderbird dianggap sebagai makhluk gaib yang berkuasa dan kuat.
statement.en: The thunderbird is considered a supernatural being of power and strength.

claims.quote: In Algonquian mythology, the thunderbird controls the upper world while the underworld is governed by the underwater panther or Great Horned Serpent.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Algonquian, thunderbird menguasai alam atas sementara dunia bawah diperintah makhluk lain.
statement.en: In Algonquian mythology, the thunderbird controls the upper world while the underworld is governed by the underwater panther or Great Horned Serpent.

claims.quote: Across cultures, thunderbirds are generally depicted as birds of prey, or hybrids of humans and birds.

statement.id: Di berbagai kebudayaan makhluk ini digambarkan sebagai burung pemangsa atau perpaduan manusia dan burung.
statement.en: Across cultures, thunderbirds are generally depicted as birds of prey, or hybrids of humans and birds.

claims.quote: The thunderbird is said to create thunder by flapping its wings in Algonquian tellings, and lightning by flashing its eyes in both Algonquian and Iroquois tellings.

statement.id: Dalam penuturan Algonquian, thunderbird dikatakan menciptakan guntur dengan mengepakkan sayap; dalam penuturan Algonquian dan Iroquois, ia menciptakan petir dengan mengerjapkan matanya.
statement.en: The thunderbird is said to create thunder by flapping its wings in Algonquian tellings, and lightning by flashing its eyes in both Algonquian and Iroquois tellings.

claims.quote: Thunderbirds are often viewed as protectors, sometimes intervening on people's behalf, but expecting veneration, prayers, and gifts.

statement.id: Thunderbird sering dipandang sebagai pelindung yang kadang turun tangan membela manusia, tetapi mengharapkan penghormatan, doa, dan persembahan.
statement.en: Thunderbirds are often viewed as protectors, sometimes intervening on people's behalf, but expecting veneration, prayers, and gifts.

claims.quote: The Ojibwe version of the myth states that the thunderbirds were created by Nanabozho to fight the underwater spirits. Thunderbirds also punished humans who broke moral rules.

statement.id: Versi Ojibwe menyatakan bahwa thunderbird diciptakan oleh Nanabozho untuk melawan roh-roh bawah air. Thunderbird juga menghukum manusia yang melanggar aturan moral.
statement.en: The Ojibwe version of the myth states that the thunderbirds were created by Nanabozho to fight the underwater spirits; thunderbirds also punished humans who broke moral rules.

claims.quote: In Menominee (Northern Wisconsin) folklore, thunderbirds live on a far-western mountain that floats. The thunderbirds control the rain and hail, and delight in fighting. They continually fight the great horned snakes (the Misikinubik) to keep them from overrunning the earth and devouring humankind.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Menominee (Wisconsin utara), thunderbird tinggal di gunung terapung di sebelah barat jauh, mengendalikan hujan dan hujan es, gemar bertarung, dan terus melawan ular bertanduk besar (Misikinubik) agar tidak menguasai bumi dan melahap umat manusia.
statement.en: In Menominee (Northern Wisconsin) folklore, thunderbirds live on a far-western mountain that floats, control the rain and hail, delight in fighting, and continually fight the great horned snakes (the Misikinubik) to keep them from overrunning the earth and devouring humankind.

claims.quote: Ho-Chunk tradition states that a man who has a vision of a thunderbird during a solitary fast will become a war chief of the people.

statement.id: Tradisi Ho-Chunk menyatakan bahwa seorang pria yang mendapat penglihatan tentang thunderbird saat berpuasa menyendiri akan menjadi kepala perang bagi rakyatnya.
statement.en: Ho-Chunk tradition states that a man who has a vision of a thunderbird during a solitary fast will become a war chief of the people.

claims.quote: The thunderbird creates not just thunder (with its wing-flapping) but also lightning bolts, which it casts at the underworld creatures.

statement.id: Thunderbird menciptakan bukan hanya guntur (dengan kepakan sayap) tetapi juga sambaran petir yang ia lemparkan kepada makhluk-makhluk dunia bawah.
statement.en: The thunderbird creates not just thunder (with its wing-flapping) but also lightning bolts, which it casts at the underworld creatures.

claims.quote: Petroglyphs of thunderbirds are found near Twin Bluffs, Wisconsin. They are in a shelter that was probably used c. 250 BCE to 1500 CE.

statement.id: Petroglif thunderbird ditemukan dekat Twin Bluffs, Wisconsin, di sebuah ceruk yang kemungkinan digunakan sekitar 250 SM sampai 1500 M.
statement.en: Petroglyphs of thunderbirds are found near Twin Bluffs, Wisconsin, in a shelter that was probably used c. 250 BCE to 1500 CE.

claims.quote: Stories about the struggle between the Thunderbird and Whale (q.v.) have been traditionally told by various Pacific coast tribal groups.

statement.id: Kisah tentang pergulatan antara Thunderbird dan Paus secara tradisional diceritakan oleh berbagai kelompok suku di pesisir Pasifik.
statement.en: Stories about the struggle between the Thunderbird and Whale have been traditionally told by various Pacific coast tribal groups.

claims.quote: The thunderbird is a mythological birdlike spirit in North American Indigenous peoples' history and culture. ... It is frequently depicted in the art, songs, and oral histories of many Pacific Northwest Coast cultures, but is also found in various forms among some peoples of the American Southwest, US East Coast, Great Lakes, and Great Plains.

statement.id: Thunderbird sering digambarkan dalam seni, lagu, dan sejarah lisan banyak budaya Pesisir Barat Laut Pasifik, tetapi juga ditemukan dalam berbagai bentuk di antara sebagian masyarakat di Barat Daya Amerika, Pesisir Timur AS, Danau-Danau Besar, dan Dataran Besar.
statement.en: The thunderbird is frequently depicted in the art, songs, and oral histories of many Pacific Northwest Coast cultures, but is also found in various forms among some peoples of the American Southwest, US East Coast, Great Lakes, and Great Plains.

claims.quote: Although Indigenous traditions hold that the Thunderbird is not a physical entity but a spirit, the Thunderbird also lends its namesake to a loose subset of allegedly undiscovered animals reported over North America.

statement.id: Meskipun tradisi Pribumi memandang Thunderbird sebagai roh dan bukan makhluk fisik, namanya juga dipinjam untuk sekelompok hewan yang diduga belum ditemukan dan dilaporkan di seluruh Amerika Utara.
statement.en: Although Indigenous traditions hold that the Thunderbird is not a physical entity but a spirit, its name is also lent to a loose subset of allegedly undiscovered animals reported over North America.

claims.quote: Thunderbird is a supernatural creature prominent in many Indigenous traditional stories. The thunderbird plays varying roles in different Indigenous traditions.

statement.id: Thunderbird adalah makhluk gaib yang menonjol dalam banyak kisah tradisional masyarakat Pribumi dan berperan berbeda-beda dalam tiap tradisi.
statement.en: Thunderbird is a supernatural creature prominent in many Indigenous traditional stories and plays varying roles in different Indigenous traditions.

claims.quote: In some Indigenous traditional stories, thunder and lightning are attributed to the thunderbird. It produces thunder by flapping its wings and lightning by opening and closing its eyes.

statement.id: Dalam sebagian kisah tradisional Pribumi, guntur dan petir dikaitkan dengan thunderbird; ia menghasilkan guntur dengan mengepakkan sayap dan petir dengan membuka dan menutup mata.
statement.en: In some Indigenous traditional stories, thunder and lightning are attributed to the thunderbird, which produces thunder by flapping its wings and lightning by opening and closing its eyes.

claims.quote: In other traditions, the thunderbird is said to hunt whales, using its wings to shoot arrows. Among some Plains First Nations, thunderstorms are a contest between the thunderbird and a huge rattlesnake.

statement.id: Dalam tradisi lain, thunderbird dikatakan memburu paus dengan sayap yang melepaskan anak panah. Di antara sebagian Bangsa Pertama Dataran, badai petir adalah pertarungan antara thunderbird dan seekor ular derik raksasa.
statement.en: In other traditions the thunderbird is said to hunt whales, using its wings to shoot arrows; among some Plains First Nations, thunderstorms are a contest between the thunderbird and a huge rattlesnake.

claims.quote: Individuals who had been struck by lightning and survived often became Shamans, for they had received the power of the bird

statement.id: Orang yang pernah tersambar petir dan selamat sering menjadi syaman, karena mereka dianggap telah menerima kekuatan burung itu.
statement.en: Individuals who had been struck by lightning and survived often became shamans, for they had received the power of the bird.

claims.quote: Thunderbird is described as an enormous bird (according to many Northwestern tribes, large enough to carry a killer whale in its talons as an eagle carries a fish) who is responsible for the sound of thunder (and in some cases lightning as well.)

statement.id: Thunderbird digambarkan sebagai burung raksasa (menurut banyak suku di barat laut, cukup besar untuk membawa paus pembunuh dalam cakarnya seperti elang membawa ikan) yang bertanggung jawab atas bunyi guntur (dan dalam beberapa kasus petir juga).
statement.en: Thunderbird is described as an enormous bird (according to many Northwestern tribes, large enough to carry a killer whale in its talons as an eagle carries a fish) responsible for the sound of thunder (and in some cases lightning as well).

claims.quote: In some tribes, Thunderbirds are considered extremely sacred forces of nature, while in others, they are treated like powerful but otherwise ordinary members of the animal kingdom. In Gros Ventre tradition, it was Thunderbird (Bha'a) who gave the sacred pipe to the people.

statement.id: Di sebagian suku, thunderbird dianggap kekuatan alam yang sangat suci, sedangkan di suku lain diperlakukan sebagai anggota dunia hewan yang kuat namun biasa; dalam tradisi Gros Ventre, Thunderbird (Bha'a) yang memberikan pipa suci kepada rakyat.
statement.en: In some tribes thunderbirds are considered extremely sacred forces of nature, while in others they are treated as powerful but otherwise ordinary members of the animal kingdom; in Gros Ventre tradition it was Thunderbird (Bha'a) who gave the sacred pipe to the people.

claims.quote: Thunderbirds are also used as clan animals in some Native American cultures. Tribes with Thunderbird Clans include the Kwakiutl and Ho-Chunk tribes. On the Northwest Coast, the thunderbird symbol is often used as a totem pole crest.

statement.id: Thunderbird juga dipakai sebagai hewan klan di sebagian budaya Pribumi Amerika; suku dengan Klan Thunderbird mencakup Kwakiutl dan Ho-Chunk, dan di Pesisir Barat Laut simbol thunderbird sering dipakai sebagai lambang di tiang totem.

short_description.id: Unhcegila adalah makhluk mirip ular bersisik raksasa dalam mitologi Lakota yang dianggap menyebabkan banyak hilangnya orang dan kematian.
short_description.en: Unhcegila is a giant scaly serpentoid creature of Lakota mythology blamed for many unexplained disappearances and deaths.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Lakota, Unhcegila (juga Unk Cekula) adalah makhluk mirip ular yang bertanggung jawab atas banyak hilangnya orang dan kematian yang tak terjelaskan. Pasangan laki-lakinya dikenal sebagai Unk Tehi. Halaman Native Languages menyebut Unktehila sebagai ular air bertanduk dalam mitologi Lakota dan Dakota, lawan utama Burung Guntur Wakinyan.
long_description.en: Unhcegila (also Unk Cekula) is a serpent-like being of Lakota mythology that was blamed for numerous unexplained disappearances and deaths; Unk Tehi is known as her male counterpart. The Native Languages page calls Unktehila the horned water serpent of Lakota and Dakota mythology, the diametrical opponent of the Thunderbird Wakinyan.

long_description.id: Pada mulanya ia digambarkan tanpa bentuk yang nyata, bermata api, dengan mulut bertaring yang diselubungi massa seperti asap atau awan. Kemudian wujudnya terungkap besar, berbadan panjang bersisik dengan zirah alami yang hampir tidak dapat ditembus; matanya menyala dengan kelaparan murka, cakarnya seperti besi, dan suaranya seperti guntur. Siapa pun yang memandangnya menjadi buta atau gila.
long_description.en: She was first described as having no real shape or form, with eyes of fire and a fanged mouth shrouded in a smoky or cloudy mass. Later she was shown to be enormous, her long scaly body protected by natural armor that almost nothing could pierce; wrathful hunger blazed in her eyes, her claws were iron-like and her voice rolled like thunder. Whoever looks upon her goes blind or insane.

long_description.id: Kelemahannya adalah bintik ketujuh di torsonya, yang menutupi jantungnya; untuk membunuhnya orang harus menembakkan panah obat pada celah di zirah alaminya itu. Kisah kematiannya berbeda-beda: dua saudara kembar, salah satunya buta, membunuhnya dengan panah pemberian tabib perempuan, atau Wakinyan menewaskannya dengan badai dan petir setelah ia membanjiri daratan. Menurut satu mitos, matinya makhluk ini meninggalkan formasi batu gersang dan kerangka di Badlands.
long_description.en: Her one weak point is the seventh spot on her torso, with her heart behind it; killing her requires a medicine arrow shot into that flaw in her armor. Stories of her death differ: two twin brothers, one of them blind, kill her with arrows from a medicine woman, or Wakinyan kills her with a storm and lightning after she floods the land. According to one myth her death left the arid rock formations and skeletons of the Badlands.

long_description.id: Menurut kisah-kisah, makhluk ini dan pasangannya sampai ke Black Hills (Pahá Sápa) dan mencari rumah baru di pegunungan; dalam satu mitos ia membunuh beruang raksasa yang tubuhnya menjadi Bear Butte. Dorsey, dalam kajian lama tentang kultus bangsa Dakota, mencatat bahwa Unkteḣi, yang dalam dialek Teton disebut Ŭñktcexila atau Uŋkćeġila, adalah banyak dewa air yang paling berkuasa dan dianggap memakan roh manusia; bawahan mereka adalah ular, kadal, katak, hantu, burung hantu, dan elang. Konon makhluk ini juga punya keturunan yang harus dibunuh suku-suku ketika mulai memangsa manusia. Dalam budaya populer, kisahnya muncul dalam komik Marvel Comics Presents dan dalam film Dreamkeeper (2003).
long_description.en: In the accounts the creature and her companion travel to the Black Hills (Pahá Sápa), where they look for a new home in the mountains; in one myth she kills a giant bear whose body becomes Bear Butte. Dorsey, in an old study of Dakota cults, notes that the Unkteḣi, called Ŭñktcexila or Uŋkćeġila in the Teton dialect, are many water gods, the most powerful of all, thought to feed on the spirits of human beings; their subordinates are serpents, lizards, frogs, ghosts, owls and eagles. The creature is also said to have had offspring that the tribes had to kill when they began feeding on people. In popular culture her story appears in Marvel Comics Presents and in the film Dreamkeeper (2003).

claims.quote: is a serpentoid creature which was responsible for many unexplained disappearances and deaths. Her male counterpart is known as Unk Tehi.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Lakota, Unhcegila adalah makhluk mirip ular yang dianggap penyebab banyak kematian dan kehilangan misterius; pasangan jantannya bernama Unk Tehi.
statement.en: In Lakota mythology, Unhcegila is a serpent-like creature blamed for many unexplained disappearances and deaths; her male counterpart is Unk Tehi.

claims.quote: As time went on further, her form was exposed as being massive, with a long scaly body whose natural armor was almost impenetrable.

statement.id: Belakangan wujudnya terungkap sangat besar, bertubuh panjang bersisik dengan pelindung alami yang hampir tak tertembus.
statement.en: Her form was later revealed as massive, with a long scaly body whose armor was almost impenetrable.

claims.quote: Whoever looked upon her will become blind or go insane.

statement.id: Siapa pun yang memandangnya akan buta atau gila.
statement.en: Whoever looks upon her goes blind or insane.

claims.quote: Her weakness is the seventh spot on her torso, behind which lies her heart. To kill her, one has to shoot a medicine arrow at this flaw in her natural armor.

statement.id: Kelemahannya adalah titik ketujuh di badannya, tempat jantungnya berada; untuk membunuhnya, panah obat harus ditembakkan ke titik itu.
statement.en: Her weakness is the seventh spot on her torso, over her heart; to kill her, one must shoot a medicine arrow there.

claims.quote: She was described at first as having no real shape or form; she had eyes of fire, and a fanged mouth that was shrouded in a smoky or cloudy mass.

statement.id: Pada mulanya ia digambarkan tanpa bentuk yang nyata, bermata api, dengan mulut bertaring yang diselubungi massa seperti asap atau awan.
statement.en: She was first described as having no real shape or form, with eyes of fire and a fanged mouth shrouded in a smoky or cloudy mass.

claims.quote: Her eyes burned with wrathful hunger, her claws were like iron, and her voice raged like thunder rolling in the clouds.

statement.id: Matanya menyala dengan kelaparan murka, cakarnya seperti besi, dan suaranya mengamuk seperti guntur bergulung di awan.
statement.en: Her eyes burned with wrathful hunger, her claws were like iron and her voice raged like thunder rolling in the clouds.

claims.quote: Until they made their way to the Black Hills (Pahá Sápa) and sought a new home in the mountains.

statement.id: Menurut kisah-kisah itu, makhluk ini dan pasangannya akhirnya sampai ke Black Hills (Pahá Sápa) dan mencari rumah baru di pegunungan.
statement.en: According to the accounts, the creature and her companion finally made their way to the Black Hills (Pahá Sápa) and sought a new home in the mountains.

claims.quote: In one myth, Unk Cekula fights with and kills a giant bear, whose fallen body produced the Bear Butte in the Black Hills.

statement.id: Dalam satu mitos, Unk Cekula bertarung dengan beruang raksasa dan membunuhnya; tubuh beruang yang rubuh itu membentuk Bear Butte di Black Hills.
statement.en: In one myth Unk Cekula fights and kills a giant bear, whose fallen body produced Bear Butte in the Black Hills.

claims.quote: Alternatively, two twin brothers, one of whom was blind, killed Unk Cekula using arrows given to them by a medicine woman.

statement.id: Menurut versi lain, dua saudara kembar, salah satunya buta, membunuh Unk Cekula dengan panah pemberian seorang tabib perempuan.
statement.en: Alternatively, two twin brothers, one of them blind, killed Unk Cekula with arrows given to them by a medicine woman.

claims.quote: In another myth, Unk Cekula emerged from the primordial waters to flood the land. The resulting devastation angered Wakinyan, who flapped his wings to create a great storm to dry up the land and shoot lightning, killing Unk Cekula.

statement.id: Dalam mitos lain, Unk Cekula muncul dari perairan purba dan membanjiri daratan; kehancuran itu membuat Wakinyan murka, yang mengepakkan sayapnya menciptakan badai besar untuk mengeringkan tanah dan menembakkan petir sehingga membunuh Unk Cekula.
statement.en: In another myth Unk Cekula emerged from the primordial waters and flooded the land; the devastation angered Wakinyan, who flapped his wings to create a great storm to dry the land and shoot lightning, killing Unk Cekula.

claims.quote: As she finally died, the Sun scorched her flesh and dried up the land, resulting in the arid rock formations and skeletons found in the Badlands

statement.id: Ketika ia akhirnya mati, Matahari menghanguskan dagingnya dan mengeringkan tanah, menghasilkan formasi batu gersang dan kerangka yang ditemukan di Badlands.
statement.en: As she finally died the Sun scorched her flesh and dried up the land, resulting in the arid rock formations and skeletons found in the Badlands.

claims.quote: It was learned that the creature had offspring, and the tribes had to kill them when they began feeding on people.

statement.id: Diketahui makhluk itu memiliki keturunan, dan suku-suku harus membunuh mereka ketika mulai memangsa manusia.
statement.en: It was learned that the creature had offspring, and the tribes had to kill them when they began feeding on people.

claims.quote: A fictionalized version of the myth appeared in a Marvel Comics Presents story arc starring Wolverine.

statement.id: Versi fiksi mitos ini muncul dalam alur cerita Marvel Comics Presents dengan Wolverine sebagai bintang.
statement.en: A fictionalized version of the myth appeared in a Marvel Comics Presents story arc starring Wolverine.

claims.quote: She appears in a story told in the 2003 film Dreamkeeper, in which Eagle Boy is the one who slays her with weapons given to him by an old woman.

statement.id: Ia muncul dalam kisah yang dituturkan dalam film Dreamkeeper (2003), tempat Eagle Boy membunuhnya dengan senjata pemberian seorang perempuan tua.
statement.en: She appears in a story told in the 2003 film Dreamkeeper, in which Eagle Boy slays her with weapons given to him by an old woman.

claims.quote: Unktehila is the horned water serpent of Lakota and Dakota mythology. It is the diametrical opponent of the Thunderbird Wakinyan, and there are many legends about epic fights between the two.

statement.id: Menurut Native Languages of the Americas, Unktehila adalah ular air bertanduk dalam mitologi Lakota dan Dakota, lawan utama Burung Guntur Wakinyan, dan ada banyak legenda tentang pertarungan dahsyat keduanya.
statement.en: According to Native Languages of the Americas, Unktehila is the horned water serpent of Lakota and Dakota mythology, the diametrical opponent of the Thunderbird Wakinyan, with many legends of epic fights between the two.

claims.quote: Name: Unktehila Tribal affiliation: Dakota, Lakota Alternate spellings: Uncegila, Unhcegila, Unktehi

statement.id: Halaman itu mencantumkan nama Unktehila, berafiliasi suku Dakota dan Lakota, dengan ejaan lain Uncegila, Unhcegila, dan Unktehi.
statement.en: The page lists the name Unktehila, tribal affiliation Dakota and Lakota, with alternate spellings Uncegila, Unhcegila and Unktehi.

claims.quote: THE UNKTEḢI, OR SUBAQUATIC AND SUBTERRANEAN POWERS. ... The gods of this name, for there are many, are the most powerful of all. In their external form they are said to resemble the ox, only they are of immense proportions. They can extend their horns and tails so as to reach the skies.
claims.locator: The Unkteḣi, or subaquatic and subterranean powers

statement.id: Dorsey menulis bahwa para Unkteḣi (kekuatan bawah air dan bawah tanah) adalah banyak dewa, yang paling berkuasa dari semuanya; rupa luarnya disebut seperti sapi jantan berukuran sangat besar, dan mereka dapat memanjangkan tanduk dan ekornya hingga mencapai langit.
statement.en: Dorsey writes that the Unkteḣi (subaquatic and subterranean powers) are many gods, the most powerful of all; in outward form they are said to resemble the ox but of immense proportions, and they can extend their horns and tails to reach the skies.

claims.quote: According to the Dakota cosmogony, this was done by the Unkteḣi, called in the Teton dialect Ŭñktcexila or Uŋkćeġila.
claims.locator: The Unkteḣi, or subaquatic and subterranean powers

statement.id: Menurut Dorsey, dalam kosmogoni Dakota hal itu dilakukan oleh Unkteḣi, yang dalam dialek Teton disebut Ŭñktcexila atau Uŋkćeġila.
statement.en: According to Dorsey, in the Dakota cosmogony this was done by the Unkteḣi, called in the Teton dialect Ŭñktcexila or Uŋkćeġila.

claims.quote: The Unkteḣi are thought to feed on the spirits of human beings, and references to this occur in the mystic songs.
claims.locator: The Unkteḣi, or subaquatic and subterranean powers

statement.id: Menurut Dorsey, Unkteḣi dianggap memakan roh manusia, dan hal itu disinggung dalam lagu-lagu mistik.
statement.en: According to Dorsey, the Unkteḣi are thought to feed on the spirits of human beings, as referred to in the mystic songs.

claims.quote: The subordinates of the Unkteḣi are serpents, lizards, frogs, ghosts, owls, and eagles. The Unkteḣi made the earth and men
claims.locator: The Unkteḣi, or subaquatic and subterranean powers

statement.id: Menurut Dorsey, bawahan Unkteḣi adalah ular, kadal, katak, hantu, burung hantu, dan elang, dan Unkteḣi menciptakan bumi dan manusia.
statement.en: According to Dorsey, the subordinates of the Unkteḣi are serpents, lizards, frogs, ghosts, owls and eagles, and the Unkteḣi made the earth and men.

claims.quote: It will, however, suffice to mention Unktéhi, or Unktéxi, their Neptune or divine ruler of the waters, whose name also designated a fabled monster of the deep and the whale of the salt-water.

statement.id: Menurut Gatschet, Unktéhi atau Unktéxi adalah "Neptunus" atau penguasa ilahi perairan bagi mereka, dan namanya juga menyebut monster laut dalam yang diceritakan serta paus air asin.
statement.en: According to Gatschet, Unktéhi or Unktéxi was their "Neptune" or divine ruler of the waters, and the name also designated a fabled monster of the deep and the whale of the salt water.

short_description.id: Unuqay adalah makhluk mengerikan dalam mitologi Azerbaijan, wujud kambing dari Hal anası, yang menghadang pengendara di dekat kuburan dan meninggalkan cacat seperti gagap atau pincang.
short_description.en: Unuqay is a monster of Azerbaijan mythology, the goat form of Hal anası, which waylays riders near cemeteries and leaves them with defects such as stammering or limping.

long_description.id: Unuqay adalah makhluk mengerikan dalam mitologi Azerbaijan, yang juga dipahami sebagai wujud kambing dari Hal anası. Ia biasanya menghadang penunggang kuda dan kusir kereta dalam rupa kambing tanpa pemilik, memperdaya mereka, lalu meninggalkan cacat yang lama seperti gagap atau pincang.
long_description.en: Unuqay is a monster of Azerbaijan mythology, understood as the goat form of Hal anası. It typically confronts riders and cart drivers as an ownerless goat, deceives them, and leaves them with lasting defects such as a stammer or a limp.

long_description.id: Makhluk ini terlihat di sekitar kuburan dan paling sering menampakkan diri saat senja. Wujud hewannya kambing jantan atau anak kambing, kebanyakan berwarna putih. Begitu orang sadar bahwa yang dibawanya bukan kambing biasa, kaki makhluk itu memanjang dan tenaganya bertambah; ia lalu duduk di punggung kuda seperti manusia dan menjepit si penunggang.
long_description.en: The creature is seen around cemeteries and appears most often at dusk. Its animal form is a billy goat or kid, mostly white. As soon as a person realises the goat is no ordinary animal, its legs stretch out and its strength increases; it then sits on the horse like a human and crushes the rider.

long_description.id: Seperti Hal, Unuqay takut jarum dan peniti, sehingga benda-benda itu dipakai untuk menangkapnya; titik lemahnya adalah leher dan urat pinggang. Kisah-kisah yang dicatat di Göynük menambahkan bahwa ia juga takut cahaya dan sekop, karena jarum menjahit kain kafan dan sekop menggali kubur. Dalam beberapa teks yang jarang, ia membawa orang ke dalam kuburan atau mencelakai bayi dalam kandungan.
long_description.en: Like Hal, Unuqay fears needles and pins, so these are used to catch it; its weak points are the neck and the lower-back vein. Accounts recorded in Göynük add that it also fears light and the shovel, since the needle sews the shroud and the shovel digs the grave. In a few rare texts it lures people into the cemetery or harms an unborn child.

long_description.id: Sebagian besar kisah Unuqay berasal dari desa-desa Göynük di Şəki, tempat 16 teks tentangnya dicatat. Penyusun kumpulan folklor dari daerah itu menyebut Unuqay sebagai tokoh yang sebelumnya tak dikenal dalam folklor Azerbaijan, tetapi punya padanan pada bangsa türk lain. Nama lainnya adalah Maşşax dan Kafdar.
long_description.en: Most Unuqay accounts come from the Göynük villages of Şəki, where 16 texts about it were recorded. The compiler of the folklore collection from that area calls Unuqay a figure previously unknown in Azerbaijan folklore but with analogues among other türk peoples. Its other names are Maşşax and Kafdar.

claims.quote: Unuqay və ya Hal anasının keçi dönərgəsi — Azərbaycan mifologiyasında bədheybət.

statement.id: Unuqay, atau wujud kambing (keçi dönərgəsi) Hal anası, adalah makhluk mengerikan (bədheybət) dalam mitologi Azerbaijan (Azərbaycan).
statement.en: Unuqay, or the goat transformation (keçi dönərgəsi) of Hal anası, is a monster (bədheybət) in Azerbaijan (Azərbaycan) mythology.

claims.quote: Atlıların və arabaçıların qarşısına keçi formasında çıxaraq onları aldadır və uzun müddət davam edəcək tibbi qüsurlara (kəkələmə, axsama) səbəb olur.

statement.id: Ia muncul di depan penunggang kuda dan kusir dalam wujud kambing (keçi), menipu mereka, dan menimbulkan cacat yang lama (kəkələmə, axsama: gagap, pincang).
statement.en: It appears before riders and cart drivers in the form of a goat (keçi), deceives them, and causes long-lasting defects (kəkələmə, axsama: stammering, limping).

claims.quote: Unuqay qəbiristanlıq ətrafı ərazilərdə görülür. O, əsasən axşamüstü, qaranlıq çökərkən insanların rastına çıxır.

statement.id: Unuqay terlihat di sekitar kuburan (qəbiristanlıq) dan terutama menjumpai orang saat senja, ketika gelap turun (qaranlıq çökərkən).
statement.en: Unuqay is seen around cemeteries (qəbiristanlıq) and meets people mainly at dusk, as darkness falls (qaranlıq çökərkən).

claims.quote: Yolçu keçinin bədheybət olduğunu bildikdən sonra onun ayaqları uzanmağa başlayır. Ayaqlarının uzanması ilə birlikdə Unuqayın gücü də artır.

statement.id: Setelah pengembara tahu kambing itu makhluk mengerikan, kakinya mulai memanjang (ayaqları uzanmağa), dan seiring itu kekuatan (gücü) Unuqay bertambah.
statement.en: Once the traveller realises the goat is a monster, its legs begin to lengthen (ayaqları uzanmağa), and with this Unuqay's strength (gücü) grows.

claims.quote: Bir qədər yol getdikdən sonra isə canına istilənmə gələn keçinin ayaqları uzanır və atın üstündə adam kimi oturub atlını sıxır.

statement.id: Setelah beberapa lama di jalan, kaki kambing yang menghangat itu memanjang, lalu ia duduk di atas kuda seperti manusia (adam kimi) dan menjepit penunggangnya.
statement.en: After some way on the road, the warmed-up goat's legs lengthen, and it sits on the horse like a person (adam kimi) and squeezes the rider.

claims.quote: Halın qadın dönərgəsi kimi iynədən, sancaqdan qorxur. Buna görə də Unuqayı tutmaq üçün iynə və sancaq taxıb işlətmək olar.

statement.id: Seperti wujud perempuan Hal, ia takut jarum dan peniti (iynədən, sancaqdan); karena itu jarum dan peniti dapat dipakai untuk menangkap Unuqay.
statement.en: Like Hal's female form, it fears needles and pins (iynədən, sancaqdan); therefore needles and pins can be used to catch Unuqay.

claims.quote: Unuqayda iynənin sancılacağı zəif yerlər boyun və bel damarıdır.

statement.id: Titik lemah Unuqay tempat jarum ditusukkan adalah leher dan urat pinggang (boyun və bel damarı).
statement.en: Unuqay's weak spots where the needle is to be stuck are the neck and the vein of the lower back (boyun və bel damarı).

claims.quote: Nadir mətnlərdə Unuqay cinlərlə bağlı hekayələrdə olduğu kimi adamları aldadıb onları qəbiristanlığın içinə aparır və ya hamilə qadın yatarkən onun üstünə çıxıb uşağı tələf edir.

statement.id: Dalam teks yang jarang, seperti kisah tentang jin (cinlərlə), Unuqay memperdaya orang dan membawanya ke dalam kuburan, atau naik ke atas perempuan hamil yang tidur dan membinasakan bayinya.
statement.en: In rare texts, as in stories about jinn (cinlərlə), Unuqay lures people into the cemetery, or climbs on a sleeping pregnant woman and destroys the child.

claims.quote: Şəkinin Göynük kəndlərində (Aşağı Göynük və Baş Göynük) Unuqay mifoloji qəhrəmanına tez-tez rast gəlinir. Burada Unuqayla bağlı 16 mətn qeydə alınmışdır.

statement.id: Tokoh mitologis Unuqay sering dijumpai di desa-desa Göynük di Şəki (Aşağı Göynük dan Baş Göynük); di sana tercatat 16 teks tentang Unuqay.
statement.en: The mythological figure Unuqay is often met in the Göynük villages of Şəki (Aşağı Göynük and Baş Göynük); 16 texts about Unuqay were recorded there.

claims.quote: Unuqayda görülən ətraf üzvlərin uzanması xüsusiyyəti Naxçıvanın Sədərək rayonunda qeydə alınmış Çıntırqayış (Kəndirqayış) bədheybətində də vardır.

statement.id: Ciri anggota badan yang memanjang pada Unuqay juga ada pada makhluk Çıntırqayış (Kəndirqayış) yang tercatat di distrik Sədərək, Naxçıvan.
statement.en: The lengthening limbs seen in Unuqay also occur in the monster Çıntırqayış (Kəndirqayış), recorded in the Sədərək district of Naxçıvan.

claims.quote: Erkək keçi, oğlaq formasındadır. Keçinin rəngi mifoloji mətnlərin çoxunda ağ, yalnız bircə mətndə qaradır.

statement.id: Wujud hewannya kambing jantan atau anak kambing (oğlaq); dalam sebagian besar teks warnanya putih (ağ), hanya dalam satu teks hitam (qara).
statement.en: Its animal form is a billy goat or kid (oğlaq); in most texts it is white (ağ), and in only one text black (qara).

claims.quote: Nənəqay. Adı keçən mətn olmasa da, Unuqayın variantı hesab edilir.

statement.id: Nənəqay dianggap varian Unuqay, meskipun tidak ada teks yang menyebut namanya.
statement.en: Nənəqay is considered a variant of Unuqay, although no text mentions it by name.

claims.quote: Şəki mətnlərində keçi dönərgəsinə verilən əsas ad Unuqaydır. Digər istifadə olunan ad olan Maşşax göynüklülər tərəfindən gözlərinin rəngi göy olan insanlara da deyilir.

statement.id: Dalam teks Şəki nama utama wujud kambing itu Unuqay; nama lain, Maşşax, juga dipakai orang Göynük untuk orang bermata biru (göy).
statement.en: In the Şəki texts the main name of the goat form is Unuqay; another name, Maşşax, is also used by Göynük people for blue-eyed (göy) persons.

claims.quote: Bu bölgədən Azərbaycan folkloru üçün naməlum olan xeyli mifoloji personaj və mətn qeydə almışıq ki, onların analoji variantları ilə biz digər türk xalqlarının folklorunda qarşılaşırıq. Halın keçi dönərgəsi Unuqay

statement.id: Penyusun mencatat dari daerah ini banyak tokoh mitologis yang belum dikenal dalam folklor Azerbaijan (Azərbaycan), dengan padanan dalam folklor bangsa türk lain; salah satunya Unuqay, wujud kambing Hal (Halın keçi dönərgəsi).
statement.en: The compiler recorded from this area many mythological characters unknown to Azerbaijan (Azərbaycan) folklore, with analogues in the folklore of other türk peoples; one is Unuqay, the goat form of Hal (Halın keçi dönərgəsi).

claims.quote: Huna Maşşax diyilər, Unuqay diyilər, Kafdar diyilər. Əsas Unuqay diyilər.

statement.id: Seorang penutur berkata makhluk itu disebut Maşşax, Unuqay, dan Kafdar, tetapi yang utama Unuqay (Əsas Unuqay).
statement.en: A narrator said it is called Maşşax, Unuqay and Kafdar, but mainly Unuqay (Əsas Unuqay).

claims.quote: Xortdeydi, Unuqaydı, iyneynən lapatqadan qorxuylər. Ona görə ki, iyneynən kəfən tikiliy, lapatqeynən qavır qazılıy.

statement.id: Menurut penutur, xortdan dan Unuqay takut jarum dan sekop (iyneynən lapatqadan), karena dengan jarum kain kafan (kəfən) dijahit dan dengan sekop kubur (qavır) digali.
statement.en: According to the narrator, the xortdan and Unuqay fear the needle and the shovel (iyneynən lapatqadan), because the shroud (kəfən) is sewn with a needle and the grave (qavır) is dug with a shovel.

claims.quote: gördux ki, Unuqay oturufdu atın üsdünə, yapışıfdı. Boynünə, bel damarına iynə sanciylər.

statement.id: Dalam satu kisah, Unuqay didapati menempel di atas kuda (atın üsdünə), lalu orang menusukkan jarum (iynə) ke leher dan urat pinggangnya (bel damarına).
statement.en: In one account Unuqay was found stuck on top of the horse (atın üsdünə), and people stuck a needle (iynə) into its neck and lower-back vein (bel damarına).

claims.quote: İşıxdan qorxuy də. İynədən, işıxdan qorxuy.

statement.id: Seorang penutur menyebut Unuqay takut cahaya dan jarum (İynədən, işıxdan qorxuy).
statement.en: A narrator says Unuqay fears light and needles (İynədən, işıxdan qorxuy).

claims.quote: Unnan sora dili pəltehləşdi ho kişinin. Sora da başdiyi axsax gəzmağa.

statement.id: Setelah kejadian itu, lidah lelaki itu menjadi pelat (dili pəltehləşdi) dan ia mulai berjalan pincang (axsax).
statement.en: After that the man's speech became slurred (dili pəltehləşdi) and he began to walk with a limp (axsax).

short_description.id: Vision Serpent adalah ular raksasa dalam mitologi Maya pra-Kolumbus yang muncul dalam penglihatan saat ritual pengeluaran darah, sebagai gerbang ke alam roh tempat leluhur dan dewa menampakkan diri.
short_description.en: The Vision Serpent is a giant serpent of pre-Columbian Maya mythology that appeared in visions during bloodletting rituals, serving as a gateway to the spirit realm through which ancestors and gods manifested themselves.

long_description.id: Vision Serpent adalah makhluk penting dalam mitologi Maya pra-Kolumbus, meski istilahnya kini mulai usang. Ia dianggap ular paling penting di antara ular-ular Maya. Menurut mitologi Maya, ular pada umumnya adalah kendaraan matahari dan bintang melintasi langit, dan pergantian kulitnya menjadikannya lambang kelahiran kembali dan pembaruan. Ia biasanya digambarkan berjenggot dan berhidung bulat, sering berkepala dua atau dengan roh dewa atau leluhur yang muncul dari rahangnya.
long_description.en: The Vision Serpent is an important creature of pre-Columbian Maya mythology, although the term is now becoming outdated. It is regarded as the foremost of the Maya serpents. Maya mythology treats serpents in general as the carriers of the sun and stars across the sky, and their shedding of skin made them symbols of rebirth and renewal. It was usually bearded with a rounded snout, and was frequently shown double-headed, or with a god's or ancestor's spirit coming out of its mouth.

long_description.id: Dalam ritual pengeluaran darah Maya, peserta mengalami penglihatan tempat mereka berkomunikasi dengan leluhur atau dewa, dan penglihatan itu berwujud ular raksasa yang menjadi gerbang ke alam roh. Kertas upacara berlumur darah dibakar sehingga asapnya menjadi medium bagi Vision Serpent untuk muncul. Bagi orang Maya, ia menjadi penghubung langsung antara alam roh para dewa dan dunia fisik. Pengeluaran darah juga, meski lebih jarang, dilakukan untuk berkomunikasi dengan leluhur.
long_description.en: In Maya bloodletting rituals, participants experienced visions in which they communicated with ancestors or gods, and the visions took the form of a giant serpent serving as a gateway to the spirit realm. Blood-soaked ceremonial papers were burned so that the smoke became a medium for the Vision Serpent to appear. To the Maya it joined the gods' spirit world directly with the physical one. Bloodletting was also, less often, carried out to communicate with ancestors.

long_description.id: Vision Serpent berakar pada konsepsi Maya yang lebih awal dan berada di pusat dunia sebagaimana mereka bayangkan. Ada pula Vision Serpent bernama Och-Kan, penguasa Kalak'mul. Sebuah relief dari Kuil 23 di Yaxchilan menampilkan ular raksasa berkepala dua dengan seorang prajurit dan dewa Tlaloc yang muncul dari mulutnya di atas seorang pemuja yang berlutut. Catatan sekitar tahun 1930 menyebut orang Maya Q'eqchi' masih melakukan ritual yang sangat mirip pencarian penglihatan Maya klasik.
long_description.en: It reaches back to older Maya ideas and sits at the centre of the world as they pictured it. There was also a Vision Serpent named Och-Kan, lord of Kalak'mul. A relief from Temple 23 at Yaxchilan shows a giant double-headed serpent with a warrior and the god Tlaloc emerging from its mouths over a kneeling worshipper. A note from around 1930 reports that the Q'eqchi' Maya kept up a ritual closely resembling the classic Maya vision quest.

short_description.id: Elang Kaukasus adalah elang raksasa, dalam satu versi anak Tifon dan Ekhidna, yang diutus Zeus memakan hati Prometheus setiap hari hingga dibunuh Herakles.
short_description.en: The Caucasian Eagle is a gigantic eagle, in one version child of Typhon and Echidna, sent by Zeus to eat Prometheus's liver every day until Herakles killed it.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Yunani, Elang Kaukasus adalah elang, anak Tifon dan Ekhidna. Setelah Zeus merantai Prometheus di tebing pegunungan Kaukasus, setiap hari seekor elang datang memakan hatinya. Elang itu digambarkan sebagai elang raksasa yang diutus Zeus sebagai hukuman karena Prometheus mencuri api dari para dewa.
long_description.en: In Greek mythology the Caucasian Eagle is an eagle, child of Typhon and Echidna. After Zeus chained Prometheus to a cliff in the Caucasus, an eagle came every day to eat his liver. It is described as a gigantic eagle sent by Zeus as punishment for Prometheus stealing fire from the gods.

long_description.id: Menurut satu sumber, elang itu juga digambarkan sebagai automaton perunggu buatan Hephaistos. Dalam Theogony karya Hesiodos, hati Prometheus tumbuh kembali setiap malam sebanyak yang dimakan burung itu sepanjang hari. Dalam Prometheus Bound karya Aeschylus, elang itu disebut anjing bersayap Zeus yang mencabik tubuh Prometheus dan berpesta atas hatinya sepanjang hari, sedangkan dalam Argonautica karya Apollonius Rhodius bentuknya bukan bentuk burung biasa, dengan bulu sayap panjang yang naik turun seperti deretan dayung.
long_description.en: According to one source the eagle is also described as a bronze automaton built by Hephaistos. In Hesiod's Theogony Prometheus' liver grew as much again each night as the bird devoured in the day. In Aeschylus' Prometheus Bound the eagle is the winged hound of Zeus that tears Prometheus' body and feasts upon his liver all day long, while in Apollonius Rhodius' Argonautica its form is not that of an ordinary bird, its long quill-feathers rising and falling like a bank of oars.

long_description.id: Herakles menjatuhkan elang itu dengan hujan anak panah ketika ia datang membebaskan Prometheus.
long_description.en: Herakles felled the eagle with a volley of arrows when he came to free Prometheus.

description.id: Elang itu memakan hati Prometheus yang memulihkan diri; dalam Hesiodos hati itu tumbuh kembali setiap malam sebanyak yang dimakan sepanjang hari.

sources.author: Aaron J. Atsma

claims.quote: Dalam mitologi Yunani, Elang Kaukasus adalah seekor burung elang yang merupakan anak dari Tifon dan Ekhidna.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Yunani, Elang Kaukasus adalah elang anak Tifon dan Ekhidna.
statement.en: In Greek mythology, the Caucasian Eagle is an eagle, child of Typhon and Echidna.

claims.quote: Zeus merantai Prometheus di sebuah tebing di pegunungan Kaukasus dan setiap hari akan datang seekor elang yang memakan hati Prometheus.

statement.id: Zeus merantai Prometheus di tebing pegunungan Kaukasus, dan setiap hari seekor elang datang memakan hatinya.
statement.en: Zeus chained Prometheus to a Caucasus cliff, and every day an eagle came to eat his liver.

claims.quote: THE AETOS KAUKASIOS (Caucasian Eagle) was a gigantic eagle sent by Zeus to feed upon the ever-regenerating liver of the Titan Prometheus after he was chained to a peak of the Kaukasos (Caucasus) Mountains as punishment for stealing fire from the gods.

statement.id: Aetos Kaukasios (Elang Kaukasus) adalah elang raksasa yang diutus Zeus untuk memakan hati Titan Prometheus yang terus memulihkan diri setelah ia dirantai di puncak pegunungan Kaukasos (Kaukasus) sebagai hukuman karena mencuri api dari para dewa.
statement.en: The Aetos Kaukasios (Caucasian Eagle) was a gigantic eagle sent by Zeus to feed upon the ever-regenerating liver of the Titan Prometheus after he was chained to a peak of the Kaukasos (Caucasus) Mountains as punishment for stealing fire from the gods.

claims.quote: The eagle was variously described as a bronze automaton constructed by the god Hephaistos (Hephaestus), or as a fell creature spawned by the drakaina Ekhidna (Echidna).

statement.id: Elang itu digambarkan beragam: sebagai automaton perunggu buatan dewa Hephaistos (Hephaestus), atau sebagai makhluk ganas yang dilahirkan drakaina Ekhidna (Echidna).
statement.en: The eagle was variously described as a bronze automaton constructed by the god Hephaistos (Hephaestus), or as a fell creature spawned by the drakaina Ekhidna (Echidna).

claims.quote: When Herakles set out to free Prometheus from his bonds, he felled the eagle with a volley of arrows.

statement.id: Ketika Herakles berangkat membebaskan Prometheus dari belenggunya, ia menjatuhkan elang itu dengan hujan anak panah.
statement.en: When Herakles set out to free Prometheus from his bonds, he felled the eagle with a volley of arrows.

claims.quote: Hesiod, Theogony 507 ff (trans. Evelyn-White) ... Ready-witted Prometheus he [Zeus] bound with inextricable bonds, cruel chains ... set on him a long-winged eagle, which used to eat his immortal liver; but by night the liver grew as much again everyway as the long-winged bird devoured in the whole day. That bird Herakles (Heracles), the valiant son of shapely-ankled Alkmene (Alcmena), slew

statement.id: Dalam Theogony karya Hesiodos (terjemahan Evelyn-White), seekor elang bersayap panjang yang biasa memakan hati abadi Prometheus ditempatkan padanya, tetapi pada malam hari hati itu tumbuh sebanyak yang dimakan burung itu sepanjang hari; burung itu dibunuh Herakles (Heracles), putra gagah Alkmene (Alcmena).
statement.en: In Hesiod's Theogony (trans. Evelyn-White), a long-winged eagle was set on Prometheus to eat his immortal liver, but by night the liver grew as much again as the bird devoured in the whole day; Herakles (Heracles), the valiant son of Alkmene (Alcmena), slew that bird.

claims.quote: Apollonius Rhodius, Argonautica 2. 1238 ff (trans. Rieu) ... They saw it in the afternoon flying high above the ship with a strident whirr. It was near the clouds, yet it made all their canvas quiver to its wings as it beat by. For its form was not that of an ordinary bird : the long quill-feathers of each wing rose and fell like a bank of polished oars.

statement.id: Dalam Argonautica karya Apollonius Rhodius (terjemahan Rieu), mereka melihat elang itu pada sore hari terbang tinggi di atas kapal dengan desing nyaring; ia dekat awan, tetapi sayapnya membuat seluruh layar mereka bergetar saat ia melintas. Bentuknya bukan bentuk burung biasa: bulu-bulu sayap panjangnya naik turun seperti deretan dayung yang digosok.
statement.en: In Apollonius Rhodius' Argonautica (trans. Rieu), they saw it in the afternoon flying high above the ship with a strident whirr; it was near the clouds, yet its wings made all their canvas quiver as it beat by. Its form was not that of an ordinary bird: the long quill-feathers of each wing rose and fell like a bank of polished oars.

claims.quote: Aeschylus, Prometheus Bound 1021 ff ... The winged hound of Zeus, the ravening eagle, coming an unbidden banqueter the whole day long, with savage appetite shall tear your body piecemeal into great rents and feast his fill upon your liver until it is black with gnawing.

statement.id: Dalam Prometheus Bound karya Aeschylus, anjing bersayap Zeus, elang yang rakus, datang sebagai tamu tak diundang sepanjang hari, dengan nafsu buas akan mencabik tubuhmu sepotong-sepotong dan berpesta atas hatimu sampai menghitam karena dikoyak.
statement.en: In Aeschylus' Prometheus Bound, the winged hound of Zeus, the ravening eagle, comes an unbidden banqueter the whole day long and with savage appetite shall tear the body piecemeal into great rents and feast his fill upon the liver until it is black with gnawing.

short_description.id: Átahsaia adalah iblis raksasa pemakan manusia dalam agama dan mitos suku Zuni di wilayah barat daya (Southwestern United States). Dalam kisah Zuni ia dibunuh oleh dua dewa perang kembar.
short_description.en: Átahsaia is a man-eating giant demon of Zuni religion and myth in the Southwestern United States. In Zuni tales he is slain by the twin war gods.

long_description.id: Átahsaia (juga ditulis A'tahsaia atau Atasaya) adalah iblis raksasa pemakan manusia dalam agama dan mitos suku Zuni di wilayah barat daya (Southwestern United States). Ia iblis, tetapi digambarkan berwujud fisik: raksasa yang beberapa kali lebih besar daripada manusia biasa, hingga pernah tak muat memasukkan bahunya ke gua yang mudah dimasuki manusia. Ia kanibal yang juga lapar akan daging manusia dan pembohong kawakan.
long_description.en: Átahsaia (also spelled A'tahsaia or Atasaya) is a man-eating giant demon of the religion and myths of the Zuni people in the Southwestern United States. He is a demon but is depicted with a physical form: a giant several times larger than an ordinary human, once so huge he could not fit his shoulders into a cave a normal person enters easily. He is a cannibal who also hungers for human flesh, and an inveterate liar.

long_description.id: Dalam penuturan Cushing, ia tinggal di sebuah gua yang hingga kini disebut Gua Átahsaia; tubuhnya sebesar rusa elk terbesar, dadanya berbulu kaku seperti duri landak, dan ia sopan tetapi pembohong besar. Ia membujuk dua gadis dengan menyebut dirinya kakek mereka, dan dalam kisah itu dikatakan ia menggorok leher tawanannya, sementara si kembar Áhaiyúta dan Mátsailéma, anak Bapa Matahari dan Ibu Air Dunia, mengintai. Dalam kisah itu Áhaiyúta menembaknya dengan anak panah, dan kepalanya dilempar menjadi bintang pembohong.
long_description.en: In Cushing's telling he lives in a cave still called the Cave of Átahsaia; his body is as big as the biggest elk's, his breast shaggy with hair stiff as porcupine quills, and he is polite yet a great liar. He lures two maidens by calling himself their grandfather and, in the tale, is said to cut the throats of his captives, while the twins Áhaiyúta and Mátsailéma, offspring of the Sun-father and the Mother Waters of the World, watch. In the tale Áhaiyúta shoots him with an arrow, and his head is cast into the sky as a lying star.

long_description.id: Menurut antropolog Elsie Clews Parsons, Átahsaia muncul dalam tarian spiritual Zuni untuk mengajarkan anak-anak tentang kepatuhan; a'doshlě ("dewa kakek") dan suukě ("dewa nenek") adalah representasinya.
long_description.en: Anthropologist Elsie Clews Parsons records Átahsaia in a Zuni spiritual dance that teaches children to obey; the a'doshlě ("grandfather god") and suukě ("grandmother god") are representations of him.

cultural_context.id: Menurut Elsie Clews Parsons, Átahsaia muncul dalam tarian spiritual Zuni yang dimaksudkan mengajarkan anak tentang kepatuhan; a'doshlě dan suukě adalah representasinya.
cultural_context.en: According to Elsie Clews Parsons, Átahsaia figures in a Zuni spiritual dance meant to teach children obedience; the a'doshlě and suukě are representations of him.

short_description.id: Chiwen adalah motif hiasan atap dalam arsitektur Tiongkok dan juga nama naga bercampur ciri ikan, salah satu dari sembilan anak naga.
short_description.en: Chiwen is a roof ornamental motif in Chinese architecture and also the name of a dragon that mixes fish features, one of the nine sons of the dragon.

long_description.id: Chiwen adalah motif hiasan atap dalam arsitektur dan seni tradisional Tiongkok. Nama yang sama dipakai untuk naga Tiongkok yang memadukan ciri-ciri ikan, dan dalam mitologi Tiongkok ia termasuk sembilan anak naga yang sama-sama dipakai sebagai hiasan atap istana. Chiwen disebut menempati urutan kedua atau ketiga dalam daftar itu, dan setiap naga dalam daftar itu berfungsi melindungi.
long_description.en: Chiwen is a roof ornamental motif in traditional Chinese architecture and art. The same name is used for a Chinese dragon that mixes fish features, and in Chinese mythology it is counted with the nine sons of the dragon, whose forms also serve to decorate imperial roofs. The chiwen is listed second or third in that list, and each dragon in the list has a protective function.

long_description.id: Namanya menggabungkan unsur naga tanpa tanduk dan mulut hewan, dan ejaan alternatif menghubungkannya dengan mulut burung hantu. Chiwen digambarkan sebagai naga tanpa tanduk mirip ikan dengan tubuh sangat pendek dan mulut lebar di sepanjang bubungan atap. Menurut Wuzazu dari zaman Ming, chiwen suka menelan dan diletakkan di kedua ujung bubungan untuk menelan semua pengaruh jahat.
long_description.en: Its name combines elements denoting a hornless dragon and an animal's mouth, and an alternative spelling associates it with an owl's mouth. The chiwen is described as a fish-like hornless dragon with a very truncated body and a wide mouth along roof ridges. According to the Ming Dynasty Wuzazu, chiwen like swallowing and are placed on both ends of the ridgepoles to swallow all evil influences.

long_description.id: Kehadirannya di atap dikatakan menjaga dari kebakaran, dan menurut teori fengshui juga dari banjir dan topan. Sebuah buku dari Dinasti Tang menyebut makhluk laut mitos bernama chiwen dipasang pada atap bangunan pada zaman Han untuk melindungi bangunan dari kebakaran. Label museum menyatakan bahwa naga dahulu dipercaya menguasai badai dan air, serta menjaga bangunan dari petir dan bencana alam lain.
long_description.en: Its presence on roofs is said to guard against fires, and in Fengshui theory also against floods and typhoons. A book from the Tang dynasty says a mythical sea creature called the chiwen was put on roofs during the Han dynasty to protect buildings from fire. A museum label states that dragons were believed to command storms and water, and to shield buildings from lightning and other natural disasters.

long_description.id: Pendahulu hiasan chiwei muncul pada model arsitektur keramik zaman Han. Pada pertengahan Dinasti Tang chiwen yang mirip ikan menjadi motif yang menonjol di samping chiwei, dan pada Dinasti Song chiwen sepenuhnya menggantikannya. Sebuah ubin bubungan di museum menampilkan naga besar yang menggigit bubungan atap dengan rahang terbuka lebar, tampak seperti menelan bubungan itu.
long_description.en: The earlier chiwei ornament appears on Han-era ceramic architectural models. In the mid-Tang dynasty the fish-like chiwen became a prevailing motif alongside the chiwei, and in the Song dynasty chiwen fully replaced it. A roof-ridge tile in a museum shows a large dragon biting the roof ridge with wide-open jaws, appearing to swallow the ridge.

claims.quote: Chiwen (Chinese: 蚩吻; pinyin: chīwěn; Wade–Giles: ch'ih-wen; lit. 'hornless-dragon mouth') is a roof ornamental motif in traditional Chinese architecture and art.

statement.id: Chiwen adalah motif hiasan atap dalam arsitektur dan seni tradisional Tiongkok.
statement.en: Chiwen is a roof ornamental motif in traditional Chinese architecture and art.

claims.quote: Chiwen is also the name of a Chinese dragon that mixes features of a fish, and in Chinese mythology is one of the nine sons of the dragon, which are also used as imperial roof decorations.

statement.id: Chiwen juga nama seekor naga Tiongkok yang memadukan ciri-ciri ikan, dan dalam mitologi Tiongkok merupakan salah satu dari sembilan anak naga yang juga dipakai sebagai hiasan atap kekaisaran.
statement.en: Chiwen is also the name of a Chinese dragon that mixes features of a fish, and in Chinese mythology is one of the nine sons of the dragon, which are also used as imperial roof decorations.

claims.quote: The name for this dragon is chīwěn (蚩吻), which  compounds chī (蚩; 'hornless dragon', 'young dragon') and wěn (吻; 'animal's mouth'). Chīshǒu (螭首) and Chītóu (螭頭),  both literally meaning "hornless-dragon head".

statement.id: Namanya menggabungkan unsur naga tanpa tanduk dan mulut hewan.
statement.en: Its name combines elements denoting a hornless dragon and an animal's mouth.

claims.quote: Chiwen is alternatively written 鴟吻; 'owl mouth', using the homophonous character chī (鴟; 'owl', 'bird of prey'). The chīwěi (鴟尾; 'owl tail') and chīméng (鴟甍; 'owl roof-ridge') are additional birdlike roof decorations.

statement.id: Ejaan alternatif menghubungkan chiwen dengan mulut burung hantu.
statement.en: An alternative spelling associates chiwen with an owl's mouth.

claims.quote: The origin of the roof decoration of chiwen can be traced to the roof decoration alternatively named as chiwei (鸱尾), the earliest visual examples found in the Han dynasty on many ceramic architectural models, que-towers, and tomb murals and stone-reliefs.

statement.id: Pendahulu hiasan chiwei ditemukan pada model arsitektur keramik zaman Han.
statement.en: The earlier chiwei ornament appears on Han-era ceramic architectural models.

claims.quote: According to the Ming Dynasty Wuzazu ( 五雜俎) "The ch'i-wen, which like swallowing, are placed on both ends of the ridgepoles of roofs (to swallow all evil influences)."

statement.id: Menurut Wuzazu dari zaman Ming, chiwen yang suka menelan diletakkan di kedua ujung bubungan atap (untuk menelan semua pengaruh jahat).
statement.en: According to the Ming Dynasty Wuzazu, the ch'i-wen, which like swallowing, are placed on both ends of the ridgepoles of roofs (to swallow all evil influences).

claims.quote: This is the fish-like, hornless dragon with a very truncated body and large, wide mouth usually found along roof ridges (as if swallowing the roof beams). His presence on roofs is also said to guard against fires.

statement.id: Chiwen adalah naga tanpa tanduk mirip ikan dengan tubuh sangat pendek dan mulut lebar yang biasanya ada di sepanjang bubungan atap; kehadirannya di atap juga dikatakan menjaga dari kebakaran.
statement.en: The chiwen is the fish-like, hornless dragon with a very truncated body and large wide mouth usually found along roof ridges; its presence on roofs is also said to guard against fires.

claims.quote: A paragraph in the Tang dynasty book Su Shi Yan Yi ( 蘇氏演義) by Su E ( 蘇鶚) says that a mythical sea creature called the chi wen [sic] was put on the roofs of buildings during the Han dynasty to protect the structures from fire hazards.

statement.id: Sebuah paragraf dalam buku Su Shi Yan Yi karya Su E dari zaman Tang menyebut makhluk laut mitos yang dipasang pada atap bangunan pada zaman Han untuk melindungi bangunan dari bahaya kebakaran.
statement.en: A paragraph in the Tang dynasty book Su Shi Yan Yi by Su E says a mythical sea creature called the chi wen was put on the roofs of buildings during the Han dynasty to protect the structures from fire hazards.

claims.quote: In Fengshui theory, a chiwen or chiwei supposedly protects against not only fires, but also floods and typhoons.

statement.id: Dalam teori fengshui, chiwen atau chiwei dipercaya melindungi bukan hanya dari kebakaran, tetapi juga dari banjir dan topan.
statement.en: In Fengshui theory, a chiwen or chiwei supposedly protects not only against fires but also against floods and typhoons.

claims.quote: The chiwen is listed second or third among the Lóng shēng jiǔzǐ ( 龍生九子; 'dragon gives birth to nine young'), "Nine Dragons" ( 九龍; jiǔlóng), which are traditional mythological creatures that have become traditional Chinese feng shui architectural decorations. Each one of the nine dragons has a protective function.

statement.id: Chiwen terdaftar di urutan kedua atau ketiga di antara Long sheng jiuzi ("naga melahirkan sembilan anak"), makhluk mitos tradisional yang menjadi hiasan arsitektur fengshui Tiongkok; masing-masing dari sembilan naga itu berfungsi melindungi.
statement.en: The chiwen is listed second or third among the Long sheng jiuzi ("dragon gives birth to nine young"), traditional mythological creatures that have become feng shui architectural decorations; each of the nine dragons has a protective function.

claims.quote: Over the course of the mid-Tang dynasty, the fish-like chiwen became another prevailing ornamental motif alongside the chiwei. In the Song dynasty, chiwen fully replaced the chiwei and adopted a more dragon-like appearance while also retaining some of their predecessor's bird-like features such as wings or bird's head.

statement.id: Pada pertengahan Dinasti Tang, chiwen yang mirip ikan menjadi motif hias yang menonjol di samping chiwei; pada Dinasti Song chiwen sepenuhnya menggantikan chiwei dan berpenampilan lebih mirip naga sambil mempertahankan sebagian ciri burung seperti sayap atau kepala burung.
statement.en: Over the course of the mid-Tang dynasty the fish-like chiwen became another prevailing ornamental motif alongside the chiwei; in the Song dynasty chiwen fully replaced the chiwei and adopted a more dragon-like appearance while retaining some bird-like features such as wings or a bird's head.

claims.quote: Dragons controlled storms and water and were thought to protect buildings from lightning and other natural calamities.

statement.id: Label galeri museum menyatakan bahwa naga mengendalikan badai dan air serta dianggap melindungi bangunan dari petir dan bencana alam lainnya.
statement.en: The museum's gallery label states that dragons controlled storms and water and were thought to protect buildings from lightning and other natural calamities.

claims.quote: This tile originally decorated one end of the roof ridge of a temple. Facing inwards, the large dragon appears to be swallowing the roof ridge.

statement.id: Menurut label museum, ubin ini semula menghiasi salah satu ujung bubungan atap sebuah kuil, dan naga besar yang menghadap ke dalam tampak seperti menelan bubungan atap.
statement.en: According to the museum label, this tile originally decorated one end of the roof ridge of a temple, and the large dragon, facing inwards, appears to be swallowing the roof ridge.

claims.quote: The larger dragon is biting the roof ridge with wide-open jaws and its winding tail turns upward.

short_description.id: Dragon King adalah dewa air dan cuaca yang dikenal dalam tradisi Asia, termasuk agama rakyat Tiongkok.
short_description.en: The Dragon King is a water and weather deity in Asian traditions, including Chinese folk religion.

long_description.id: Dragon King adalah dewa air dan cuaca yang dikenal dalam tradisi Asia, termasuk agama rakyat Tiongkok. Ia dipercaya mengatur hujan serta menguasai laut, sungai, dan badan air lainnya.
long_description.en: The Dragon King is a water and weather deity in Asian traditions, including Chinese folk religion. Belief attributes rainfall and dominion over seas, rivers, and other waters to him.

long_description.id: Kisah menggambarkan istana bawah air dan sistem istana kerajaan miliknya. Tradisi juga mengenal Raja Naga Empat Laut. Dewa naga dapat berperan sebagai pelindung wilayah. Desa pertanian dahulu mengadakan upacara di kuil raja naga untuk meminta hujan.
long_description.en: Accounts describe his underwater palace and royal court system. The tradition also recognizes the Dragon Kings of the Four Seas. The dragon deity may also serve as a territorial protector. Farming villages formerly held rites at dragon-king shrines to seek rain.

long_description.id: Menurut Werner, para Raja Naga Laut tinggal di istana megah di dasar laut dan memakan mutiara dan opal. Mereka berjumlah lima: satu yang utama di tengah, empat lainnya di utara, barat, selatan, dan timur. Mereka disebut abadi dan saling mengetahui pikiran tanpa berbicara. Seperti dewa lain, mereka naik setahun sekali ke Surga untuk melapor kepada Penguasa Tertinggi pada bulan ketiga. Di dunia roh, Departemen Air Asin dalam Kementerian Perairan dipimpin empat Raja Naga dari empat penjuru.
long_description.en: According to Werner, the Sea-dragon Kings live in splendid palaces in the depths of the sea and feed on pearls and opals. There are five of them: the chief in the centre and four others in the north, west, south, and east. They are described as immortal and as knowing each other's thoughts without speaking. Like other gods, they go up once a year to the Heavens to report to the Supreme Ruler, in the third month. In the spirit-world, the Department of Salt Waters in the Ministry of Waters is presided over by four Dragon-kings of the four directions.

claims.quote: The Dragon King, also known as the Dragon God, is a celestial creature, water and weather god in Asian mythology. They can be found in various cultural and religious symbolic materials all around Asia, specifically in South, Southeast Asia and distinctly in East Asian cultures (Chinese folk-religion).

claims.quote: He can manipulate and control the weather, move seasons and bring rainfall with his divine power at his own will, thus, he is regarded as the dispenser of rain, divine ruler of the Seas, rivers and water bodies,  commanding over all bodies of water. short_description.id: Katak puru raksasa adalah makhluk gaib dalam kumpulan cerita Jepang zaman Edo.
short_description.en: The giant toad is a supernatural creature in Edo-period Japanese tale collections.

long_description.id: Katak puru raksasa (Ōgama) adalah makhluk gaib dalam kumpulan cerita Jepang zaman Edo. Cerita Ehon Hyaku Monogatari menempatkannya di pegunungan Suō, dan menyebut panjangnya sekitar 2,4 meter. Ia konon menarik burung dan serangga ke mulutnya melalui embusan seperti pelangi dan memakan ular pada musim panas.
long_description.en: The giant toad (Ōgama) is a supernatural creature in Edo-period Japanese tale collections. An Ehon Hyaku Monogatari tale places it in the mountains of Suō and gives it a length of roughly 2.4 metres. It is said to draw birds and insects into its mouth through a rainbow-like breath and to eat snakes in summer.

long_description.id: Kisah lain, dari kumpulan Hokuetsu Kidan, menuturkan bahwa benda yang dikira batu tempat seorang bernama Fujita duduk membuka mata merah seperti api dan menguap, lalu lenyap; diduga itu katak puru raksasa. Katak puru raksasa juga muncul dalam lakon kabuki tahun 1804 dan dalam gambar yang menunjukkan Jiraiya menungganginya atau katak itu muncul di belakang Takiyasha-hime.
long_description.en: Another tale, from the Hokuetsu Kidan collection, relates that the thing taken for a rock on which a man named Fujita sat opened fire-red eyes and yawned, then vanished; it was surmised to be a giant toad. Giant toads also appear in an 1804 kabuki play and in pictures showing Jiraiya riding one or one appearing behind Takiyasha-hime.

long_description.id: Pada sekitar Meiji 33, surat kabar Osaka memberitakan katak puru raksasa Gunung Shinoda dan sebuah tiruan katak ditampilkan di kuil. Tradisinya ditafsirkan berasal dari hewan liar pegunungan yang bisa sangat besar, serta dari anggapan bahwa katak menyedot serangga dan jiwa manusia.
long_description.en: Around Meiji 33, an Osaka newspaper reported on the giant toad of Mount Shinoda and a model toad was shown at a shrine. The tradition is interpreted as stemming from the sometimes very large wild animals of the mountains and from the notion that toads suck in insects and human spirit.

cultural_context.id: Para pengkaji menafsirkan bahwa tradisi katak puru raksasa muncul dari hewan liar pegunungan yang kadang sangat besar, dan bahwa katak dipandang gaib karena tampak menyedot serangga ke mulutnya.
cultural_context.en: Interpretations hold that giant-toad traditions arose from the sometimes very large wild animals of the mountains, and that toads were seen as uncanny because they appear to suck insects into their mouths.

name.id: Embusan seperti pelangi yang menyedot mangsa
name.en: Rainbow-like breath that draws in prey

description.id: Dari mulutnya ia mengembuskan hawa seperti pelangi; burung dan serangga yang terkena hawa itu terisap ke mulutnya, dan pada musim panas ia memakan ular.
description.en: It breathes out a rainbow-like vapor from its mouth; birds and insects touched by it are drawn into its mouth, and in summer it eats snakes.

role.id: Katak puru raksasa yang tinggal di pegunungan Iwakuni.
role.en: A giant toad living deep in the mountains of Iwakuni.

summary.id: Menurut teks Ehon Hyaku Monogatari, ia tinggal jauh di pegunungan Gunung Iwakuni di Provinsi Suō dan panjangnya sekitar 2,4 meter. Gambar dalam buku itu menunjukkan katak ini memegang tombak, dan ada yang menyebut ia memakainya untuk menyerang orang.
summary.en: According to the Ehon Hyaku Monogatari text, it lives deep in the mountains of Iwakuni in Suō Province and is about 2.4 metres long. The illustration shows this toad holding a spear, and one view says it used the spear to attack people.

role.en: A giant toad mistaken for a rock.

summary.id: Benda yang dikira batu, tempat seorang bernama Fujita duduk, dikatakan telah membuka mata merah seperti api dan menguap; benda itu lalu lenyap tanpa bekas, dan diduga itu katak puru raksasa.
summary.en: The thing taken for a rock on which a man named Fujita sat is said to have opened fire-red eyes and yawned; it then vanished without a trace, and it was surmised to have been a giant toad.

description.id: Tempat katak puru raksasa dalam Ehon Hyaku Monogatari tinggal jauh di pegunungan; kini Iwakuni, Prefektur Yamaguchi.

description.id: Pada bulan ketujuh Kyōwa 4 (Agustus 1804), lakon karya Tsuruya Nanboku menampilkan katak puru raksasa dan disambut baik.

statement.en: The giant toad is a supernatural creature in Edo-period Japanese tale collections.

claims.quote: 『絵本百物語』本文によれば、周防国の岩国山（現・山口県岩国市）の山奥に住む大蝦蟇で、体長は約8尺（約2.4メートル）。

statement.id: Cerita Ehon Hyaku Monogatari menempatkannya di pegunungan Suō.

statement.id: Cerita tersebut memberinya panjang sekitar 2,4 meter.
statement.en: That tale gives it a length of roughly 2.4 metres.

claims.quote: 口から虹のような気を吐き、この気に触れた鳥や虫たちを口の中へと吸い込み、夏には蛇を食べるとある。

statement.id: Ia konon menarik burung dan serangga ke mulutnya melalui embusan seperti pelangi.
statement.en: It is said to draw birds and insects into its mouth through a rainbow-like breath.

claims.quote: 北陸地方の奇談集『北越奇談』などに見られる巨大なガマガエルの怪異。 妖山中に棲息する野生動物は通常の野外のものよりもずっと巨大なものもあることから、このような巨大なガマの伝承が生まれたと考えられている。

statement.id: Tradisi tentang katak puru sebesar itu dianggap muncul karena hewan liar yang hidup di pegunungan angker kadang jauh lebih besar daripada hewan di luar.
statement.en: Traditions of such giant toads are thought to have arisen because wild animals living in uncanny mountains can be much larger than those found in ordinary outdoor places.

claims.quote: ガマガエルが妖怪視されたことについては、カエルが長い舌で虫などを捕える様子が、あたかも虫がカエルの口の中に吸い込まれるようにも見えるため、こうしたカエルやガマが人間の精気を吸うなどの怪異のあるものと考えられたとの解釈もある。

statement.id: Ada tafsiran bahwa katak puru dipandang sebagai yōkai karena cara katak menangkap serangga dengan lidah panjang tampak seperti serangga terisap ke mulutnya, sehingga katak dan katak puru dianggap punya kekuatan gaib seperti menyedot jiwa manusia.
statement.en: There is an interpretation that toads were regarded as yōkai because the way a frog catches insects with its long tongue looks as if the insects are sucked into its mouth, so frogs and toads came to be thought to have uncanny powers such as sucking the spirit from people.

claims.quote:
「気づかなかったか? 貴行が先ほどまで乗っていたものが、火のように赤い目玉を開き、口をあけてあくびをしたのだ」と恐れながら答えた。
再び2人が元の場所へ戻ってみたところ、藤田の乗っていた岩とおぼしきものは跡形もなく消え失せていた。あれは岩ではなく大蝦蟇であり、突起と思ったものは蝦蟇のイボだったと推測されたという。

statement.id: Dalam satu kisah, benda yang dikira batu tempat seorang bernama Fujita duduk dikatakan membuka mata merah seperti api dan menguap, lalu lenyap tanpa bekas; diduga itu katak puru raksasa dan tonjolan yang dikira batu adalah kutil katak.
statement.en: In one tale, the thing taken for a rock on which a man named Fujita had been sitting was said to have opened fire-red eyes and yawned, then vanished without a trace; it was surmised to have been a giant toad and the bumps taken for rock to have been its warts.

claims.quote: 享和4年7月（1804年8月）には江戸河原崎座で鶴屋南北作、初代尾上松助主演『天竺徳兵衛韓噺』（天竺徳兵衛）にて大蝦蟇が登場し好評を博した。

statement.id: Pada bulan ketujuh Kyōwa 4 (Agustus 1804), sebuah katak puru raksasa muncul dalam lakon "Tenjiku Tokubei Ikoku-banashi" karya Tsuruya Nanboku yang dibintangi Onoe Matsusuke generasi pertama di Teater Kawarazaki, Edo, dan mendapat sambutan baik.
statement.en: In the seventh month of Kyōwa 4 (August 1804), a giant toad appeared in "Tenjiku Tokubei Ikoku-banashi" by Tsuruya Nanboku, starring the first Onoe Matsusuke, at the Kawarazaki Theater in Edo, and was well received.

claims.quote: 明治33年ころ、大阪毎日新聞が三面記事で「信田山の大蝦蟇」について連日報道した。その夏、瀬戸物町陶器神社に、うっそうとした渓谷に人間ほどの大きさの大蝦蟇が大目玉を光らせている、という作り物が登場し、観客が群がった。

statement.id: Sekitar Meiji 33, sebuah surat kabar Osaka memberitakan "katak puru raksasa Gunung Shinoda" setiap hari; pada musim panas itu, sebuah tiruan katak sebesar manusia dengan mata besar bersinar di lembah rimbun dipamerkan di kuil di Setomono-chō (陶器神社) dan ditonton banyak orang.
statement.en: Around Meiji 33, an Osaka newspaper reported daily on the "giant toad of Mount Shinoda"; that summer, a model of a human-sized toad with glaring big eyes in a thick gorge was shown at the shrine in Setomono-chō (陶器神社) and crowds gathered.

short_description.id: Hatsadiling adalah burung mitos yang umum muncul dalam seni Thailand utara, digambarkan sebesar rumah dengan kepala dan badan singa, belalai gajah, dan sayap burung, serta berkekuatan lima gajah.
short_description.en: Hatsadiling is a mythical bird commonly found in Northern Thai art, described as house-sized with a lion's head and body, an elephant's trunk and a bird's wings, and the strength of five elephants.

long_description.id: Hatsadiling adalah burung mitos yang umum muncul dalam seni Thailand utara. Rupanya dianggap sebesar rumah, dengan kepala dan badan singa, belalai dan gading gajah, jengger ayam, serta sayap burung. Dalam bahasa Thai ia juga disebut nok hatsading, nok hatsadi, dan nok hat.
long_description.en: Hatsadiling is a mythical bird commonly found in Northern Thai art. Tradition pictures it as big as a house, with a lion's head and body, an elephant's trunk and tusks, a rooster's comb and a bird's wings. In Thai it is also known as nok hatsading, nok hatsadi and nok hat.

long_description.id: Menurut tuturan lisan di timur laut Thailand, burung ini pernah mendiami hutan legendaris Himavanta. Buddhaghosa menyebutnya sebagai hewan berkekuatan lima gajah. Sebuah makalah akademik menyebut Hatsadiling muncul dalam Tipitaka dan banyak Atthakatha (komentar), termasuk karya sastra Buddhis Tom-nan Mun Sasana; burung ini dikatakan berasal dari Benua Uttarakuru dan, menurut teks Buddhis, membawa pergi orang karena mengira mereka mangsa, tanpa niat mencelakai.
long_description.en: An oral myth from northeastern Thailand places the bird in the legendary Himavanta forest, where it once lived. Buddhaghosa describes it as an animal with the strength of five elephants. An academic paper says Hatsadiling appears in the Tipitaka and many Atthakathas (Commentaries), including the Buddhist literature Tom-nan Mun Sasana; the bird is said to have originated on the Uttarakuru Continent and, according to Buddhist texts, carried people off because it thought they were prey, with no intention of harm.

long_description.id: Burung ini dianggap berperan penting dalam pendirian Hariphunchai, kerajaan Mon di Thailand masa kini, dan muncul dalam Cāmadevivaṃsa, kronik berbahasa Pali tentang pendirian kerajaan itu oleh Ratu Camadevi. Motifnya sering dipakai pada kereta jenazah biksu terkemuka dalam upacara kremasi di Thailand utara, dan juga oleh orang Marma. Makalah akademik itu menyebut konsep ini memengaruhi lukisan dan patung Istana Burung Hatsadiling di krematorium.
long_description.en: The bird is regarded as having helped bring about the founding of Hariphunchai, a Mon kingdom in what is now Thailand, and it appears in the Cāmadevivaṃsa, a Pali chronicle about Queen Camadevi founding that kingdom. Its motif is often used on funerary hearses of prominent Buddhist monks in cremation ceremonies in Northern Thailand, and also by the Marma people. The academic paper says these ideas influenced paintings and sculptures of the Hatsadiling Bird Castle at crematoriums.

cultural_context.id: Motif Hatsadiling dipakai pada kereta jenazah biksu terkemuka di Thailand utara dan oleh orang Marma sebagai motif utama kereta jenazah.
cultural_context.en: The Hatsadiling shape decorates the funeral hearses of eminent Buddhist monks in Northern Thailand, and the Marma people likewise take it as a main motif for such hearses.
